headline: Punjab to abolish hospital parchi system within four weeks
description: The Punjab government has assured the Lahore High Court (LHC) that it will abolish the existing parchi (registration slip) system in all government hospitals
author: APP
article_text:
The Punjab government has assured the Lahore High Court (LHC) that it will abolish the existing parchi (registration slip) system in all government hospitals across the province within four weeks to ensure timely medical treatment and eliminate long queues.

Special Secretary (Health) Nabila Irfan gave the undertaking before Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains during the hearing of a public interest petition filed by the Judicial Activism Panel on Friday.

She told the court that patients visiting public-sector hospitals, including those requiring emergency treatment and outpatient services, would no longer need to obtain registration slips from designated counters before receiving medical attention.

The court was also informed that the Punjab Health Department would introduce a modern, technology-based patient management system to streamline medical examinations and treatment and reduce unnecessary delays and overcrowding.

During the hearing, the court expressed serious concern over the authorities' failure to submit compliance reports despite repeated notices and directions issued since the petition was filed in 2020.

Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains observed that the continued failure to comply with court orders reflected a casual and indifferent attitude towards statutory and constitutional obligations.

The petition seeks enforcement of fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 4 and 9 of the Constitution and implementation of superior courts' judgments concerning the provision of essential healthcare facilities in public hospitals.

The Special Secretary sought further time to submit a comprehensive report on the availability, adequacy and standard of healthcare facilities in government hospitals across Punjab.

Accepting her undertaking, the court directed the authorities to implement the promised reforms within four weeks and submit a detailed compliance report supported by documentary evidence at the next hearing.

All respondents were also directed to submit comprehensive reports addressing the grievances raised in the petition and detailing measures taken to ensure essential healthcare facilities in public hospitals.

The court warned that any further unjustified failure to comply with its directions could result in proceedings against the responsible officials in accordance with the law.

The court adjourned further proceedings for six weeks.

headline: Ali Dar inaugurates new passage at Data Darbar
description: Advisor to the Chief Minister Punjab on Artificial Intelligence and Special Initiatives Ali Dar on Friday inaugurated a newly developed passage at the shrine
author: NNI
article_text:
Advisor to the Chief Minister Punjab on Artificial Intelligence and Special Initiatives Ali Dar on Friday inaugurated a newly developed passage at the shrine complex of Hazrat Ali Hajveri (RA), popularly known as Data Ganj Bakhsh, to improve accessibility and facilitate the movement of devotees.

During his visit, Ali Dar, who also chairs the Ravi Project Committee (RPC), reviewed ongoing construction and development work across the shrine complex.

Speaking on the occasion, he said providing better facilities to devotees visiting Data Darbar remained a priority of the Punjab government under the vision of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif.

He said the newly developed passage would improve visitor movement, strengthen crowd management and reduce difficulties faced by devotees, particularly during periods of heavy footfall.

Ali Dar said various development initiatives were being undertaken to accommodate the large number of visitors and provide them with a safer, more comfortable and accessible environment.

He emphasised that the preservation, restoration and development of historical and religious sites were among the government's priorities, stressing the need to maintain quality standards and complete ongoing projects on time.

He said serving devotees visiting the shrine of Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA), which holds immense spiritual and religious significance, was a matter of honour.

Ali Dar reaffirmed the government's commitment to improving facilities, accessibility and visitor arrangements at Data Darbar.

headline: PTI lawmakers back talks to end Governor's Rule in KP
description: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) provincial parliamentary party has supported negotiations with the federal government to resolve issues surrounding the
author: NNI
article_text:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) provincial parliamentary party has supported negotiations with the federal government to resolve issues surrounding the imposition of Governor's Rule and the emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

According to sources, a meeting of the PTI provincial parliamentary party was held in Peshawar, attended by former chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur and more than 40 lawmakers. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar and Noor-ul-Haq Qadri also participated.

Participants agreed that negotiations with the federal government should focus on ending Governor's Rule and the emergency, paving the way for the restoration of the party's mandate.

Some members proposed including Ali Amin Gandapur in the negotiating team, saying his participation could help resolve outstanding issues through mutual consultation.

The participants also appreciated the decision of party workers not to stage street protests following the imposition of Governor's Rule and the emergency, observing that demonstrations could have led to incidents similar to those of May 9.

PTI leader Shaukat Yousafzai expressed support for negotiations and urged the federal government to reduce political tensions and withdraw Governor's Rule and the emergency.

He said that if Ali Amin Gandapur was the parliamentary party's choice for the negotiations, there should be no objection, describing him as an old and loyal associate of Imran Khan.

Yousafzai further said that anyone making statements against state institutions had no connection with the PTI.

headline: SBP raises collateral-free SME loan limit to Rs50 million
description: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad has said that expanding financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) is among the government's key
author: Web Desk
article_text:
State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad has said that expanding financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) is among the government's key economic priorities, alongside agriculture, housing and export promotion.

Addressing the business community at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) on Friday, he said the limit for SME loans without collateral had been increased from Rs10 million to Rs50 million to improve businesses' access to financing.

He said the definition of SMEs had also been revised, raising the annual turnover limit for small enterprises from Rs150 million to Rs400 million and for medium enterprises from Rs800 million to Rs2 billion. Businesses with annual turnover of up to Rs2 billion can now benefit from SME financing facilities.

The SBP governor said the government was also taking measures to address challenges related to the cost of doing business, taxation and energy prices.

He said the government's housing finance scheme was revised in March 2026. Before the revision, banks' outstanding housing finance stood at Rs251 billion. Under the revised scheme, banks approved financing worth Rs521 billion for around 80,000 applicants within six to seven months.

Under the Prime Minister's Youth Business and Agriculture Scheme, young entrepreneurs were also being provided loans at markup rates ranging from zero to seven per cent.

Jameel Ahmad said the SBP, in collaboration with the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) and commercial banks, had simplified the SME loan application form into a single page.

He announced that the SME Connect Portal would become operational on November 1, 2026, allowing entrepreneurs to apply for loans online and track their applications from home.

Sharing financing figures, he said outstanding SME financing had increased from Rs491 billion in June 2024 to Rs691 billion in June 2025 and approximately Rs1,110 billion in June 2026.

The number of SME borrowers also increased from 177,000 in June 2024 to 275,000 in June 2025 and around 325,000 in June 2026.

Regarding export financing, the SBP governor said the limit under the Export Refinance Scheme had been increased from Rs1 trillion to Rs1.5 trillion, with Rs300 billion specifically allocated for SME exporters.

He added that the Cabinet had approved a 10-year long-term export financing scheme to support investment in export-oriented industries.

Speaking on the occasion, LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar proposed a joint financing mechanism involving industry, the government, EXIM Bank and commercial banks to accelerate SME growth.

He suggested selecting 1,000 SMEs based on available data, identifying their financing challenges and developing a facilitation model that could later be replicated across the country.

He also urged the SBP to link its complaint centre with the LCCI complaint centre to address banking-related issues faced by importers and exporters, including delays in opening letters of credit (LCs).

Ali Hussam Asghar said financing facilities should also be extended to local industries and businesses beyond the export sector. He proposed performance-based incentives for businesses that increased employment.

LCCI Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani highlighted the potential of Islamic banking in expanding SME financing, saying the sector's total financing had reached Rs6 trillion, with annual growth of 48.9 per cent.

He said Islamic banking accounted for 39.1 per cent of total banking financing, while its share in SME financing stood at only 15.9 per cent.

He proposed setting a minimum SME financing target of 5.9 per cent for Islamic banks, which could provide an additional Rs204 billion to the sector.

He added that the bad-debt ratio in Islamic banks' SME portfolio was 2.2 per cent, compared with 5.5 per cent across the overall banking sector.

LCCI Vice President Chaudhry Khadim Hussain thanked the SBP governor and his team for engaging with the business community and stressed that proposals discussed at such meetings should translate into practical measures to resolve business challenges.

State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad has said that expanding financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) is among the government's key economic priorities, alongside agriculture, housing and export promotion.

Addressing the business community at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) on Friday, he said the limit for SME loans without collateral had been increased from Rs10 million to Rs50 million to improve businesses' access to financing.

He said the definition of SMEs had also been revised, raising the annual turnover limit for small enterprises from Rs150 million to Rs400 million and for medium enterprises from Rs800 million to Rs2 billion. Businesses with annual turnover of up to Rs2 billion can now benefit from SME financing facilities.

Federal Constitutional Court upholds finality of judgments, rejects repeated challenges in land dispute

The SBP governor said the government was also taking measures to address challenges related to the cost of doing business, taxation and energy prices.

He said the government's housing finance scheme was revised in March 2026. Before the revision, banks' outstanding housing finance stood at Rs251 billion. Under the revised scheme, banks approved financing worth Rs521 billion for around 80,000 applicants within six to seven months.

Under the Prime Minister's Youth Business and Agriculture Scheme, young entrepreneurs were also being provided loans at markup rates ranging from zero to seven per cent.

DG ISPR says Pakistan-Saudi defence cooperation could expand, rules out wider military campaigns

Jameel Ahmad said the SBP, in collaboration with the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) and commercial banks, had simplified the SME loan application form into a single page.

He announced that the SME Connect Portal would become operational on November 1, 2026, allowing entrepreneurs to apply for loans online and track their applications from home.

Sharing financing figures, he said outstanding SME financing had increased from Rs491 billion in June 2024 to Rs691 billion in June 2025 and approximately Rs1,110 billion in June 2026.

The number of SME borrowers also increased from 177,000 in June 2024 to 275,000 in June 2025 and around 325,000 in June 2026.

Qatar offers Pakistani travellers free 30-day visa on arrival under four conditions

Regarding export financing, the SBP governor said the limit under the Export Refinance Scheme had been increased from Rs1 trillion to Rs1.5 trillion, with Rs300 billion specifically allocated for SME exporters.

He added that the Cabinet had approved a 10-year long-term export financing scheme to support investment in export-oriented industries.

Speaking on the occasion, LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar proposed a joint financing mechanism involving industry, the government, EXIM Bank and commercial banks to accelerate SME growth.

He suggested selecting 1,000 SMEs based on available data, identifying their financing challenges and developing a facilitation model that could later be replicated across the country.

He also urged the SBP to link its complaint centre with the LCCI complaint centre to address banking-related issues faced by importers and exporters, including delays in opening letters of credit (LCs).

Ali Hussam Asghar said financing facilities should also be extended to local industries and businesses beyond the export sector. He proposed performance-based incentives for businesses that increased employment.

LCCI Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani highlighted the potential of Islamic banking in expanding SME financing, saying the sector's total financing had reached Rs6 trillion, with annual growth of 48.9 per cent.

He said Islamic banking accounted for 39.1 per cent of total banking financing, while its share in SME financing stood at only 15.9 per cent.

He proposed setting a minimum SME financing target of 5.9 per cent for Islamic banks, which could provide an additional Rs204 billion to the sector.

He added that the bad-debt ratio in Islamic banks' SME portfolio was 2.2 per cent, compared with 5.5 per cent across the overall banking sector.

LCCI Vice President Chaudhry Khadim Hussain thanked the SBP governor and his team for engaging with the business community and stressed that proposals discussed at such meetings should translate into practical measures to resolve business challenges.

headline: Three flour mills sealed over smuggling

author: IHSAN UL HAQ
article_text:
RAHIM YAR KHAN - The district administration and the Food Department of Rahim Yar Khan have intensified their operations to crush the mafia involved in the unauthorised outflow of wheat. The authorities have successfully sealed three prominent flour mills and initiated criminal proceedings by lodging formal FIRs against operators involved in cross-border smuggling and the dangerous adulteration of staple flour with inferior rice flour. Over the preceding weeks, the region had become a hotspot for illicit activities, with intelligence indicating that strategic collusion between certain facilitators and mill owners was facilitating the systematic bleeding of local wheat reserves toward other provinces. Furthermore, consumer protection forums had raised red flags over compromised quality, exposing how certain commercial mills were diluting pure wheat flour with cheap corn and low-grade broken rice flour—a practice posing severe health hazards to unsuspecting consumers. In response to these compounding crises, the district administration and the Food Department deployed joint vigilance teams, overhauling the monitoring architecture of regional flour mills and transit routes. The intensified surveillance culminated in decisive raids on Wednesday and Thursday. Inspectors caught the violating mills red-handed while processing adulterated stocks and preparing illegal consignments for transportation. Immediate punitive measures saw the premises sealed, criminal cases filed under relevant legal frameworks, and law enforcement agencies bracing for subsequent arrests as investigations deepen. To fortify the supply chain against future breaches, authorities have significantly reinforced security at all inter-provincial entry and exit check-posts by deploying fresh administrative reserves.

DC orders crackdown on canal water theft in Bahawalpur

BAHAWALPUR (news wire): Deputy Commissioner Bahawalpur Syed Hasan Raza has directed the relevant departments to intensify efforts to prevent canal water theft, ensure fair water distribution among farmers, and take legal action against violators. He chaired a meeting to review measures to prevent canal water theft, take action against those responsible, and implement relevant laws. District Police Officer Rana Abdul Wahab, Additional Deputy Commissioner Municipal Services Dr. Ayesha Khan, Deputy Director Agriculture Hafiz Muhammad Shafiq and officers of the concerned departments attended the meeting. The participants reviewed incidents of canal water theft, the performance of relevant committees and measures being taken to ensure the equitable distribution of irrigation water. Deputy Commissioner Syed Hasan Raza directed assistant commissioners to conduct joint field visits with Irrigation Department and police officials and take coordinated action to prevent water theft. He stressed that Irrigation Department officials must remain active in the field and that committees established to curb canal water theft should be made fully functional. He also directed all relevant departments to ensure effective implementation of the measures adopted for this purpose. The deputy commissioner said the illegal diversion of canal water deprived other farmers of their rightful share and adversely affected their agricultural interests. He called for regular monitoring of the irrigation water distribution system and indiscriminate legal action against those found violating the rules. He further instructed the concerned officers to respond promptly to complaints of water theft and ensure action against the responsible persons in accordance with the law. On the occasion, District Police Officer Rana Abdul Wahab said legal action would be taken against those involved in canal water theft without discrimination. He directed the concerned officials to preserve photographs and videos of reported incidents as evidence, ensure effective monitoring of field operations and respond promptly to complaints so that those responsible could be brought to justice.

headline: Man dies, 12 injured in road accidents in Layyah, Muzaffargarh
description: LAYYAH / MUZAFFARGARH - A 40-year-old man was killed and another injured when a motorcycle hit a pedestrian on Ladhana Pir Jagi Road near Chak No. 168/TDA,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAYYAH / MUZAFFARGARH - A 40-year-old man was killed and another injured when a motorcycle hit a pedestrian on Ladhana Pir Jagi Road near Chak No. 168/TDA, rescuer said. The pedestrian Muhammad Afzal suffered a head injury and died on the spot, while bike rider Muhammad Umar, 22, sustained a cut on his head. Rescue personnel provided first aid to the injured man and shifted him to the District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital for further treatment. At least 12 people, including a woman, were injured in three separate road accidents in Muzaffargarh and one accident in Multan, rescuer said. According to Rescue 1122, an overspeeding Suzuki Alto car went out of control and collided head-on with an oncoming oil tanker near Chundar Mor on Shah Jamal Road in Muzaffargarh, leaving three people injured. The injured were identified as Talib Hussain, 45, Ghulam Mustafa, 45, and Muhammad Iqbal, 55. Rescue personnel provided them with first aid and shifted them to Rural Health Centre (RHC), Shah Jamal, for further treatment. Both vehicles were later handed over to the local police for legal proceedings. No loss of life was reported in the accident. In another incident in Basti Thar on Jhugi Wala Road in Jatoi tehsil, a motorcycle collided with a harvester machine, injuring 25-year-old Fazila Bibi, wife of Muhammad Naseem. She sustained injuries to her forehead and left arm. Rescue personnel provided her with first aid and shifted her to Tehsil Headquarters (THQ) Hospital, Jatoi, for further treatment. Meanwhile, in Multan, five passengers were seriously injured when a speeding loader rickshaw hit a Qingqi rickshaw from the side near Greenland Marriage Hall, close to Coca-Cola factory. Rescuers rushed to the scene after receiving information about the accident, provided first aid to the injured and shifted all five to Nishtar Hospital for further treatment.

headline: Violent crime falls at historic rate in Bahawalpur
description: BAHAWALNGAR - The crime rate has been declining across Bahawalnagar due to an effective strategy being implemented by police as the region has witnessed 30 per
author: Ali Raza
article_text: BAHAWALNGAR - The crime rate has been declining across Bahawalnagar due to an effective strategy being implemented by police as the region has witnessed 30 per cent reduction in overall crime rate. According to the police sources, the police in Bahawalnagar and across the region are striving to implement the vision of the Chief Minister of Punjab, Safe Punjab, through effective patrolling, monitoring of Safe City cameras and timely registration. Under the supervision of RPO Bahawalpur Ghazi Muhammad Salahuddin, there has been a clear reduction in crime. From January 1, 2026 to October 28, 2026, a total of 16,399 crime calls were received in the region, while the number was 23,630 during the same period last year. Thus, a decrease of about 30% was recorded in overall crime calls. Calls for robbery decreased by 70%, from 270 to 82, and calls for car theft decreased by about 60% from 62 to 25. Similarly, calls related to theft incidents decreased by 20 percent, from 16,483 to 13,119, while calls related to motorcycle theft also decreased significantly, from 4,069 to 1,785, recording a decrease of about 56℅. And calls related to snatching of vehicles and motorcycles decreased by 49 percent from 2,746 to 1,388.Similarly, there was a 16 percent decrease in calls related to murder and attempted murder incidents, from 1,276 to 1,068. These figures reflect a significant decrease in calls received related to various types of crimes in the Bahawalpur Region. The Bahawalpur Regional Police is committed to continuing effective policing and professional measures to protect the lives and property of citizens, prevent crimes and maintain law and order.

headline: Natasha Daultana calls for strengthening Pakistan, Germany relations
description: VEHARI - Pakistan Peoples Party South Punjab General Secretary and Member of the National Assembly Natasha Daultana has said that there are vast opportunities
author: Sh Fazal Ur Rehman
article_text: VEHARI - Pakistan Peoples Party South Punjab General Secretary and Member of the National Assembly Natasha Daultana has said that there are vast opportunities to further strengthen the longstanding friendly relations between Pakistan and Germany. She said enhanced cooperation in education, women’s empowerment, entrepreneurship and skills development could benefit the people of both countries. She expressed these views in connection with a meeting between the Pakistan-Germany Parliamentary Friendship Group, led by its Convener and Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah, and German Ambassador Ina Lepel at Parliament House, Islamabad. The meeting discussed ways to strengthen parliamentary ties, bilateral relations, trade, investment and people-to-people contacts between the two countries. Members of the National Assembly Mohammad Ilyas Choudhary, Mohammad Riaz Fatyana and Dr Shahida Rehmani also attended the meeting. Natasha Daultana expressed hope that expanding the partnership between Pakistan and Germany would open new avenues for mutual cooperation, shared benefits and development in various sectors.

headline: Three-year-old girl allegedly sexually assaulted, suspect arrested
description: MUZAFFARGARH - A three-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted in Chowk Sarwar Shaheed, Muzaffargarh district, and is in critical condition, prompting
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text: MUZAFFARGARH - A three-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted in Chowk Sarwar Shaheed, Muzaffargarh district, and is in critical condition, prompting Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to take immediate notice of the incident. The child, who was reportedly playing outside her home, was allegedly taken away and assaulted. She was subsequently shifted to Nishtar Hospital in Multan in critical condition, where she is receiving medical treatment. CCTV footage that emerged after the incident reportedly shows the suspect taking the child away. Police used the footage to trace and arrest the alleged perpetrator within two hours of the incident. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz took immediate notice of the case and directed the authorities to take prompt action. The incident has sparked widespread concern in the area, with residents expressing alarm over the safety of children. headline: Stent shortage hits Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology Hospital
description: FAISALABAD - A severe shortage of cardiac stents at the Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology Hospital (FIC) over the past several days has left a large number of
author: Mian Muhammad Zeeshan
article_text: FAISALABAD - A severe shortage of cardiac stents at the Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology Hospital (FIC) over the past several days has left a large number of heart patients facing difficulties in accessing treatment. According to sources, the FIC hospital has been experiencing a serious shortage of stents used in angioplasty for approximately the past 10 days. The new stock required by the hospital is expected to arrive in another two to three weeks. Under the current circumstances, stents are being provided only to patients brought to the hospital in critical condition due to heart attacks. Meanwhile patients visiting the OPD including those who have been waiting for months for their scheduled angioplasty procedures, are being deprived of the required treatment. A large number of patients travel to the hospital from Faisalabad, Toba Tek Singh, Gojra, Jhang, Chiniot, Bhowana, Jaranwala and other surrounding areas, spending thousands of rupees on transportation. However due to the unavailability of stents for their procedures, many are reportedly forced to return home disappointed without receiving treatment. The situation has raised serious concerns about the procurement, supply and inventory management of cardiac stents. Alleged shortcomings in planning and negligence on the part of those responsible have further aggravated the difficulties faced by heart patients. However, no action against those responsible has so far been reported by the Punjab government or the district administration in connection with this sensitive matter. Deputy Commissioner Faisalabad Nauman Siddique said he would review all the facts surrounding the issue. Meanwhile, Executive Director of FIC, Professor Dr Hamid Saeed said that stocks had been arranged from the cardiology hospitals in Dera Ghazi Khan and Wazirabad to address the shortage. He added that angioplasty procedures were continuing at the hospital around the clock. Citizens said they visit FIC in the hope of receiving free treatment in line with the vision of the CM Punjab. However, they complained that the hospital was facing a serious shortage of facilities.They added that amid rising inflation, many patients could not afford private treatment for heart disease.The citizens have appealed to CM Maryam Nawaz to take immediate notice of the situation, ensure an uninterrupted supply of cardiac stents and initiate action against those found responsible for any negligence.

headline: Families of police martyrs get residential plots documents in Sargodha
description: SARGODHA - Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Akhtar Sukhera paid rich tributes to the police martyred and assured full support to their families.
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: SARGODHA - Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Akhtar Sukhera paid rich tributes to the police martyred and assured full support to their families. “Police martyrs are our pride and it is our responsibility to take care of their families, RPO Sohail Akhtar Sukhera said while addressing a ceremony to distribute ownership letters of residential plots among heirs of 8 police martyrs here. He said that the police department is making special efforts to support heirs of the police martyrs. Service and welfare of the families of martyrs is our priority, he said. RPO Sohail Akhtar Sukhera also said that the immortal sacrifices of police martyrs will always be remembered. On this occasion, families of martyrs were given allotment letters of residential plots in modern housing society located on Sargodha-Lahore Road. Sargodha Commissioner Hafiz Shaukat Ali and DPO Khushab Tauqeer Muhammad Naeem also attended the ceremony besides others. The practical patronage of the heirs of the martyrs is a commendable effort of Sargodha Region Police, Commissioner Hafiz Shaukat Ali said. The papers for residential plots were distributed among the heirs of 8 martyrs, including martyred driver Constable Mazhar Hussain, Shaheed Constable Saifullah, Muhammad Riaz, Muhammad Waris, Muhammad Jameel, Muhammad Sarfaraz, Abid Hussain and Sajid Hussain. Sargodha Region Police reiterates commitment to provide practical support and welfare to the families of martyrs.

headline: Pakistan, Singapore vow to deepen ties in AI, education, trade
description: Islamabad - Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with Singapore, both bilaterally and
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Islamabad - Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with Singapore, both bilaterally and multilaterally including within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

He was talking to Foreign Minister of Singapore Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, who called on him in Islamabad. The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its longstanding and friendly relations with Singapore, particularly as the two countries are commemorating the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year.

The PM expressed admiration for Singapore’s remarkable economic transformation and achievements in innovation and development. The two sides discussed ways to enhance bilateral trade and investment and expand cooperation in priority areas, including the digital economy, fintech, infrastructure development, logistics, SMEs and services sector.

They also discussed exploring new avenues for mutually beneficial economic cooperation and enhancing people-to-people contacts. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral fora.

Also, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Singapore Dr Vivian Balakrishnan called on Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in Rawalpindi.

During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and global security dynamics and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation were discussed. Both sides exchanged views on regional peace and stability and underscored the importance of sustained engagement and cooperation in areas of shared interest. The Field Marshal underscored Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its relations with Singapore, emphasizing the importance of enhanced institutional linkages and constructive engagement for promoting regional peace, stability and security.

The visiting dignitary reciprocated strengthening of bilateral ties, appreciated the professionalism of Pakistan Armed Forces and acknowledged Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability.

Meanwhile, Pakistan and Singapore have reaffirmed their commitment to further deepening their cooperation in diverse fields including trade, investment, disaster management, and people to people contacts. The commitment was expressed during a joint press stakeout of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar and visiting Foreign Minister of Singapore Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan in Islamabad.

In his opening remarks, the Deputy Prime Minister said Pakistan and Singapore enjoy long standing and friendly relations focused on mutual respect and goodwill. He said Pakistan was among the first countries to recognize Singapore following its independence in 1965.

The Deputy Prime Minister said the visit of Foreign Minister Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan reflects shared commitment to strengthen friendship and broaden cooperation between Pakistan and Singapore.

He said Pakistan and Singapore during today’s talks agreed to hold regular bilateral political consultation and promote high level exchanges to strengthen cooperation between our governments and institutions.

He said economic cooperation was also central to our discussions and both sides welcomed the significant growth in bilateral trade and discussed ways to build on this progress.

Ishaq Dar said Pakistan and Singapore agreed to encourage closer engagement between business communities through exchange of business delegations and stronger links between Chambers of Commerce and in order to facilitate stronger business to business ties.

He said the reopening of Pakistan Trade Investment Office at our High Commission in Singapore, is a testament of Pakistan resolve to promote stronger B2B ties with great friendly country, Singapore.

Ishaq Dar said the two sides also discussed the scope for closer cooperation in education, research and innovation, including digital technologies and artificial intelligence

He said both the sides agreed to deepen cooperation in human resource development, agriculture and climate domains and to encourage greater cultural, academic, youth and people to people exchanges.

The Deputy Prime Minister said we look forward to working closely with Singapore in support of its priorities as Chair and to further strengthen Pakistan ASEAN cooperation.

On regional and international issues, Ishaq Dar said both sides reaffirmed the central role of dialogue and diplomacy, respect for international law and adherence to the principles of the UN Charter in addressing regional and global challenges.

The Deputy Prime Minister said he also shared Pakistan’s perspective on Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir dispute.

He reiterated Pakistan’s firm support for an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous state of Palestine based on pre June 1967 borders with Al Quds Al Sharif as his capital, which is the stated policy of Islamic Republic of Pakistan in context of South Asia.

The Deputy Prime Minister also stressed on the importance of a just, durable and peaceful settlement of the long standing Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

In his remarks, the Foreign Minister of Singapore emphasised to strengthen bilateral cooperation in business, trade, investment, disaster management, culture, and people to people exchanges, science and technology.

He particularly commended the historic and tremendous mediatory role played by Pakistan in defusing tension and facilitating dialogue to resolve the crisis in the Middle East and Gulf.

On the occasion, the two sides exchanged documents regarding Memorandum of Understanding on cooperation in Disaster Management between National Disaster Management Authority of Pakistan and Singapore Civil Defence Force.

Islamabad - Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with Singapore, both bilaterally and multilaterally including within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

He was talking to Foreign Minister of Singapore Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, who called on him in Islamabad. The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its longstanding and friendly relations with Singapore, particularly as the two countries are commemorating the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year.

The PM expressed admiration for Singapore’s remarkable economic transformation and achievements in innovation and development. The two sides discussed ways to enhance bilateral trade and investment and expand cooperation in priority areas, including the digital economy, fintech, infrastructure development, logistics, SMEs and services sector.

They also discussed exploring new avenues for mutually beneficial economic cooperation and enhancing people-to-people contacts. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral fora.

Also, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Singapore Dr Vivian Balakrishnan called on Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in Rawalpindi.

During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and global security dynamics and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation were discussed. Both sides exchanged views on regional peace and stability and underscored the importance of sustained engagement and cooperation in areas of shared interest. The Field Marshal underscored Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its relations with Singapore, emphasizing the importance of enhanced institutional linkages and constructive engagement for promoting regional peace, stability and security.

The visiting dignitary reciprocated strengthening of bilateral ties, appreciated the professionalism of Pakistan Armed Forces and acknowledged Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability.

Meanwhile, Pakistan and Singapore have reaffirmed their commitment to further deepening their cooperation in diverse fields including trade, investment, disaster management, and people to people contacts. The commitment was expressed during a joint press stakeout of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar and visiting Foreign Minister of Singapore Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan in Islamabad.

In his opening remarks, the Deputy Prime Minister said Pakistan and Singapore enjoy long standing and friendly relations focused on mutual respect and goodwill. He said Pakistan was among the first countries to recognize Singapore following its independence in 1965.

The Deputy Prime Minister said the visit of Foreign Minister Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan reflects shared commitment to strengthen friendship and broaden cooperation between Pakistan and Singapore.

He said Pakistan and Singapore during today’s talks agreed to hold regular bilateral political consultation and promote high level exchanges to strengthen cooperation between our governments and institutions.

He said economic cooperation was also central to our discussions and both sides welcomed the significant growth in bilateral trade and discussed ways to build on this progress.

Ishaq Dar said Pakistan and Singapore agreed to encourage closer engagement between business communities through exchange of business delegations and stronger links between Chambers of Commerce and in order to facilitate stronger business to business ties.

He said the reopening of Pakistan Trade Investment Office at our High Commission in Singapore, is a testament of Pakistan resolve to promote stronger B2B ties with great friendly country, Singapore.

Ishaq Dar said the two sides also discussed the scope for closer cooperation in education, research and innovation, including digital technologies and artificial intelligence

He said both the sides agreed to deepen cooperation in human resource development, agriculture and climate domains and to encourage greater cultural, academic, youth and people to people exchanges.

The Deputy Prime Minister said we look forward to working closely with Singapore in support of its priorities as Chair and to further strengthen Pakistan ASEAN cooperation.

On regional and international issues, Ishaq Dar said both sides reaffirmed the central role of dialogue and diplomacy, respect for international law and adherence to the principles of the UN Charter in addressing regional and global challenges.

The Deputy Prime Minister said he also shared Pakistan’s perspective on Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir dispute.

He reiterated Pakistan’s firm support for an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous state of Palestine based on pre June 1967 borders with Al Quds Al Sharif as his capital, which is the stated policy of Islamic Republic of Pakistan in context of South Asia.

The Deputy Prime Minister also stressed on the importance of a just, durable and peaceful settlement of the long standing Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

In his remarks, the Foreign Minister of Singapore emphasised to strengthen bilateral cooperation in business, trade, investment, disaster management, culture, and people to people exchanges, science and technology.

He particularly commended the historic and tremendous mediatory role played by Pakistan in defusing tension and facilitating dialogue to resolve the crisis in the Middle East and Gulf.

On the occasion, the two sides exchanged documents regarding Memorandum of Understanding on cooperation in Disaster Management between National Disaster Management Authority of Pakistan and Singapore Civil Defence Force.

headline: Trump claims Iran war will ‘get wrapped up soon’

author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump while speaking ahead of the November 3 midterm congressional elections, said on Friday that he believes the war with Iran will end soon, but does not say how that will happen.

“It’s going to get wrapped up soon,” Trump said in an interview with Kansas City radio station KCMO. “We need a guarantee there’ll never be a nuclear weapon.” Trump has said the US would not strike Iran before the elections.

He has also promised several times in recent weeks that the US and Israel will soon “finish the job” in Iran, without specifying whether he intends to push for diplomatic or military measures.

Qatari mediators have returned to Tehran as part of efforts to reach a deal between the US and Iran, an official briefed on the talks tells Reuters. The mediation talks have been coordinated with the US, the officials said on Friday.

US intelligence believes working with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council head Mohsen Rezaei is Washington’s best option if it wants to head off renewed fighting, according to The Washington Post, after the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Vance had contacted the hardline official.

In his letter to Rezaei, Vance reportedly stressed the need for the US and Iran to return to negotiations focused on their respective national interests — Washington’s being preventing a nuclear-armed Iran and Tehran’s being its economy and sovereignty — an official familiar with the matter tells the Post.

The official tells the Post that Vance stressed the need for Iran to dispatch negotiators who are “empowered” to discuss and resolve the nuclear issue, indicating that the White House believes Rezaei has that ability.

According to the Post, US intelligence believes Rezaei is a key player in the Iranian regime, as he is in contact with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and has his finger on the pulse of the country’s security and economic situation. He is believed to have been in contact with Khamenei after receiving Vance’s letter, the report says.

It cites US officials as saying they believe Rezaei “understands the dire situation.”

Rezaei has yet to respond to Vance’s letter, however, and the Post notes that his hardline stance against the US over the years casts doubt on his willingness to pursue a deal with Washington.

“It’s going to get wrapped up soon,” Trump said in an interview with Kansas City radio station KCMO. “We need a guarantee there’ll never be a nuclear weapon.” Trump has said the US would not strike Iran before the elections.
He has also promised several times in recent weeks that the US and Israel will soon “finish the job” in Iran, without specifying whether he intends to push for diplomatic or military measures.

Qatari mediators have returned to Tehran as part of efforts to reach a deal between the US and Iran, an official briefed on the talks tells Reuters. The mediation talks have been coordinated with the US, the officials said on Friday.

US intelligence believes working with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council head Mohsen Rezaei is Washington’s best option if it wants to head off renewed fighting, according to The Washington Post, after the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Vance had contacted the hardline official.

In his letter to Rezaei, Vance reportedly stressed the need for the US and Iran to return to negotiations focused on their respective national interests — Washington’s being preventing a nuclear-armed Iran and Tehran’s being its economy and sovereignty — an official familiar with the matter tells the Post.

The official tells the Post that Vance stressed the need for Iran to dispatch negotiators who are “empowered” to discuss and resolve the nuclear issue, indicating that the White House believes Rezaei has that ability.

According to the Post, US intelligence believes Rezaei is a key player in the Iranian regime, as he is in contact with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and has his finger on the pulse of the country’s security and economic situation. He is believed to have been in contact with Khamenei after receiving Vance’s letter, the report says.
It cites US officials as saying they believe Rezaei “understands the dire situation.”
Rezaei has yet to respond to Vance’s letter, however, and the Post notes that his hardline stance against the US over the years casts doubt on his willingness to pursue a deal with Washington.

headline: Punjab CM launches historic Rs1.99 trillion Pivot economic plan
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Friday launched the Punjab Innovation, Value Addition and Economic Transformation (PIVOT) Plan
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Friday launched the Punjab Innovation, Value Addition and Economic Transformation (PIVOT) Plan 2026–29, a comprehensive Rs1,995.3 billion economic strategy aimed at positioning Punjab as an export-led industrial hub. The roadmap targets $6.8 billion in incremental exports, 162,000 new direct jobs and support for over one million livelihoods.

Speaking at the launch, Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said, “Punjab is ready to move towards a new model of economic growth—one driven by industry, innovation, value addition and exports. Our objective is to create an environment where businesses can invest with confidence, industries can expand and our people can access better employment and livelihood opportunities.”

The unveiling brought together an unprecedented gathering of leading corporate figures, economic policymakers, international development agencies and diplomats invited by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Prominent business icons including Mian Mansha, Arif Habib, Fawad Mukhtar, Ziad Bashir and Osman Khalid Waheed attended the launch, signalling private-sector engagement with the initiative.

Financial sector leadership was represented by State Bank of Pakistan Governor Jameel Ahmad, alongside heads and senior executives of major commercial banks and financial institutions. International participation included foreign ambassadors, members of the diplomatic corps and representatives of key international development partners, including the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and United Nations organisations.

Senior government figures, led by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb and Chief Secretary Zahid Akhtar Zaman, provincial cabinet ministers, administrative secretaries and district focal officers, were also present to outline the government’s operational commitments.

Addressing the business community, the CM said, “My message to investors and industrialists across Pakistan and around the world is clear: Punjab welcomes your investment. We want to work with you, facilitate your businesses and create the conditions in which enterprise can grow. Government will facilitate, industry will lead.”

A primary pillar of the PIVOT framework is the Strategic Trade Enhancement Programme (STEP), supported by a newly introduced digital portal. Under this mechanism, the government envisages Rs300 billion in concessional financing at rates ranging between zero and five per cent for eligible commercial categories, giving businesses access to lower-cost capital for expansion, subject to programme terms and conditions.

This financing structure forms part of an overall investment framework combining Rs1,089 billion in public investment with a target of Rs906 billion in private-sector investment.

“We are not looking at economic growth as a government-only responsibility. Sustainable growth requires private investment, a strong industrial base and a partnership in which the public sector enables the private sector to innovate, produce and compete. PIVOT is designed to turn that partnership into measurable economic progress, the CM stated.

The plan directs Rs753.7 billion towards strengthening industrial output, encouraging value addition and building long-term export competitiveness.

To address operational costs and energy challenges, the government has earmarked Rs50 billion for solar power installations and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). An additional Rs50 billion has been allocated for machinery duty reimbursements to incentivise manufacturers to upgrade factories, adopt advanced technology and meet international quality standards.

The programme focuses on key manufacturing value chains, including garments and textiles, sports goods, leather and footwear, surgical instruments, pharmaceuticals, fans, cutlery, steel and ceramics. Modern testing laboratories, certification facilities and plug-and-play industrial infrastructure are also envisaged to help businesses meet international compliance requirements and access export markets.

The CM also said, “Our industries must not be limited to producing more; they must produce better, add greater value and compete in international markets. We want Punjab’s manufacturers to have access to modern technology, reliable energy solutions, quality infrastructure and the financing they need to expand their businesses and exports.”

To move agriculture beyond raw commodity production towards higher-value processing, PIVOT includes four specialised agro-processing parks in Sargodha, Khanewal, Okara and Bhakkar.

These facilities are designed to reduce post-harvest losses, modernise food-processing infrastructure and integrate agricultural producers into higher-value supply chains.

Agricultural value-chain interventions include wheat value enhancement and improved quality and market access for citrus, potato and mango crops, alongside targeted export financing for horticulture and floriculture. The programme also envisages dedicated Horticulture Authorities in 20 districts.

The initiative further supports commercial expansion across livestock, dairy, aquaculture, halal meat and milk value chains, with the objective of improving productivity and developing export opportunities.

Beyond industrial and agricultural manufacturing, the plan extends to tourism, digital services and workforce development.

Tourism infrastructure will be upgraded to develop destination-economy opportunities, improve facilities for visitors and encourage private-sector investment in hospitality and related services.

To address the gap between vocational education and workplace requirements, the programme envisages training 402,060 individuals over three years. The focus will be on industry-aligned, demand-driven skills required by modern manufacturing, emerging commercial sectors and technology-oriented enterprises. “Our young people must be prepared for the jobs of tomorrow. Skills development must respond to the actual needs of industry and the changing demands of the economy. We want training to lead to employment, entrepreneurship and better livelihoods,” the CM said.

To improve the business environment, PIVOT introduces regulatory and administrative reforms aimed at simplifying commercial operations and attracting long-term investment.

Through the E-Biz digital initiative, the provincial government aims to digitise 300 public administrative services to make business processes more accessible and transparent. The programme also envisages bringing 2,000 firms onto e-commerce platforms, alongside modernised labour laws, public-private partnership reforms and approved schemes for state land leases across nine productive economic sectors.

The Chief Minister said that investors should spend their time building businesses, creating jobs and expanding production—not navigating unnecessary administrative hurdles. “We are working to make government services simpler, more accessible and more transparent.”

Execution and accountability are embedded through a central governance model led by a PIVOT Board chaired by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb on behalf of the Chief Minister.

Operational coordination will be handled by a dedicated PIVOT Secretariat in the Planning and Development Department, alongside a PIVOT cell within the Chief Secretary’s Office. Deputy Commissioners will serve as district-level focal persons.

Implementation will be monitored through a central PIVOT Dashboard and an Industry Scorecard, with defined milestones, measurable performance indicators and regular reviews to track progress, identify bottlenecks and strengthen departmental accountability.

Chief Secretary Zahid Akhtar Zaman outlined the implementation arrangements and confirmed that the concept would be operationalised within six months.

The Chief Minister said, “PIVOT will not remain a document of targets and commitments. Its implementation will be tracked, its progress measured and its results assessed. Every initiative must translate into real investment, stronger businesses, more exports and better opportunities for the people of Punjab.”

Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb emphasised that the Chief Minister’s vision for PIVOT was to position government as an enabler and facilitator of enterprise, allowing the private sector to drive economic expansion.

“Our ambition is to build a Punjab where businesses can grow, industries can compete globally, our farmers can earn more from their produce and our young people can find meaningful opportunities. We are opening the doors to investment and partnership. Together, we can turn Punjab’s economic potential into prosperity,” the CM concluded.

Addressing the business community, the CM said, “My message to investors and industrialists across Pakistan and around the world is clear: Punjab welcomes your investment. We want to work with you, facilitate your businesses and create the conditions in which enterprise can grow. Government will facilitate, industry will lead.”

A primary pillar of the PIVOT framework is the Strategic Trade Enhancement Programme (STEP), supported by a newly introduced digital portal. Under this mechanism, the government envisages Rs300 billion in concessional financing at rates ranging between zero and five per cent for eligible commercial categories, giving businesses access to lower-cost capital for expansion, subject to programme terms and conditions.

This financing structure forms part of an overall investment framework combining Rs1,089 billion in public investment with a target of Rs906 billion in private-sector investment.

“We are not looking at economic growth as a government-only responsibility. Sustainable growth requires private investment, a strong industrial base and a partnership in which the public sector enables the private sector to innovate, produce and compete. PIVOT is designed to turn that partnership into measurable economic progress, the CM stated.

The plan directs Rs753.7 billion towards strengthening industrial output, encouraging value addition and building long-term export competitiveness.

To address operational costs and energy challenges, the government has earmarked Rs50 billion for solar power installations and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). An additional Rs50 billion has been allocated for machinery duty reimbursements to incentivise manufacturers to upgrade factories, adopt advanced technology and meet international quality standards.

The programme focuses on key manufacturing value chains, including garments and textiles, sports goods, leather and footwear, surgical instruments, pharmaceuticals, fans, cutlery, steel and ceramics. Modern testing laboratories, certification facilities and plug-and-play industrial infrastructure are also envisaged to help businesses meet international compliance requirements and access export markets.

The CM also said, “Our industries must not be limited to producing more; they must produce better, add greater value and compete in international markets. We want Punjab’s manufacturers to have access to modern technology, reliable energy solutions, quality infrastructure and the financing they need to expand their businesses and exports.”

To move agriculture beyond raw commodity production towards higher-value processing, PIVOT includes four specialised agro-processing parks in Sargodha, Khanewal, Okara and Bhakkar.

These facilities are designed to reduce post-harvest losses, modernise food-processing infrastructure and integrate agricultural producers into higher-value supply chains.

Agricultural value-chain interventions include wheat value enhancement and improved quality and market access for citrus, potato and mango crops, alongside targeted export financing for horticulture and floriculture. The programme also envisages dedicated Horticulture Authorities in 20 districts.

The initiative further supports commercial expansion across livestock, dairy, aquaculture, halal meat and milk value chains, with the objective of improving productivity and developing export opportunities.

Beyond industrial and agricultural manufacturing, the plan extends to tourism, digital services and workforce development.

Tourism infrastructure will be upgraded to develop destination-economy opportunities, improve facilities for visitors and encourage private-sector investment in hospitality and related services.

To address the gap between vocational education and workplace requirements, the programme envisages training 402,060 individuals over three years. The focus will be on industry-aligned, demand-driven skills required by modern manufacturing, emerging commercial sectors and technology-oriented enterprises. “Our young people must be prepared for the jobs of tomorrow. Skills development must respond to the actual needs of industry and the changing demands of the economy. We want training to lead to employment, entrepreneurship and better livelihoods,” the CM said.

To improve the business environment, PIVOT introduces regulatory and administrative reforms aimed at simplifying commercial operations and attracting long-term investment.

Through the E-Biz digital initiative, the provincial government aims to digitise 300 public administrative services to make business processes more accessible and transparent. The programme also envisages bringing 2,000 firms onto e-commerce platforms, alongside modernised labour laws, public-private partnership reforms and approved schemes for state land leases across nine productive economic sectors.

The Chief Minister said that investors should spend their time building businesses, creating jobs and expanding production—not navigating unnecessary administrative hurdles. “We are working to make government services simpler, more accessible and more transparent.”

Execution and accountability are embedded through a central governance model led by a PIVOT Board chaired by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb on behalf of the Chief Minister.

Operational coordination will be handled by a dedicated PIVOT Secretariat in the Planning and Development Department, alongside a PIVOT cell within the Chief Secretary’s Office. Deputy Commissioners will serve as district-level focal persons.

Implementation will be monitored through a central PIVOT Dashboard and an Industry Scorecard, with defined milestones, measurable performance indicators and regular reviews to track progress, identify bottlenecks and strengthen departmental accountability.

Chief Secretary Zahid Akhtar Zaman outlined the implementation arrangements and confirmed that the concept would be operationalised within six months.

The Chief Minister said, “PIVOT will not remain a document of targets and commitments. Its implementation will be tracked, its progress measured and its results assessed. Every initiative must translate into real investment, stronger businesses, more exports and better opportunities for the people of Punjab.”

Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb emphasised that the Chief Minister’s vision for PIVOT was to position government as an enabler and facilitator of enterprise, allowing the private sector to drive economic expansion.

“Our ambition is to build a Punjab where businesses can grow, industries can compete globally, our farmers can earn more from their produce and our young people can find meaningful opportunities. We are opening the doors to investment and partnership. Together, we can turn Punjab’s economic potential into prosperity,” the CM concluded.

headline: Pak Army destroys Afghan posts in retaliation for Angoor Adda shelling
description: Islamabad - Pakistan Army targeted and destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and military positions in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Islamabad - Pakistan Army targeted and destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and military positions in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar, state media reported on Friday.

Pakistan Army gave a befitting reply to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban along the Pak-Afghan border in the Angoor Adda area on Tuesday last, Radio Pakistan reported.

According to the security sources, Pakistan Army successfully targeted and destroyed several posts and military positions of the Afghan Taliban in the areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar. Using heavy weaponry, Pakistan Army forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their posts and flee.

Reports indicate that several Afghan Taliban regime personnel were also killed during the precise and effective operation by the Pakistan Army.

Security forces remain committed to the defense of the country and the protection of its people and there will be no compromise on national security.

The security forces on Wednesday had destroyed multiple Afghan Taliban checkposts in a retaliatory operation after an attack on civilians in South Waziristan’s Angoor Adda area resulted in the death of one person and injured five members of the same family, the security sources had said.

Lower South Waziristan Deputy Commissioner had said Afghan Taliban forces opened unprovoked fire on the Angoor Adda bazaar and nearby residential areas.

A mortar shell struck the area, martyring one civilian and injuring five others, while several shops were damaged. The deputy commissioner had said Pakistani forces deployed along the border were carrying out an effective and forceful response to the attack.

Security sources had said the Pakistan Army swiftly retaliated, destroying several Afghan Taliban checkposts across the border.

The incident came amid recurring cross-border violence in the Angoor Adda sector.

In late April, mortar shelling from across the border injured civilians and damaged homes in South Waziristan, prompting Pakistani forces to target Afghan Taliban positions, according to security sources and local authorities.

The clashes followed renewed hostilities in February, when Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil-Haq.

Islamabad has repeatedly called on Kabul to prevent militant groups from using Afghan territory to launch attacks in Pakistan.

headline: Saudi-led coalition destroys ballistic missile fired by Houthis over Makkah region
description: RIYADH - The Saudi Air defence forces intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Eastern Province, said
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
RIYADH - The Saudi Air defence forces intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Eastern Province, said Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen.

The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen’s Houthis in the Makkah region, the coalition said in a statement.

The reported incident is the latest in a series of cross-border attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis on Saudi Arabia, involving drones and missiles targeting military installations, airports and energy infrastructure.

The group has repeatedly denied targeting Makkah and Medina, Islam’s two holiest cities, rejecting previous Saudi-led coalition accusations that it had launched drones towards the cities.

Yemen’s Houthis denied launching any attack towards Saudi Arabia this morning, after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the group over the Makkah region.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree dismissed the coalition’s account as false in a post on X, saying the group had not carried out any operation towards Saudi territory. He says its operations target Saudi oil facilities and military bases.

The Iran-backed Houthis have launched a series of cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia targeting military installations, airports and energy infrastructure. The group has repeatedly denied targeting Makkah and Madinah, Islam’s two holiest cities, rejecting previous Saudi-led coalition accusations that it had launched drones towards the cities.

headline: Tahir Ashrafi welcomes Punjab law facilitating registration of seminaries
description: CHINIOT - Chairman Pakistan Ulema Council and Prime Minister’s Coordinator Allama Hafiz Muhammad Tahir Mahmood Ashrafi has welcomed the Punjab
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
CHINIOT - Chairman Pakistan Ulema Council and Prime Minister’s Coordinator Allama Hafiz Muhammad Tahir Mahmood Ashrafi has welcomed the Punjab government’s approval of legislation concerning religious seminaries, saying it would pave the way for their registration across the province. Addressing the annual All Pakistan Khatm-e-Nabuwwat Conference in Chiniot and Chenabnagar on Friday, followed by a media talk, he said resolving administrative and legal issues faced by seminaries, protecting mosques and religious institutions, and facilitating their administration were among the key priorities. He said efforts would be made to accelerate the registration of seminaries in Punjab and address their longstanding issues, including facilitating the opening of bank accounts, as had been done in other provinces.

Ashrafi thanked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, government officials, religious leaders and seminaries’ representatives for their role in resolving the matter.

He said issues concerning religious institutions in Balochistan and other parts of the country would also be addressed through consultation and government cooperation.

headline: PFA imposes Rs108,000 fines on five food outlets
description: GUJRAT - The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) conducted 53 inspections across the district to ensure food quality and compliance with food safety regulations,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: GUJRAT - The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) conducted 53 inspections across the district to ensure food quality and compliance with food safety regulations, imposed a total of Rs108,000 fine on five outlets over violations. According to an official source, the authority also issued 18 improvement notices during the inspections. During the crackdown, officials discarded 6-kg pickle, 3-kg expired and prohibited food items, 3-kg insect-infested sugar syrup and 1-kg China salt. The PFA is continuing its enforcement campaign to ensure the availability of safe and quality food to citizens and take action against those violating food safety regulations.

headline: Three illegal LPG stations sealed
description: SIALKOT - The district administration has imposed fines on three petrol pumps for short measurement and sealed three illegal LPG stations during an inspection
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: SIALKOT - The district administration has imposed fines on three petrol pumps for short measurement and sealed three illegal LPG stations during an inspection drive. According to a spokesperson on Friday, Assistant Commissioner Pasrur Sana Sharafat, along with her team, inspected fuel measuring equipment at various petrol pumps on Chawinda Road. During the drive, she also identified three LPG stations involved in illegal decanting at different locations across the city. The authorities imposed fines, confiscated the equipment used for illegal decanting and referred the cases to the Civil Defence Department for further legal action.

headline: Final land distribution, allotment decisions cannot be reopened, rules FCC
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Constitutional Court (FCCP) has ruled that final decisions by revenue and consolidation authorities regarding land distribution and
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Federal Constitutional Court (FCCP) has ruled that final decisions by revenue and consolidation authorities regarding land distribution and allotment cannot be reopened merely on the basis of disputes over land identification or khasra numbers. Dismissing a woman’s petition concerning ownership of land on which a girls’ school was built in Bhakkar, the court also held that an executing cannot not amend a final decree or go beyond its scope. A two-member bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Hussain Shah and Justice Rozi Khan Barrech ruled that repeatedly raising the same dispute through different judicial proceedings was impermissible and that final court decisions must be respected. The petitioner, Anwari, claimed that a girls’ school in Shah Alam Dagar village of Kallur Kot tehsil, Bhakkar district, had been constructed on her land instead of the three kanals and 16 marlas donated by Shera Khan for the purpose. During the proceedings, land consolidation in the area was completed, and the petitioner challenged the process before various forums, eventually reaching the Supreme Court. The apex court had held that land redistribution and re-allotment primarily fell within the jurisdiction of consolidation authorities, whose decisions could not ordinarily be interfered with by courts. The FCCP observed that the consolidation proceedings had finally determined the petitioner’s land rights and ownership, without reducing her overall landholding. It further held that constitutional jurisdiction was not meant to provide another forum for reopening factual matters already decided by competent authorities. A final decision could only be reopened in cases involving fraud, mistake or lack of jurisdiction. Finding no illegality, legal defect or misreading of evidence in the decisions of the lower forums, the court dismissed the petition and declined leave to appeal.

headline: Car falls into Abbasia canal
description: BAHAWALPUR - A speeding car fell down into Abbasia canal near Head Panjnad; however, no loss of life was reported, said officials of the Rescue 1122. According
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: BAHAWALPUR - A speeding car fell down into Abbasia canal near Head Panjnad; however, no loss of life was reported, said officials of the Rescue 1122. According to Rescue 1122, a car plunged into the Abbasia canal near Head Panjnad. The vehicle was carrying two occupants, both of whom managed to get out of the water safely before fleeing the scene. Before rescue teams arrived, Patrolling Police had secured the vehicle with a rope. The car remained clearly visible near the canal bank. Rescue personnel were briefed on safety precautions, and the Tehsil In-charge was also informed. Local police have been investigating the incident. Further probe was in process.

headline: GCUF organises seminar to highlight role of AI in improving learning outcomes
description: FAISALABAD - Government College University Faisalabad (GCUF) through its department of Education organized a seminar titled “Outcome Based Assessment in
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: FAISALABAD - Government College University Faisalabad (GCUF) through its department of Education organized a seminar titled “Outcome Based Assessment in the Age of AI” to explore emerging trends in educational assessment and highlight the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving learning outcomes. Prof Dr. Nasir Mahmood (T.I.) Vice Chancellor of Allama Iqbal Open University Islamabad and Chairman of the National Accreditation Council for Teacher Education attended the seminar as the chief guest. Addressing the participants Prof Dr. Nasir Mahmood highlighted the transformative role of artificial intelligence in educational assessment. He emphasized the need for authentic, skill based and outcome oriented assessment methods to ensure meaningful learning and effectively evaluate students’ competencies in the age of AI. Prof Dr. M. Asim Mahmood Dean of the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences emphasized the importance of aligning teaching and assessment practices with clearly defined learning outcomes to meet the evolving demands of education in the era of artificial intelligence. Dr Shumaila Shahzad Chairperson of the Department of Education reaffirmed the department’s commitment to promoting innovative assessment practices and incorporating emerging educational approaches to enhance the quality of education. The seminar provided a platform for highlighting the significance of outcome based assessment and exploring the potential of artificial intelligence in strengthening educational practices and improving learning outcomes. Meanwhile, The City Traffic Police continues its crackdown on dangerous one wheeling and over speeding by motorcycles and vehicles. In this regard, special anti one wheeling checkpoints were established on Canal Road during the night between Thursday and Friday, where intensive checking and effective enforcement measures were carried out. The operations were conducted under the supervision of DSP Madina Town Irfan Ashiq Goraya on the directions of CTO Nasir Javed Rana. During the operation, a case was registered against a motorcyclist involved in one wheeling. The suspect along with the motorcycle was transferred to the concerned police station and the suspect was taken into custody. In addition vehicles and motorcycles were checked to prevent over speeding, and legal action was taken against violators. CTO Nasir Javed Rana stated that dangerous practices such as one wheeling and over speeding would not be tolerated under any circumstances. He emphasized that indiscriminate enforcement actions against those endangering public safety would continue to protect the lives and property of citizens. He urged citizens to refrain from one wheeling and over-speeding, observe prescribed speed limits, comply with traffic laws and ensure the safety of their own lives as well as those of others.

headline: No-parking sign ignored as vehicles occupy footpath in Muzaffargarh
description: MUZAFFAR GARH - A no-parking signboard appears to have been reduced to a mere display as vehicles continue to occupy the footpath beneath it, causing
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text: MUZAFFAR GARH - A no-parking signboard appears to have been reduced to a mere display as vehicles continue to occupy the footpath beneath it, causing inconvenience to pedestrians and raising questions about the enforcement of traffic regulations in the city. The footpath, meant to provide a safe passage for pedestrians, has allegedly been turned into an informal parking stand, forcing citizens to walk on busy roads and exposing themselves to the risk of traffic accidents. Residents have expressed concern over the deteriorating condition of footpaths, many of which are damaged and further obstructed by illegally parked vehicles. They questioned whether the designated pedestrian pathways were meant for public use or had effectively been handed over to motorists. Citizens have urged Deputy Commissioner Hafiz Usman Tahir Jappa to take immediate notice of the situation and order action against those responsible for turning no-parking zones and pedestrian footpaths into parking spaces. They also called for effective enforcement of parking restrictions and restoration of footpaths to ensure safe and unobstructed passage for pedestrians.
