headline: Rahim Yar Khan to hold grand Diwali event on instructions of CM
description: RAHIM YAR KHAN - On the directions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the district administration has decided to hold a grand event in Rahim Yar
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: RAHIM YAR KHAN - On the directions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the district administration has decided to hold a grand event in Rahim Yar Khan for the Hindu community’s religious festival of Diwali this year, instead of marking it in the usual way. Several provincial ministers, senior officials, public representatives and leaders of minority communities are expected to attend in large numbers. The administration has also announced a polio vaccination campaign that will run from November 2 to 5. More than 1.1 million children will be given polio drops during the campaign. Special health department teams will be posted at inter-provincial and inter-district checkpoints and at railway stations to make sure that every child travelling during the campaign is vaccinated. According to details, Deputy Commissioner Zaheer Anwar Jappa chaired two special meetings on Friday. Officials of the relevant departments from across the district attended. The first meeting decided, on the Chief Minister’s instructions, to hold the grand Diwali event on November 4. Along with the Diwali celebrations, cheques and gifts will be distributed to members of the minority community on behalf of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to share in their festivities. Low-cost Diwali bazaars will also be set up so that families can buy festive goods at affordable prices. Speaking at the meeting, the Deputy Commissioner said that, in line with the vision of the founder of Pakistan, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, followers of all religions in Pakistan enjoy complete religious freedom. He said promoting interfaith harmony and tolerance is among the government’s top priorities. The meeting was also told that special security arrangements will be made for the event to ensure that it takes place smoothly and safely. Speaking at the second meeting, Deputy Commissioner Zaheer Anwar Jappa said a special anti-polio campaign will be carried out across the district from November 2 to 5. More than 1.1 million children under the age of five will be vaccinated against the disease.

headline: Man sentenced to death, accomplice jailed for 30 years in murder case
description: SARGODHA - Additional District and Sessions Judge Akhtar Bhatti on Friday awarded the death sentence to one accused and 30 years of imprisonment to his
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: SARGODHA - Additional District and Sessions Judge Akhtar Bhatti on Friday awarded the death sentence to one accused and 30 years of imprisonment to his accomplice in a murder case. According to the prosecution, accused Shoukat and Usman had murdered Khurram Abbas during a domestic dispute. The concerned police registered a case and arrested both accused. Subsequently, police submitted challans before the court. After hearing arguments from both sides and examining the evidence, the court awarded the death sentence to Shoukat along with a fine of Rs500,000, while his co-accused Usman was sentenced to 30 years of imprisonment and fined Rs100,000.

headline: Man sets himself on fire outside Muzaffargarh district courts
description: MUZAFFAR GARH - A 45-year-old man allegedly attempted suicide by setting himself on fire outside the main gate of the District and Sessions Court in
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text: MUZAFFAR GARH - A 45-year-old man allegedly attempted suicide by setting himself on fire outside the main gate of the District and Sessions Court in Muzaffargarh on Friday, leaving 45.5 per cent of his body burnt, Rescue 1122 officials said. The injured man was identified as Allah Bakhshaya, son of Allah Wasaya, a resident of Mauza Walot in Shah Jamal. According to Rescue 1122, its ambulance and rescue motorcycle reached the scene shortly after receiving information about the incident. Rescue personnel provided first aid to the victim at the site before shifting him in critical condition to the District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital, Muzaffargarh. Meanwhile, sources familiar with the matter claimed that the incident was linked to a decade-old case involving the alleged sexual assault of the man’s daughter. According to these sources, the victim’s father had been pursuing the case against an influential and wealthy suspect for nearly 10 years but had allegedly failed to secure justice through the country’s judicial system. The allegations and circumstances surrounding the decade-old case could not be independently verified. Further details about the incident and the man’s motive were awaited.

headline: Foreign Office appoints key diplomats in major reshuffle
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has undertaken a major reshuffle in its diplomatic team, involving key ambassadorial appointments in Europe and important assignments at
author: MATEEN HAIDER
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has undertaken a major reshuffle in its diplomatic team, involving key ambassadorial appointments in Europe and important assignments at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with senior diplomat Nabeel Munir appointed as Pakistan’s new Ambassador to the European Union and Belgium in Brussels. Nabeel Munir, who was serving as Special Secretary at the Foreign Office dealing with United Nations affairs, will replace Ambassador Rahim Hayat Qureshi, who has been transferred and posted as Pakistan’s Ambassador to Spain. This would be Ambassador Nabeel Munir second Ambassadorial posting. He earlier served as ambassador to South Korea. The latest diplomatic changes also involve several senior officers returning from important overseas assignments and being given new responsibilities at the Foreign Office in Islamabad. Ambassador Khalil Hashmi, who recently returned from Beijing after completing his assignment as Pakistan’s Ambassador to China, has been appointed National Coordinator for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at the Foreign Office. Dr Muhammad Faisal, who was previously serving as National Coordinator for the SCO, has been assigned the additional responsibility of Additional Secretary Asia-Pacific at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Dr Faisal is considered as an expert on South Asia and India. In another significant administrative change, Ambassador Ibrar Hashmi has been appointed Additional Secretary for Economic Diplomacy and the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) at the Foreign Office. Sajjad Haider Khan, who is new spokesman of the foreign Office, has been directed to continue additionally as DG South Asia desk in the foreign Ministry. The reshuffle is part of the Foreign Office’s broader exercise to reposition senior diplomats across key bilateral, multilateral and economic diplomacy portfolios, particularly at a time when Pakistan is seeking to strengthen its engagement with European institutions, regional organisations and international economic partners. The appointments place experienced diplomats in important positions dealing with Pakistan’s relations with the European Union, China, the SCO, the Asia-Pacific region and international economic cooperation.

headline: IHC CJ refers plea challenging Judicial Commission decision to another bench
description: ISLAMABAD - Chief Justice, Islamabad High Court (IHC) Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar on Friday directed the constitution of a new bench to hear a constitutional
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Chief Justice, Islamabad High Court (IHC) Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar on Friday directed the constitution of a new bench to hear a constitutional petition challenging the April 28, decision of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan. During the hearing of the petition along with objections raised by the court office, petitioner’s counsel Yawar Gardezi submitted that the petition had been filed under Article 199 of the Constitution, making the Federation of Pakistan, Judicial Commission, President and Prime Minister respondents. The petitioner has sought the annulment of the Judicial Commission’s decision, which held that a vacancy arising from the transfer of a high court judge would not be treated as a vacant position for an initial appointment. The petition contends that the decision is contrary to Articles 4, 25, 175-A and 193 of the Constitution and should be declared unlawful. It also seeks a declaration that the three vacancies arising after the transfers of judges on April 29, 2026, be treated as vacant positions under Article 175-A(8), allowing every member of the Judicial Commission to exercise the constitutional right to propose nominations for these posts. Chief Justice Dogar observed that he was also a member of the Judicial Commission against whose decision the petition had been filed, and therefore it would be appropriate for another bench to hear the matter. “I do not want to pass any order in this case, as it may give the impression that favour is being extended,” he observed, adding that the case would be placed before another bench within a day or two. The chief justice, however, observed that the new bench would also examine the objections. The court subsequently directed that the matter be placed before another bench and adjourned the hearing.

headline: Two die, one injured in bike-van collision
description: MAILSI - A terrible collision between a motorcycle and a passenger van near Adda Chakliyar on Mitro Tibba Sultanpur Road resulted in the death of two people
author: Peer Abdul Razaq Qureshi
article_text: MAILSI - A terrible collision between a motorcycle and a passenger van near Adda Chakliyar on Mitro Tibba Sultanpur Road resulted in the death of two people including a 10-year-old child, while a woman was seriously injured. According to Rescue 1122, the tragic accident occurred near Adda Chakliyar when a passenger van going from Mitro to Tibba Sultanpur collided with a motorcycle. As a result of the accident, the motorcycle rider Muhammad Nawaz son of Ghulam Hussain, resident of Chak No. 198, Tibba Sultanpur, died on the spot, while 10-year-old Ali Hassan son of Muhammad Irfan was critically injured due to severe head injuries, who later succumbed to his injuries. Mumtaz Bibi, wife of Muhammad Nawaz, was also injured in the accident with severe head injuries. As soon as the accident was reported, Rescue 1122 ambulances immediately reached the scene. Rescue personnel provided first aid to the injured and shifted them to Rural Health Center (RHC) Tibba Sultanpur. The tragic accident has left the area in a state of grief and sorrow over the loss of two precious human lives, including a 10-year-old innocent child. The exact reasons for the accident are yet to be revealed. Man killed in motorcycle-rickshaw collision in Khanewal A man was killed, while another sustained injuries when a motorcycle collided with a rickshaw near 4-AH in the Makhdum Pur area of Khanewal, rescuers said on Friday. The deceased was identified as 46-year-old Muhammad Waseem, while the injured person was identified as 37-year-old Ismail. The injured man was shifted to a nearby hospital, while the body was transported to the Civil Hospital. Further investigation was underway.

headline: Pakistan stresses need to uphold Int’l law, strengthen ICJ
description: UNITED NATIONS - Pakistan has stressed that international relations be governed by international law rather than the use of force, coercion or intimidation.
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: UNITED NATIONS - Pakistan has stressed that international relations be governed by international law rather than the use of force, coercion or intimidation. First Secretary Zulfiqar Ali said this during the General Assembly’s debate on the report of the International Court of Justice. He said that Pakistan reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to international law and the central role of the International Court of Justice in upholding the rules-based international order. The Ambassador also welcomed the ICJ’s recent Advisory Opinion on Israel’s obligations in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. which affirmed Israel’s legal obligation, as the occupying power, to facilitate rather than obstruct humanitarian relief operations by the United Nations and its entities. Zulfiqar Ali called for renewed commitment to the rule of law and the continued strengthening of the Court and reaffirmed Pakistan’s abiding faith in the principles of the UN Charter and international law.

headline: PA marks October as breast cancer awareness month
description: LAHORE - The Punjab Assembly (PA) marked ‘Breast cancer awareness month’ through a special awareness gathering organised under the leadership of
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - The Punjab Assembly (PA) marked ‘Breast cancer awareness month’ through a special awareness gathering organised under the leadership of the Women Parliamentary Caucus (WPC), reaffirming its commitment to promoting breast cancer awareness, early detection and timely screening among women. The gathering was held here on Friday under the leadership of MPA and Women Parliamentary Caucus Convener Ishrat Ashraf.

As part of the initiative, a pink ribbon was displayed to symbolize hope, courage and solidarity with those affected by breast cancer. The gathering provided an opportunity to honour breast cancer survivors, remember those who lost their lives to the disease and highlight the importance of awareness, early diagnosis and access to appropriate healthcare. Dr Omer Ayub, a qualified medical specialist, also delivered an awareness briefing on breast cancer, emphasizing the importance of recognizing potential warning signs, seeking timely medical advice and undergoing appropriate screening. The session underscored that early detection can significantly improve treatment outcomes and save lives. Participants were encouraged to wear pink as a gesture of support for breast cancer awareness and to help spread the message that timely diagnosis and access to healthcare are essential in the fight against the disease. Through the initiative, the Punjab Assembly and the Women Parliamentary Caucus reiterated their commitment to raising public awareness, encouraging preventive healthcare practices and supporting efforts to reduce the impact of breast cancer on women, families and communities.

headline: Punjab govt hospitals to abolish ‘parchi’ system within four weeks, LHC told
description: LAHORE - The Lahore High Court (LHC) has been informed that the Punjab government will abolish the existing ‘parchi’ (registration slip) system in
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LAHORE - The Lahore High Court (LHC) has been informed that the Punjab government will abolish the existing ‘parchi’ (registration slip) system in all government hospitals across the province within four weeks to ensure prompt medical attention to patients without unnecessary delays and long queues. Special Secretary (Health) Nabila Irfan gave the undertaking before Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains during the hearing of a public interest petition filed by Judicial Activism Panel seeking enforcement of fundamental rights and provision of basic healthcare facilities in government hospitals, on Friday. She assured the court that patients visiting public-sector hospitals, including those requiring emergency treatment and outpatient services, would no longer be required to obtain registration slips from designated counters before receiving medical attention.

headline: TikTok removed 23.2m videos in Pakistan for violating community guidelines
description: Islamabad - TikTok removed more than 23.2 million (23,243,711) videos in Pakistan between April and June 2026 for violating its Community Guidelines, according
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Islamabad - TikTok removed more than 23.2 million (23,243,711) videos in Pakistan between April and June 2026 for violating its Community Guidelines, according to its Q2 2026 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report. Globally, the platform removed over 188.2 million videos during the same period. The report provides an overview of TikTok’s enforcement efforts during the quarter, including data on content removals and account actions in Pakistan and worldwide. In Pakistan, the video removal rate stood at 1.1%. Of these, 99.7% were detected and taken down proactively, while 94.5% were taken down within 24 hours of posting. Meanwhile, 519,075 videos were restored following further review.

Globally, automated detection technologies accounted for 99.5% of video removals. Following further review, 6,262,383 videos were restored, while 92.7% of violating videos were removed within 24 hours of posting. The report also details action taken against fake and underage accounts. During the quarter, TikTok removed 146.8 million (146,807,400) fake accounts and an additional 26.8 million (26,840,767) accounts suspected of belonging to users under the age of 13. Globally, sensitive or mature themes accounted for 19.5% of video removals, while content related to mental and behavioural health accounted for 16.1%. Content involving body exposure and sexualised behaviour made up 13.8% of removals, followed by dangerous activities and challenges at 13.5%. Edited media and AI-generated content (AIGC) accounted for 1.8% of removed videos. TikTok’s quarterly Community Guidelines Enforcement Report provides an overview of its content moderation and enforcement efforts. For more information about the Q2 2026 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report and to learn more about TikTok’s Community Guidelines, safety tools, and policies, visit the TikTok Transparency Centre in Urdu or English.

headline: US orders non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia over security risks
description: DUBAI - The United States ordered non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia due to safety risks, the US embassy in

headline: Dildar Parvez Bhatti remembered on 32nd death anniversary
description: ISLAMABAD - Renowned television presenter, radio broadcaster, actor, columnist and professor Dildar Parvez Bhatti was remembered on his 32nd death anniversary
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Renowned television presenter, radio broadcaster, actor, columnist and professor Dildar Parvez Bhatti was remembered on his 32nd death anniversary on Friday. Born on November 30, 1948, he began his professional career with Radio Pakistan in the early 1970s and hosted the popular programme ‘Sohni Dharti’. His engaging presentation style earned him widespread recognition among viewers. He gained widespread popularity for hosting several well-known programmes, including Takra and Yadish Bakhair, which brought him considerable acclaim. Besides his work in broadcasting, Bhatti also made contributions to drama and literature as an actor and columnist. His versatile personality and command over language made him a prominent figure in Pakistan’s entertainment and literary circles. He passed away on October 30, 1994, following a brain hemorrhage. His contributions to radio, television and literature continue to be remembered by his admirers.

headline: Bill proposing quarterly determination to gas prices lands in Senate
description: ISLAMABAD - The federal government on Friday tabled a bill proposing quarterly determination to natural gas prices amid ongoing controversy over fuel’s
author: Imran Mukhtar
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The federal government on Friday tabled a bill proposing quarterly determination to natural gas prices amid ongoing controversy over fuel’s volatile pricing mechanism. Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry introduced the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the House that seeks to insert a new Section 8A in the OGRA Ordinance, 2002. The chair referred the bill to the Standing Committee on Cabinet Secretariat for further review. Under the proposed mechanism, a licensee for natural gas will submit its total revenue requirement on a quarterly basis — only to the extent of wellhead gas prices and cost of imported gas, including RLNG — for review by the Authority. The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) will then advise the federal government on the revised prescribed prices. In turn, the federal government, within 30 days, must determine minimum charges and sale price for each category of retail consumer. The bill also empowers the federal government to advise OGRA to consider the entire or part of a quarterly adjustment in its forthcoming determination under Section 8. In a controversial move, the bill amends Section 9 of the OGRA Ordinance abolishing the mandatory condition of public hearing by the Authority for revision of prescribed prices under section 8A. The statement of objects and reasons of the bill says the primary objective is to establish a quarterly gas pricing mechanism with the intent to adjust price fluctuation of natural gas including RLNG along with Rupee-Dollar parity in a timely manner to align tariffs with market realities. The tariff adjustment will signal accurate pricing, curb accumulation of circular debt in the gas sector and ensure financial and operational stability of the entire gas supply chain, it adds. Speaking on his calling attention notice, Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Senator Waqar Mehdi raised the proposed shifting of Pakistan Petroleum Limited’s (PPL) head office from Karachi to Islamabad, warning that the move might diminish “the strategic importance” of the port city in the national economy. He said a pattern was emerging of moving federal headquarters, ministries and corporations away from Karachi. He said PPL’s head office had been in Karachi since around 1951. Now attempts were being made to shift it to Islamabad through the board of directors, whose members were not elected representatives of the people, Senator Mehdi said. He said shifting would cost billions of rupees. Around 500 employees from Sindh worked in the PPL and would face severe economic burden besides separating from their families, he said. The company’s core activities and related infrastructure were linked to Karachi, he added. “From the federal government’s conduct, it seems tomorrow they will talk of shifting Karachi’s sea to Islamabad,” he said on a lighter note. He demanded the decision be withdrawn. PPP Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro said oil and gas was a subject of the Council of Common Interests. “How can you shift it without the permission of the CCI?” he asked. Replying to queries, Minister of State for Interior Chaudhry said PPL’s board had repeatedly said vacating the building had become inevitable. “We take everything towards provincialism, regionalism. PPL’s assets are not only in Sindh but also in Balochistan,” he said. He ruled out the notion that any employee of the company would get affected. “There is no provincialism in shifting this office from Karachi,” he said. Raising a calling attention notice on the deteriorating condition of the Hazara Motorway, Senator Mohsin Aziz said Rs168 billion had been spent on the project, amounting to nearly Rs1 billion per kilometre, yet sections of the road were caving in every five kilometres. He said if the project collapsed in ten years, someone must be held responsible. “The consultant and contractor should be questioned,” he said, noting that frequent accidents had been reported due to dilapidated condition of the motorway. Responding, Chaudhry said the Hazara Motorway project was started in 2015 and completed in 2018 and no pothole appeared in the first two years. After this, the contractor’s liability ended, he added. He said depressions had emerged at seven locations in 2024, prompting a study, while Rs900 million had been allocated for rehabilitation. “Restoration work on the Hazara Motorway has begun,” he added. ENDS/

PPP Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro said oil and gas was a subject of the Council of Common Interests. “How can you shift it without the permission of the CCI?” he asked.

Replying to queries, Minister of State for Interior Chaudhry said PPL’s board had repeatedly said vacating the building had become inevitable. “We take everything towards provincialism, regionalism. PPL’s assets are not only in Sindh but also in Balochistan,” he said. He ruled out the notion that any employee of the company would get affected. “There is no provincialism in shifting this office from Karachi,” he said.

Raising a calling attention notice on the deteriorating condition of the Hazara Motorway, Senator Mohsin Aziz said Rs168 billion had been spent on the project, amounting to nearly Rs1 billion per kilometre, yet sections of the road were caving in every five kilometres.

He said if the project collapsed in ten years, someone must be held responsible. “The consultant and contractor should be questioned,” he said, noting that frequent accidents had been reported due to dilapidated condition of the motorway.

Responding, Chaudhry said the Hazara Motorway project was started in 2015 and completed in 2018 and no pothole appeared in the first two years. After this, the contractor’s liability ended, he added.

He said depressions had emerged at seven locations in 2024, prompting a study, while Rs900 million had been allocated for rehabilitation. “Restoration work on the Hazara Motorway has begun,” he added.

ENDS/

headline: Multan unveils 11.41-foot chess king, seeks Guinness World Record
description: MULTAN - The divisional administration has installed an 11.41-foot-tall chess king, weighing approximately one tonne, on Multan Avenue, claiming it to be
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
MULTAN - The divisional administration has installed an 11.41-foot-tall chess king, weighing approximately one tonne, on Multan Avenue, claiming it to be Asia’s largest single-piece chess king and among the world’s six largest chess pieces. Carved from a single block of polished Gandhara stone, the monumental sculpture showcases intricate stone craftsmanship and is expected to become a major landmark and tourist attraction in the city. Commissioner Multan Aamir Kareem Khan said a formal application had been submitted to Guinness World Records to seek international recognition for the massive chess piece. He said the initiative aimed to bring global attention to Multan’s artistic heritage and distinctive creations while enhancing the city’s cultural and tourism appeal. The commissioner described the chess king as a unique symbol of Multan Avenue, adding that the administration sought to transform public spaces into prominent landmarks and project the city’s identity on the international stage.

The installation is expected to attract visitors, art enthusiasts and chess lovers, adding a distinctive feature to Multan’s urban landscape.

headline: Lahore Qalandars take talent hunt to Khushab, announce PDP trials
description: LAHORE - Lahore Qalandars have extended their Player Development Program (PDP) to Khushab, opening another pathway for emerging cricketers from the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Lahore Qalandars have extended their Player Development Program (PDP) to Khushab, opening another pathway for emerging cricketers from the region to showcase their abilities and pursue professional cricketing careers. The talent-hunt trials will take place on November 21, 2026, at 9am at the Jauharabad Sports Complex, where aspiring players will have an opportunity to impress the franchise’s talent identification team. The initiative has been launched at the request of Attorney General of Pakistan Mansoor Usman Awan, following repeated appeals from local youngsters seeking greater opportunities to demonstrate their cricketing potential. Through this programme, Lahore Qalandars aim to identify promising players from an area that has considerable enthusiasm for cricket but limited access to professional talent development platforms.

The trials will provide local youngsters with an opportunity to compete for recognition and potentially take their first steps towards higher-level cricket.

The franchise has built its reputation around discovering emerging talent beyond established cricketing centres, particularly from underrepresented regions where talented players often struggle to find exposure and professional opportunities.

Taking the PDP to Khushab represents another effort to bridge the gap between raw talent and opportunity, reinforcing Lahore Qalandars’ philosophy that geographical limitations or financial circumstances should not stand in the way of sporting ambitions.

Expressing his appreciation for the initiative, Attorney General Mansoor Usman Awan said the trials would play an important role in motivating young cricketers of Khushab to recognise and develop their potential.

He added that the programme could open doors to future opportunities for the region’s talented youngsters and expressed gratitude to Lahore Qalandars for bringing such an initiative to the district.

Awan also described the event as a significant development for Khushab, noting that an initiative of this scale and standard was being organised in the district for the first time in recent history.

headline: North Punjab clinch Mas-Wrestling title
description: LAHORE - North Punjab claimed the 9th National Mas-Wrestling Championship 2026 with 88 points, edging runners-up Islamabad (86) at Hamidi Hall, Pakistan Sports
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - North Punjab claimed the 9th National Mas-Wrestling Championship 2026 with 88 points, edging runners-up Islamabad (86) at Hamidi Hall, Pakistan Sports Complex. South Punjab finished third with 57 points. WAPDA’s Tayyaba Zubair won women’s 55kg gold, while Islamabad athletes dominated several other categories. In the men’s events, North Punjab secured three gold medals. PMWF Chairman Nawab Furqan Khan said the federation aimed to provide athletes international exposure and establish Pakistan among the leading nations in the traditional strength sport.

headline: NA unanimously passes resolution against all forms of workplace harassment
description: ISLAMABAD - National Assembly on Friday unanimously passed a resolution reaffirming Parliament’s commitment to protecting the dignity, equality and
author: Javaid-ur-Rahman
article_text: ISLAMABAD - National Assembly on Friday unanimously passed a resolution reaffirming Parliament’s commitment to protecting the dignity, equality and rights of every individual against all forms of workplace harassment and gender-based discrimination. Member of the National Assembly and Secretary of the Women’s Parliamentary Caucus (WPC), Dr. Shahida Rehmani, moved the resolution in the House. The resolution underscores that workplace harassment is not limited to conduct of a sexual nature but may also manifest itself through gender-based discrimination, intimidation, humiliation, degrading treatment, hostile behaviour and misuse of authority, whether sexual or non-sexual in nature. It reaffirms the legislative intent and protections enshrined in the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, as amended in 2022, which expressly recognises discrimination on the basis of gender, whether sexual or non-sexual, within the statutory framework of harassment. The resolution further emphasises that the absence of a sexual advance or demand does not diminish the seriousness of gender-based harassment or discrimination. It states that the dignity of individuals cannot be subjected to narrow distinctions between different forms of harassment and that all conduct falling within the scope of the law must be addressed with equal seriousness, fairness and accountability. Through this resolution, the National Assembly has called upon the Federal Government and all concerned institutions to ensure the effective implementation of existing legislation in its entirety, ensuring that no individual is deprived of statutory protection merely because the reported harassment or gender-based discrimination is non-sexual in nature. The initiative also reinforces the broader commitment of the Women’s Parliamentary Caucus to ensuring that workplaces across Pakistan remain free from harassment, intimidation, humiliation and discrimination. The resolution reaffirmed that a workplace free from harassment, humiliation and gender-based discrimination is not a privilege but a fundamental requirement of human dignity, equality and justice.

article_text:
KARACHI - Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab visited the Food Walk established in Sindhi Muslim Society. Chairman Chanesar Town Farhan Ghani accompanied him and gave a detailed briefing on various aspects of the Food Walk project, the facilities being provided, and the arrangements made for visitors. After reviewing the project, Mayor Karachi appreciated the efforts of Chanesar Town and said that the town deserved appreciation for creating such an excellent recreational destination for the people of Karachi. He said that the Food Walk would not only provide citizens with quality food facilities but also offer them a pleasant, traffic-free environment where families could comfortably spend their leisure time.

Barrister Murtaza Wahab said that Karachi is a large and diverse city, and providing citizens with better municipal services as well as recreational opportunities is also our responsibility. Projects like the Food Walk play an important role in bringing positive changes to urban life and making different parts of the city more attractive and vibrant.

He said that, alongside the Food Walk, efforts were also underway to develop Burns Road into an excellent food street to further promote Karachi’s traditional food culture and provide citizens with better dining facilities in an improved environment. The Mayor said that extensive efforts were being made to serve citizens under the local government system in Sindh. Our aim is to work in collaboration with all town administrations and increase both basic municipal facilities and recreational opportunities for citizens at their doorsteps.

He said that municipal institutions should introduce projects keeping in view the needs of the people and ensuring that these initiatives directly benefit the public. Development and public welfare projects would be undertaken across different parts of the city in collaboration with town administrations so that all citizens of Karachi could benefit from these facilities.

Mayor Karachi further said that the people of Karachi should visit this magnificent Food Walk in Sindhi Muslim Society and enjoy the environment and facilities available there. Public cooperation is also essential for the success of such projects.

He added that all available resources were being utilised to restore the vibrancy of Karachi and transform the city into a better, more beautiful and recreational destination. On the occasion, the Mayor Karachi also met citizens present at the Food Walk, interacted with them and sought their views and feedback regarding the project.

headline: Preserving Peshawar’s heritage key to promoting tourism & cultural identity, says Governor Kundi
description: PESHAWAR - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday said preserving Peshawar’s rich historical heritage was essential to promoting
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: PESHAWAR - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday said preserving Peshawar’s rich historical heritage was essential to promoting tourism and strengthening the city’s cultural identity, directing the authorities concerned to take practical measures for the restoration and promotion of historical sites. He expressed these views while chairing a meeting on the preservation, restoration and development of Peshawar’s historical heritage and tourist attractions. Adviser for Planning and Development Usman Saifullah Khan, Secretary Tourism Sadat Hassan and other relevant officials attended the meeting. The meeting was given a detailed briefing on Peshawar’s historical and cultural significance, conservation of heritage sites, night tourism, heritage tourism, and ongoing as well as proposed development projects. The Governor said Peshawar was a living symbol of centuries-old history, civilisation and culture, and stressed the need to project its historical identity to attract both domestic and foreign tourists. He directed the authorities to relocate the vintage ambulance and old fire brigade vehicles at Gor Khatri to a prominent place where visitors could easily view them. He also called for operating special tourist buses to facilitate visits to the city’s historical landmarks. Kundi further instructed officials to install large information boards near the motorway toll plaza highlighting Peshawar’s historical sites and cultural heritage so that visitors entering the city could learn about its rich past. He said cultural events should be organised regularly to preserve and promote Peshawar’s traditions, arts and literary heritage, adding that restoration work on the ancestral houses of legendary film icons Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor should also begin at the earliest. The Governor welcomed the practical steps being taken to conserve the city’s historical heritage and said restoration of heritage sites along with improved tourism facilities would further strengthen Peshawar’s cultural identity.

headline: Pakistan beat Djibouti 4-2 to end U-15 WCup debut in style
description: LAHORE - Pakistan’s young Shaheens finished their historic FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 campaign in Azerbaijan on a winning note,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan’s young Shaheens finished their historic FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 campaign in Azerbaijan on a winning note, defeating Djibouti 4-2 after staging an impressive second-half comeback. After trailing 1-0 at half-time, Pakistan produced a spirited response to secure their fourth victory in 10 matches and finish 169th in the overall standings, with four wins and two draws. PFF President Syed Mohsen Gilani, who attended the match, congratulated the players and team management, praising their efforts throughout the competition. He expressed confidence that the international exposure would help the young footballers develop and represent Pakistan with greater distinction in the future.

headline: Abid, Nosherwan share lead at 43rd Millat Tractors Governors Cup
description: LAHORE - Abid Iqbal of Lahore Gymkhana and Nosherwan Aslam of Garrison Club emerged as joint leaders after the opening round of the 43rd Millat Tractors
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Abid Iqbal of Lahore Gymkhana and Nosherwan Aslam of Garrison Club emerged as joint leaders after the opening round of the 43rd Millat Tractors Governors Cup, setting the stage for an exciting contest over the remaining two rounds. Both golfers produced impressive performances, carding identical net scores of 66 to take the early lead in the prestigious championship. Their strong starts have placed them in a promising position, although several contenders remain within striking distance as the competition progresses. Rawalpindi’s Jaswa Amjad and Lahore’s Qasim Ali Khan also made notable starts, returning net scores of 69 each to remain firmly in contention. Muhammad Shoaib of Lahore followed closely with a net 70, keeping himself in the hunt for the title. With the leading players separated by only a few strokes, the championship is shaping up to be a closely fought battle. Consistency, composure and effective course management are expected to play a decisive role in determining the eventual winner as the field heads into the next two rounds.

headline: LHC dismisses petition against procurement of 24 CT Scan machines
description: LAHORE - In a significant development for Punjab’s public healthcare sector, the Health and Population Department’s initiative to establish
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - In a significant development for Punjab’s public healthcare sector, the Health and Population Department’s initiative to establish in-house CT Scan facilities in 24 District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospitals has successfully withstood a rigorous legal and regulatory challenge, following the dismissal of the constitutional petition by the Lahore High Court (LHC). At the forefront of the legal proceedings, Muhammad Zeeshan Akhtar, Advocate High Court, contested the matter on behalf of M/s Vertex Medical, which emerged as the lowest successful bidder for the supply of Siemens-manufactured CT Scan Machines, globally recognized medical technology manufacturer.

The initiative was spearheaded by Secretary Health and Population Department, Nadia Saquib, who pursued the procurement of 24 CT Scan Machines with the objective of strengthening the diagnostic infrastructure of public-sector hospitals. The initiative is expected to strengthen institutional capacity, reduce dependence on outsourced diagnostic services and provide patients with improved access to essential diagnostic facilities within public-sector hospitals. One of the most remarkable aspects of this procurement is its exceptionally competitive pricing.

However, following the initiation of the procurement process, the matter encountered a rigorous challenge and was agitated before multiple forums. The procurement faced legal scrutiny and objections concerning its legality, technical suitability and public-interest implications, creating substantial challenges for the Department’s initiative. During the course of the proceedings, the matter was examined by the Punjab Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA). Following proceedings before the Lahore High Court and the consideration of the matter at the regulatory level, the Managing Director of PPRA, Sahabzadi Wasimah Umar, played a significant role in adjudicating the procurement dispute through a considered and reasoned approach. The matter subsequently came before the Lahore High Court in Constitutional Petition No. 66022 of 2026, filed by Eastern Medical Technology Services. The Court dismissed the petition, thereby allowing the procurement initiative to proceed without constitutional interference. The Court observed that the petitioner had failed to establish any violation of the Punjab Procurement Rules, 2014, and that the procurement did not fall within the sphere of mis-procurement. The Court also recognized that the Executive was entitled to move towards in-house arrangements for providing diagnostic and medical services to the public. The Court observed that technical, financial and policy matters fall primarily within the domain of the competent executive authorities and relevant experts, rather than being matters for judicial substitution of administrative judgment. The dismissal of the constitutional petition represents an important judicial development, sustaining the Department’s initiative against a substantial legal challenge, highlighting the role of Managing Director PPRA, Sahabzadi Wasimah Umar.

M/s Vertex Medical emerged as the lowest successful bidder for the supply of 24 Siemens CT Scan Machines. The successful completion of this procurement initiative would provide DHQ Hospitals with enhanced diagnostic capabilities. The development brings together the policy initiative of Secretary Health Nadia Saquib, the regulatory deliberation of Managing Director PPRA Sahabzadi Wasimah Umar, and the successful defense of the procurement through legal representation by Muhammad Zeeshan Akhtar, Advocate.

headline: Abubakar, Rubtsova claim two titles each at ITF J-30 Lahore
description: LAHORE - Pakistan’s Abubakar Talha and Russia’s Varvara Rubtsova claimed the boys’ and girls’ U-18 singles and doubles titles
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan’s Abubakar Talha and Russia’s Varvara Rubtsova claimed the boys’ and girls’ U-18 singles and doubles titles respectively as the ITF J-30 Lahore Ali Embroidery Mills International Junior Tennis Championship 2026 concluded at Aitchison College, marking the return of international junior tennis to the city after a gap of 25 years. In an all-Pakistan boys’ singles final, Abubakar overcame compatriot Hassan Usmani 7-6(7-5), 6-0, recovering from a closely contested opening set to dominate the second and secure the title. Hassan, meanwhile, reached his first international junior final, underlining the progress of Pakistan’s emerging tennis talent. Abubakar added the boys’ doubles trophy to his collection, partnering Hamza Roman to defeat Ahtesham Humayun and Amir Mazari 6-3, 6-2. Rubtsova secured the girls’ singles crown with a convincing 6-2, 6-2 victory over fellow Russian Stefaniila Vasilevskaia, completing an impressive campaign in Lahore. In the girls’ doubles final, Rubtsova completed the brace of titles as she, partnering with Evelina Dzepa, defeated Daixi Hu and Bismel Zia 6-0, 6-0. Ali Embroidery Mills Chief Executive Officer Tariq Zaman attended the concluding ceremony as chief guest. Among the distinguished guests were Pakistan Tennis Federation (PTF) President Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi, former Punjab sports secretary Fazal-ur-Rehman, Col (R) Asif Dar, Aitchison College Director of Sports Sajjad Rasool, Haider Ismail from USA, Naseem Ahmed, and Said Hassan, along with players, officials and members of the tennis fraternity. Organised by the Punjab Lawn Tennis Association (PLTA) with the support of Ali Embroidery Mills, the ITF J-30 event attracted more than 42 players from China, Kazakhstan, Australia, Russia, Bangladesh and other countries. The international participation provided Pakistani players with an opportunity to compete against foreign opponents, gain valuable match experience and earn ranking points. PLTA Senior Executive Vice-President Rashid Malik, recipient of the Sitara-e-Imtiaz and Tamgha-e-Imtiaz, thanked the sponsors, institutions and officials whose support contributed to the successful staging of the championship. He particularly acknowledged Tariq Zaman for sponsoring the event and supporting the development of junior tennis in Pakistan.

Malik also appreciated Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi for his leadership and support in bringing international junior tennis back to Lahore. He said the hosting of successive international tournaments, including ITF junior, Futures and women’s events, was an encouraging development for Pakistan tennis and would help local players improve their standards and international rankings.

He also thanked PLTA President Capt (R) Fazeel Asghar and the association’s management, as well as the Punjab government and Sports Board Punjab, for their support in promoting tennis. Special appreciation was extended to Aitchison College and its Principal, Dr S. M. Turab Hussain, for providing excellent facilities, hospitality and cooperation.

headline: MP/Rijas reach subsidiary final of Memorial Polo Cup
description: LAHORE - Master Paints/Rijas delivered a dominant performance to qualify for the subsidiary final of the 14th Maj Gen Saeed-uz-Zaman Janjua Memorial Polo Cup
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Master Paints/Rijas delivered a dominant performance to qualify for the subsidiary final of the 14th Maj Gen Saeed-uz-Zaman Janjua Memorial Polo Cup 2026, sponsored by JS Bank, after thumping Lotto Carpets Singapore 12–5.5 at the Lahore Garrison Polo Grounds on Friday. From the winning side, Raja M Mekayial Sami emerged as top scorer with superb seven goals while Sufi Hashim Bin Haris thrashed in three goals and Sufi Haroon Bin Haris converted one. For the losing side, which had a half goal handicap advantage, Imran Abid Mir banged in a brace while Arib Ali Malik and Ahmed Zubair Butt scored one goal apiece. The match showcased an aggressive display of teamwork and precise execution from Master Paints/Rijas, who asserted their control over the game right from the opening chukker. Master Paints/Rijas set an explosive pace immediately, with Mekayial leading the charge by netting three consecutive field goals to give his side a commanding early advantage. Lotto Carpets Singapore attempted to fight back as Imran Mir struck a field goal. However, MP/Rijas quickly responded through another field goal by Mekayial, followed by a field goal from Imran Mir for Lotto Carpets. MP/Rijas then extended their cushion further with a field goal by Sufi Haroon, another brilliant field goal by Mekayial, and a field goal by Sufi Hashim, maintaining complete dominance. Lotto Carpets Singapore’s Imran Mir converted a penalty to add to their tally. MP/Rijas kept up the pressure, with Mekayial scoring two back-to-back field goals, smoothly followed by a field goal from Sufi Hashim. In the final chukker, Sufi Hashim added another field goal for MP/Rijas. Lotto Carpets fought valiantly with field goals from Arib Ali Malik and Ahmed Zubair Butt, while Mekayial sealed the comprehensive victory with a final field goal for MP/Rijas.

headline: EOC reviews preparations for November polio campaign across 13 districts
description: Lahore - Punjab Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) Coordinator Khalid Parvaiz chaired a virtual meeting with representatives of District Health Authorities from
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Lahore - Punjab Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) Coordinator Khalid Parvaiz chaired a virtual meeting with representatives of District Health Authorities from 13 districts to review preparations for the upcoming November Sub-National Immunization Days (SNIDs), emphasizing comprehensive microplanning, effective campaign implementation and strengthened monitoring to ensure that every eligible child is vaccinated. The November campaign will commence on 2 November and continue until 8 November in Lahore, targeting approximately 9.3 million children across 1,161 union councils in 13 districts of Punjab. In Lahore, vaccination activities will be conducted over seven days, followed by two additional days for follow-up. In the remaining 12 districts, the campaign will be conducted over four days, comprising three days of vaccination and one additional day for follow-up.

A workforce of 77,894 personnel will be mobilized to conduct house-to-house vaccination, operate fixed vaccination points and deploy transit teams to reach children in high-mobility areas and other locations. During the meeting, the Punjab EOC Coordinator stressed the need to ensure that campaign microplans are comprehensive, accurate and responsive to the population dynamics of each district. He directed district health authorities to ensure the inclusion of migrant populations in microplans, improve team composition and deployment according to local requirements, and address operational gaps ahead of the campaign. “Microplanning must be of the highest standard, with particular attention to migrant and mobile populations to ensure that no eligible child is missed,” he emphasized. He also urged district authorities to give the campaign the highest priority and ensure that all operational arrangements are completed well before its commencement. Under the campaign plan, 31,869 mobile teams, 1,776 fixed teams and 1,150 transit teams will be deployed, supported by 1,211 Union Council Medical Officers and 6,205 Area In-Charges. The campaign will cover 13 districts: Bhakkar, Chakwal, Dera Ghazi Khan, Kot Addu, Lahore, Layyah, Mianwali, Multan, Murree, Muzaffargarh, Rajanpur, Rawalpindi and Rahim Yar Khan.

Lahore has the largest target, with more than 2.28 million children to be vaccinated, followed by Rahim Yar Khan with over 1.14 million, Multan with more than one million and Rawalpindi with approximately 990,000 children. Khalid Parvaiz directed district officials to maintain close oversight of campaign activities and ensure that Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) and other relevant supervisory officers regularly review progress during the campaign. He underscored the importance of effective intra-campaign monitoring to identify missed children, address implementation challenges and take timely corrective measures. He further directed that a 100 per cent post-campaign assessment be ensured to verify vaccination coverage, identify any missed children and assess the quality of campaign implementation.

Reiterating the importance of community engagement, the Punjab EOC Coordinator called for sustained communication with parents and caregivers, local influencers and community representatives to encourage cooperation with vaccination teams. He emphasized that children must receive polio drops during every campaign, irrespective of how many times they have been vaccinated previously.

“Polio has no cure, but it is preventable through vaccination. Parents must ensure that every eligible child receives polio drops whenever vaccination teams visit their homes,” he said, urging communities to cooperate with vaccinators and facilitate follow-up visits for children missed during initial visits.

The November campaign is part of ongoing efforts to strengthen population immunity and protect children against poliovirus transmission. The Punjab Emergency Operations Centre reiterated its commitment to ensuring high-quality campaign implementation, with a focus on reaching every eligible child and maintaining vigilance against the threat of polio.

author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Friday vowed to eliminate corruption from provincial government departments, acknowledging that officials in the revenue department, police and even the Anti-Corruption Establishment had been found involved in corrupt practices. Speaking at the launch ceremony of the Punjab Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Technology (PIET) initiative, she said Patwaris and Tehsildars routinely took bribes from people approaching them for official documents and resolution of their problems. She added that officials involved in corruption were being penalised and dismissed from service.

“You would be surprised to know that officials of the Anti-Corruption Establishment, a department responsible for eliminating corruption, were also found to be corrupt,” she told the audience. The chief minister asserted that she would resign if even a single penny of corruption was proved against her, while stressing that her government was determined to eliminate corrupt practices and red tape from public departments.

The chief minister called upon provincial ministers to keep their security and protocol arrangements to a minimum, saying unnecessary official privileges should not come in the way of public service. She said the provincial government had introduced a range of reforms to bring Punjab into the digital age, improve the business environment and equip young people with modern skills to meet the changing demands of industry. Highlighting the importance of industrial growth, she said Punjab played a significant role in the national economy and that the expansion of businesses depended on modern technology, a skilled workforce and a business-friendly environment. She said the government had issued loans worth around Rs200 billion under the Asaan Karobar Scheme, while more than 200,000 people had obtained no-objection certificates and other approvals through the e-Biz platform. Punjab had a workforce of 36 million, with industries increasingly demanding skilled labour, she said, adding that the government had provided training to 400,000 workers and planned to train another 600,000. More than 1,200 startups were operating in the province, while 50 common facilities had been brought together to develop industrial clusters. Skill development programmes had also been consolidated under one roof to improve access to vocational training, she added.

The chief minister said environmental monitoring was essential for sustainable industrial growth, but shutting down factories in the name of environmental protection was not the answer. Inspections should be strengthened and industrial units encouraged to meet environmental standards without depriving workers of their livelihoods. “I have no desire to shut down anyone’s business, but there will be no compromise on standards,” she said, adding that the government’s objective was to provide people with a clean environment and safe food. She said the provincial government was focusing on broadening the tax base rather than imposing additional taxes, claiming that Punjab’s revenue had increased from Rs200 billion to Rs1 trillion.

Before launching PIET, she said, the government had pledged to eliminate red tape across departments. She also urged banks to simplify their procedures for extending financing to businesses.

Referring to the challenges faced by local manufacturers, she said Punjab produced cutlery and electric fans but manufacturers had to send their products to China for glazing, material testing and even noise testing of fans because of the absence of adequate local certification facilities.

International organisations, including FIFA, were reluctant to procure Pakistani sports goods without proper certification, she said, adding that the government would address these shortcomings and strengthen local testing facilities to improve the competitiveness of domestic industries.

She observed that industrial estates and special economic zones had largely turned into real estate ventures instead of serving their intended purpose of promoting manufacturing.

The government planned to provide land for industrial use on lease at monthly rates ranging from Rs80,000 to Rs200,000 to encourage investment in manufacturing, she said.

The chief minister also said the government was taking steps to eliminate encroachments and the so-called ‘Dala culture’ from Punjab, adding that longstanding illegal occupations had been removed. Designated spaces had been created for street vendors to ensure that roads remained accessible to commuters.

Highlighting agricultural reforms, she said the government aimed to distribute 45,000 tractors during the current year, compared with just 3,000 distributed over the previous two decades.

Modern agricultural machinery was also being introduced to improve productivity, while farmers were being provided tractors and super seeders at subsidised rates, she added.

She said financial support was being extended to small and medium-sized investors, while substantial resources were being allocated for agriculture and livestock development.

Stressing the need for a stable business environment, Ms Maryam said frequent protests, unrest and vandalism disrupted economic activity and made it difficult for businesses and workers to operate.

“People are my family, and ensuring the safety of the food they consume is also my responsibility,” she said, reiterating that the government wanted businesses to flourish while maintaining quality standards and protecting public health.

headline: MIT Solutions defeat SBP in thrilling finale to lift President’s Trophy
description: LAHORE - Markhor IT (MIT Solutions) emerged as champions of the President’s Trophy Grade-I after overcoming State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) by 51 runs in a
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Markhor IT (MIT Solutions) emerged as champions of the President’s Trophy Grade-I after overcoming State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) by 51 runs in a gripping final at Bagh-e-Jinnah on Friday, with experienced all-rounder Khalid Usman delivering the decisive blow through an impressive four-wicket haul. Chasing a challenging target of 237, SBP resumed the final day’s play at 165-7 but failed to withstand MIT Solutions’ bowling attack, managing just 20 additional runs before being dismissed for 185 in the first session to surrender the title. Khalid Usman spearheaded the successful defence, finishing with outstanding figures of 4-38 in 16.5 overs. Mohammad Ismaeel provided valuable support with two wickets, while Aamer Jamal and Salman Aslam claimed one apiece. SBP’s hopes rested on Mubashir Khan, who had remained unbeaten overnight, but Ismaeel ended his resistance by dismissing him for 32 off 56 balls. Mohammad Abbas contributed six before falling, while Kashif Bhatti’s dismissal for two at the hands of Khalid Usman sealed MIT Solutions’ triumph. Earlier, MIT Solutions had resumed their second innings at 273-7 and extended their total to 296 in 74.5 overs. Aamer Jamal played a crucial innings of 55 off 81 deliveries, striking seven boundaries, after having already produced a match-defining seven-wicket performance in SBP’s first innings. For SBP, Test fast bowler Mohammad Abbas led the attack with 5-70, while Sirajuddin claimed three. Set 237 for victory, SBP began positively through Hasan Raza and Abdullah Fazal, who added 49 runs for the opening wicket. Hasan subsequently anchored the innings with a determined 73 off 136 balls, including eight boundaries. However, MIT Solutions repeatedly struck at crucial moments, triggering a dramatic middle-order collapse that left SBP struggling at 147-7. Despite Mubashir’s resistance, SBP could not complete the chase, as MIT Solutions finished the contest in style to lift the President’s Trophy Grade-I crown.

headline: Pakistan seek historic home tri-series title against confident Sri Lanka
description: LAHORE - Pakistan will be aiming to end their long wait for a home-grown ODI tri-series title when they take on an explosive Sri Lankan side in the final of
author: Azhar Khan
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan will be aiming to end their long wait for a home-grown ODI tri-series title when they take on an explosive Sri Lankan side in the final of the tournament at Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday, with both teams determined to finish an entertaining competition on a winning note. The final promises an intriguing battle between Pakistan’s formidable bowling attack and Sri Lanka’s aggressive batting line-up. While Pakistan have demonstrated their ability to dominate opponents with the ball, Sri Lanka have emerged as one of the most dangerous batting sides in the competition, producing several remarkable performances. Pakistan entered the final after winning their opening three matches, including two victories against England and one over Sri Lanka. However, their momentum suffered a setback in their last league encounter when Sri Lanka handed them a comprehensive eight-wicket defeat, dismissing the hosts for a disappointing 110 before completing the chase comfortably. Despite that setback, Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson remains optimistic about his team’s prospects. “To get three wins in a row was a good sign, but I still don’t think we have played our best game yet. Hopefully, we are saving that for the final,” Hesson said. Pakistan’s biggest concern remains their inconsistent top-order batting. Experienced openers Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam have struggled to produce substantial contributions, scoring 31 and 118 runs respectively in four matches. Their performances will be particularly important against a confident Sri Lankan attack. In contrast, Pakistan’s pace combination of Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf has provided impressive results, with valuable support from spinners Shadab Khan and Arafat Minhas. Their ability to restrict Sri Lanka’s powerful batting unit could prove decisive. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, have been the tournament’s most exciting batting outfit. Their extraordinary chase of 430 against England highlighted their enormous scoring potential, while they accumulated 331 runs in their latest encounter despite eventually losing by 55 runs. Young middle-order sensation Pavan Rathnayake has been particularly outstanding, registering two centuries against England and scoring 79 against Pakistan. His impressive 350-run tally at an average of 116.67 makes him a major threat in Saturday’s showdown. Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis has expressed confidence but acknowledged the challenge of facing Pakistan on home soil. Pakistan will also be motivated by history, having last won an ODI tri-series title in 2008. With next year’s ODI World Cup approaching, Saturday’s final offers both sides an important opportunity to strengthen their preparations and build confidence. For Pakistan, the equation is straightforward: rediscover their batting rhythm, maintain their bowling intensity and deliver under pressure. Sri Lanka, however, will arrive determined to spoil the hosts’ celebrations once again.

headline: Heinous crime falls at historic rate across Punjab
description: LAHORE - Punjab Police Inspector General Abdul Kareem on Friday chaired an important follow-up meeting on crime control at the Central Police Office. In light
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Police Inspector General Abdul Kareem on Friday chaired an important follow-up meeting on crime control at the Central Police Office. In light of the directions issued during the meeting chaired by Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif last week, the weekly performance of all regions and districts was reviewed in detail. During the briefing, DIG Investigation Punjab informed the meeting that heinous crime incidents across Punjab had declined significantly during the current week compared to the previous week. IG Punjab Abdul Kareem directed all RPOs and DPOs to identify crime hotspots and take immediate action to curb heinous crimes. He ordered special focus on preventing robbery, robbery-murder, sexual violence against women and children, assault, organized crime and other heinous offences.

IG Punjab said that, on the directions of Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the crime situation was being reviewed regularly on a weekly basis to ensure effective measures for controlling crime and protecting the lives and property of citizens. Directing improvements in challan submission rates to ensure that suspects involved in heinous crimes receive appropriate punishment, he instructed officers to follow up daily on pending forensic reports in criminal cases, including cases of sexual violence against women and children, and ensure that the reports were obtained promptly. IG Punjab also directed that efforts to arrest proclaimed offenders involved in robbery, robbery-murder and other heinous crimes be accelerated. The meeting was attended by Additional IG Investigation Punjab, Additional IG Operations Punjab, DIG Investigation Punjab, AIG Operations and AIG Administration and Security. CCPO Lahore, Additional IG South Punjab, all RPOs, CPOs, DPOs, DIG Operations Lahore and DIG Investigation Lahore, along with other relevant officers, participated through video link.

headline: FBR destroys illegal cigarettes worth Rs 570m in Sukkur
description: SUKKUR - The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) carried out a major operation in Sukkur, destroying non tax paid cigarettes and tobacco worth Rs 570 million here
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
SUKKUR - The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) carried out a major operation in Sukkur, destroying non tax paid cigarettes and tobacco worth Rs 570 million here on Friday. The Regional Tax Office (RTO) Sukkur seized and set ablaze confiscated illegal cigarettes in an opera-tion. During the last two months, 11 operations were conducted, resulting in the seizure of 1,644 cartons of illegal cigarettes. The value of the seized cigarettes has been estimated at Rs 210 million.

Tax evasion amounting to Rs 367 million was detected under the heads of Sales Tax and Federal Excise Duty. The action against illegal cigarettes was taken on the special directives of Chief Commissioner Zigham Abbas.

The confiscated cigarettes were destroyed under the supervision of Commissioner Mumtaz Ahmed Thebo and other officers. The operations were carried out by a special team headed by Inland Reve-nue Officer Abdul Majeed Sangi. Chief Commissioner Zigham Abbas said there is a zero tolerance policy against tax evasion and tax de-faulters.

Indiscriminate action will continue against those causing loss to the national exchequer, the Chief Commissioner said. He added that the sale of illegal cigarettes not only causes loss to national revenue but also creates difficulties for legal businesses. “We will take stricter actions to end tax evasion and protect the national exchequer,” said Chief Commissioner FBR.

headline: Five criminals arrested in injured condition after separate encounters
description: KARACHI - Central District Police arrested five alleged street criminals in injured condition following separate en-counters and recovered weapons,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Central District Police arrested five alleged street criminals in injured condition following separate en-counters and recovered weapons, mobile phones, cash and other valuables from their possession, SSP Central Dr. Imran Khan said on Friday. He said police signalled four suspicious motorcyclists to stop near Sector 11-J, New Karachi, but they opened fire on the police party. In the ensuing exchange of fire, two suspects, identified as Ilyas, son of Muhammad Siddiq, and Salman, son of Manwar Ali, were arrested in injured condition, while the other two managed to escape. Police recovered two pistols with ammunition, mobile phones, cash and other belongings from their possession, he added. In another encounter near Sector 12-D, New Karachi, two suspects, Rehan and Zeeshan, both sons of Zulfiqar, were arrested in injured condition following an exchange of fire. Police recovered a pistol, two mobile phones and cash from them.

headline: KU, PPMA sign MoU for collaborative partnership
description: KARACHI - The Department of Agriculture and Agribusiness Management (DAAM) at the University of Karachi (KU) and the Pakistan Pest Management Association
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - The Department of Agriculture and Agribusiness Management (DAAM) at the University of Karachi (KU) and the Pakistan Pest Management Association (PPMA) signed a memorandum of Understand-ing to establish a collaborative partnership. This strategic partnership aims to provide internships for students, raise public awareness of sustaina-ble pest control, and promote joint initiatives in research, innovation, and sustainable pest manage-ment across academic and community platforms. The MoU aims to develop innovative, sustainable pest management strategies that benefit both pub-lic health and the environment. The President of PPMA Ashraf Sattar Adamjee informed the audience that, at present, PPMA is play-ing the role of a ‘private regulatory authority’ in the absence of any government and semi-government organization looking after this government-neglected industry. He mentioned that PPMA will offer KU’s DAAM students real-world exposure through structured in-ternship programs, allowing them to work alongside industry professionals on impactful projects, building critical skills and preparing them for future careers. He added that PPMA will also evaluate and support entrepreneurial opportunities for innovative pest management solutions and related technologies developed by researchers at KU’s DAAM.

The KU’s Dean of Faculty of Science Professor Dr Bilquess Gul observed that through a mutual ex-change of academic and industry expertise, it would be easier to bridge theoretical knowledge with practical application. She said that KU will be the best platform to provide durable solutions to industry problems, as its aca-demia has vast experience on the topic and added that joint research should focus on eco-friendly pest control technologies, pest ecology, pesticide resistance, climate impact, and disease vector stud-ies in both the agriculture and urban sectors. Prof Dr Gul mentioned that there is a need to educate the public on sustainable pest control, hygiene practices, and environmental safety. She welcomed the idea that PPMA will form and organize a train-ing facility to train pest technicians from the pest control industry and students. The KU’s Dean of Faculty of Science Professor Dr Bilquees Gul and President of PPMA Ashraf Sattar Adamjee inked the MoU documents, the event was held at the Vice Chancellor Secretariat on Wednesday. The KU’s DAAM faculty, including its Chairperson Dr Soboohi Raza, representatives of PPMA, KU’s Di-rector of the Office of Research, Innovation and Commercialization Professor Dr Muhammad Naeem Khan, team ORIC and others were also present on this occasion.

headline: Kashmore forum highlights gaps in health, education and municipal services
description: KANDHKOT - Tameer Development Organization, a partner organisation of the Citizen Network for Budget Account-ability (CNBA), organised a Community
author: Zaheer Malik
article_text: KANDHKOT - Tameer Development Organization, a partner organisation of the Citizen Network for Budget Account-ability (CNBA), organised a Community Accountability Forum in Kashmore to highlight citizens’ experi-ences, concerns and perceptions regarding the delivery of essential public services in the health, edu-cation and municipal sectors. The CNBA is a nationwide network of civil society organisations managed by the Centre for Peace and Development Initiatives (CPDI). The CPDI conducts research and provides technical assistance and guidance, while its partner organisations engage local communities and relevant stakeholders through the network. The forum brought together a diverse group of participants, including community members, teachers, health professionals, local government representatives and civil society activists. Participants shared their experiences, identified shortcomings in public service delivery and discussed issues requiring the attention of the relevant government departmental. The discussions focused on the availability and quality of healthcare facilities, teachers’ attendance and the provision of basic facilities in government schools. Participants also raised concerns regarding ac-cess to clean drinking water, sanitation, drainage systems and proper waste management services. During the forum, participants evaluated the performance of these essential public services through a Community Score Card, recording their collective perceptions and assessments on a scale of one to five. Speaking at the forum Nazeer Ahmed Soomro, Ghulam Akbar and Sohail Awan said the exercise was aimed at bringing citizens’ voice and experiences into discussions on public service delivery. They em-phasised that such initiatives could help strengthen transparency and accountability by identifying gaps in essential services and drawing the attention of concerned government departments towards re-solving public grievances. They further stressed the importance of active community participation and constructive engagement between citizens and relevant authorities to improve the quality and accessibility of public services.

headline: KU reviews progress on unified brand identity and campus design guidelines
description: KARACHI - The Vice Chancellor of the University of Karachi Professor Dr Wasim Qazi chaired a campus branding review meeting at his office to evaluate progress
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - The Vice Chancellor of the University of Karachi Professor Dr Wasim Qazi chaired a campus branding review meeting at his office to evaluate progress on the University’s evolving Brand Book and campus design guidelines. The session marked a significant step in KU’s ongoing efforts to establish a unified institutional identity across both its communications and physical environment. During the meeting, a faculty member of KU’s Department of Visual Studies and a member of the Brand Book Committee, Murtaza Khaliq, accompanied by team members Mutahir Hasan Khan and Syed Udan Ahmed, presented a detailed update on the proposed Brand Book. Their presentation outlined standards for logo application, color palettes, and typography, emphasiz-ing the importance of consistency in KU’s official communications, promotional campaigns, and digital platforms. The framework aims to strengthen KU’s visibility and ensure its identity reflects the Univer-sity’s academic stature and international aspirations. Complementing this, other committee members from the same faculty, Wajiha Siddiqui and Muham-mad Mehdi, shared the committee’s interior design guidelines. Their proposals covered materials, fin-ishes, and furniture specifications, designed to harmonize KU’s physical spaces with its updated visual identity. The integration of spatial design with branding was highlighted as a means to foster pride, profession-alism, and a welcoming environment across the campus. The meeting was attended by members of the Brand Book Committee, including its convener and in-charge KU VS department Syed Shamoon Haider, KU students’ advisor Dr Nousheen Raza, Dr Faisal Nazeer, the KU Registrar Professor Dr Imran Ahmad Siddiqui, and others. The KU VC Professor Dr Wasim Qazi commended the committee’s progress and underscored the im-portance of aligning KU’s visual identity with its physical spaces. He noted that a cohesive brand pres-ence across signage, publications, interiors, and digital platforms would not only enhance KU’s public image but also enrich the academic environment for students, faculty, and visitors. On this occasion, the Committee members expressed strong appreciation for the collaborative efforts and reaffirmed its commitment to finalizing the Brand Book and design framework. Once completed, these guidelines will serve as KU’s standard reference for institutional identity, ensuring coherence across all touch points and reinforcing the University’s vision of becoming an institution of international repute.
