headline: ASEAN plays key role in addressing regional challenges: Sindh governor
description: KARACHI - Sindh Governor Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi on Thursday said that ASEAN is an active regional or-ganisation that has played an important role in
author: The Nation
article_text: KARACHI - Sindh Governor Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi on Thursday said that ASEAN is an active regional or-ganisation that has played an important role in addressing regional challenges. While talking to media persons after a meeting with Ambassadors, Consuls General and other diplo-matic representatives of ASEAN member countries, who called on him at the Governor House, the Governor of Sindh Muhammad Nehal Hashmi said that friendship, unity and collective efforts among Asian countries were the need of the hour, adding that developing countries were facing economic, social and environmental challenges that required greater mutual cooperation. The Governor said that climate change and floods had also severely affected ASEAN countries, under-scoring the need for joint initiatives to address environmental challenges. He further said that Pakistan’s successful foreign policy had enhanced country’s diplomatic significance and international acceptance. Referring to regional peace, Hashmi said that the Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir had made efforts to prevent the region from being drawn into war, while the Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar had also played important roles. Responding to a question about India’s water-related threats, the Sindh Governor said that access to water was a fundamental human right and any Indian threat to stop Pakistan’s water supply was an act of water aggression. Earlier, the meeting concluded with a renewed commitment by ASEAN diplomatic representatives and the Sindh Governor to strengthen regional cooperation, promote environmental sustainability and foster friendly relations among Asian countries. Diplomatic representatives from the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Myanmar attended the meeting. The Sindh Governor and the visiting diplomats also planted salping at the Quaid-e-Azam Urban Forest established at the Governor House, expressing their commitment to environmental protection and promoting a greener environment.

headline: Lanjar orders police reforms, faster emergency response, improved traffic management
description: KARACHI - An important meeting was held under the chairmanship of Sindh Minister for Home and Law, Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar here on Friday, to review the overall
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - An important meeting was held under the chairmanship of Sindh Minister for Home and Law, Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar here on Friday, to review the overall law and order situation across the province, crime prevention measures, the performance of Madadgar 15 Police, and steps to further improve the Traf-fic Management and Regulatory System. The meeting reviewed matters relating to the protection of citizens’ lives and property, improving po-lice response times, ensuring smoother traffic flow, and the effective use of modern technology. The Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar directed that the policing across the province be further strengthened to maintain law and order and ensure the protection of citizens’ lives and property. He said that preventing crime and providing a safe environment to the public remain the govern-ment’s top priorities. For this purpose, police patrolling, surveillance, and operations against criminal elements must be made more effective. He directed the concerned officers to utilize all available re-sources to improve the law and order situation and take practical measures to further enhance police performance. Emphasising the need to modernise Police 15 in line with contemporary requirements, the Sindh Home Minister stressed that citizens’ complaints must be promptly registered, police response must be timely, and effective action must be ensured. He directed that Police 15 be equipped with modern facilities and transformed into an efficient system capable of providing immediate assistance to citizens during emergencies while ensuring effective co-ordination among relevant police units and other institutions. The meeting also held a detailed discussion on improving the Traffic Management and Regulatory Sys-tem. The Sindh home minister directed that comprehensive recommendations be prepared to ensure smooth traffic flow in Karachi, minimise difficulties faced by commuters, and improve traffic discipline on roads. He said that traffic conditions at signals, intersections, and major junctions should be as-sessed and an effective mechanism developed to ensure uninterrupted traffic movement and facili-tate citizens in their daily commute. headline: Rupee gains 01 paisa against dollar
description: ISLAMABAD - Rupee on Friday appreciated by 01 paisa against the US dollar in interbank trading and closed at Rs276.75, compared to the previous day’s
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Rupee on Friday appreciated by 01 paisa against the US dollar in interbank trading and closed at Rs276.75, compared to the previous day’s closing of Rs276.76. According to the Forex Association of Pakistan (FAP), the dollar’s open-market buying and selling rates were Rs277.50 and Rs280, respectively. The price of the Euro increased by Rs1.51, closing at Rs309.79 against the previous day’s rate of Rs308.28, according to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP). The Japanese Yen remained unchanged to close at Rs1.75, while the British Pound surged by Rs2.74 and closed at Rs371.19 against the previous day’s Rs368.45. The exchange rates of the Emirate Dirham and the Saudi Riyal came down by 01 paisa each and closed at Rs75.34 and Rs73.74, respectively.

headline: Airstrikes, displacement worsen humanitarian crisis in Gaza, West Bank: UN
description: UNITED NATIONS - Airstrikes and other incidents continue to affect the safety and well-being of Palestinian civilians in Gaza and the West Bank, UN
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: UNITED NATIONS - Airstrikes and other incidents continue to affect the safety and well-being of Palestinian civilians in Gaza and the West Bank, UN humanitarians said on Thursday. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said its safety and security partners reported that on Wednesday in Gaza’s Khan Younis, a UN warehouse was hit by flying debris from a nearby airstrike. UN staff members escaped injury. The UN Office for Project Services (UNOPS) reported earlier in the week explosions near facilities, small-arms rounds hitting a UNOPS staff location and the detention of humanitarian convoy drivers at checkpoints. “Partners report that over the past week, about 100 Palestinian families lost their tents and other belongings in airstrikes, fires and other incidents,” OCHA said. “Humanitarian partners have mobilised support for these families through a rapid response process.” Again, the office said that all parties must uphold their obligations to protect civilians, including humanitarian personnel. The World Health Organisation (WHO) said that acute respiratory infections are the leading health condition reported in Gaza. A WHO report covering Oct 7, 2023 to Sept 30, 2026 showed viral meningitis increased to over 200 cases and probable bacterial meningitis increased to over 70 cases. “Health partners say that overcrowding, degraded water and sanitation infrastructure, and shortages of essential treatments continue to heighten transmission risks,” OCHA said. “To scale up services, it is critical to lift restrictions on the entry of humanitarian supplies, specialised equipment, engine oil, spare parts and other supplies. It is also urgent that UN member states provide additional funding for aid efforts.” The office said that in the West Bank, its partners report that the Hebron Municipality authorities recorded that about 3,000 Palestinians remain displaced from two neighbourhoods in the city. OCHA said that Israeli forces are still operating in the Hebron neighbourhoods, blocking the way in and imposing tight movement restrictions across the governorate. Their operations are disrupting Palestinians’ access to livelihoods, education, and services such as health care. Most evacuated families are staying with relatives, who have received support from local authorities and humanitarian partners. “Palestinians across the West Bank must be protected,” OCHA said. “Those displaced must be allowed o return voluntarily and safely. Further forced displacement and demolitions must be prevented. Safe and unhindered humanitarian access must be secured and facilitated.”

author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: MADRID - The death toll from Wednesday’s train collision in Spain’s Toledo province, south of Madrid, has risen to 69, while more than a dozen people remain hospitalised in critical condition, Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of Spain’s Castilla-La Mancha region, said Thursday. Garcia-Page said another body had been found at the crash site, adding that 50 injured people remained hospitalized in Castilla-La Mancha, while 60 had been discharged. Fifteen patients remained classified as “code red”, four of whom were showing signs of improvement, he said. While authorities believed that no more bodies would be found, he urged caution as crews continued searching the mangled wreckage of some of the worst-hit carriages. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, speaking to reporters after a meeting at the 112 emergency centre in Toledo, said “the entire state is fully mobilized” on three fronts: responding to the emergency, including rescuing and identifying victims; determining the cause of the accident; and ensuring that the central government provides compensation to victims’ families, “at least in material terms”.

headline: Pakistan tells UN it cannot remain idle amid cross-border terrorism from Afghanistan
description: UNITED NATIONS - Decrying a sharp spike in cross-border violence, Pakistan has warned that it cannot “sit idle” in the face of an externally backed
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: UNITED NATIONS - Decrying a sharp spike in cross-border violence, Pakistan has warned that it cannot “sit idle” in the face of an externally backed terrorist onslaught originating from Afghanistan, where the human rights situation continues to deteriorate. Speaking in the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee during an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on the human rights situation in Afghanistan, Richard Bennett, Pakistani delegate Muhammad Jawad Ajmal said his country has the right to respond in self-defence against militant networks. In this regard, he linked the ruling Taliban regime to the unimpeded regional operations of banned terrorist proxies, including the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and its Majeed Brigade, signaling a dangerous escalation in the tensions along the Pak-Afghan border. Ajmal, a counsellor in the Pakistan Mission to the UN, was commenting on the Bennet’s report which accused the Taliban of committing systematic violations against women and children in Afghanistan. Highlighting Taliban’s continued backtracking on their international obligations, the Pakistani delegate said that women and girls are denied fundamental freedoms and basic dignity, with discriminatory and abusive practices that contravene Islamic laws, traditions, and tenets of Muslim faith. Over the years, Ajmal said Pakistan welcomed millions of Afghan refugees who pose a serious threat to the country’s security, pointing out that it continues to facilitate vulnerable Afghans despite limitations. In this regard, he urged the international community to step up and shoulder its responsibility. During the last three years alone, he said, more than 4,700 innocent Pakistanis have lost their lives to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan. “On 16th March, Pakistan precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure, including drones and ammunition storage facilities used by the TTP to target innocent Pakistani civilians,” the Pakistani delegate said. “We will respond in self-defence, as and when needed and in accordance with international law against whosoever attempts to harm our citizens and our national security,” Jawad Ajmal added. At the outset, Richard Bennett, Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Afghanistan, warned that the Taliban have shown no willingness to reverse any of their systematic human rights violations. Instead, he reported the authorities have intensified repression through new edicts. Recalling the words of a girl from Balkh, he said: “Three words have come to define our lives: fear, tears and despair.” More than 2.6 million girls have been denied secondary education since 2021, approximately 9 million children face severe hunger and 3.7 million children under five suffer acute malnutrition, it was pointed out. Child labour is increasing, with some families selling or giving away their children, Bennett warned. Meanwhile, boys remaining in school face curricula increasingly shaped by Taliban ideology. “The regime is teaching a generation of boys that the exclusion of their sisters and mothers is normal,” he noted. New judicial rules sanction violence against women and girls, with punishment only when broken bones or visible bruises result, while a separate decree makes marital separation harder and allows a girl’s silence to count as consent to marriage, the special rapporteur said. Warning against normalising relations with the Taliban without independently verified human rights improvements, Bennett urged States to sustain humanitarian assistance and support accountability, including efforts to codify gender apartheid as a crime. “Abandoning them would hand the Taliban legitimacy in exchange for nothing, and Afghan women would pay first,” he declared.

headline: Philippines raises Mayon volcano alert following explosive eruption
description: ASTANA - The Philippines has raised the alert level for Mayon volcano to Level 3 following a “moderately explosive” eruption on Friday, prompting
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ASTANA - The Philippines has raised the alert level for Mayon volcano to Level 3 following a “moderately explosive” eruption on Friday, prompting authorities to call for the evacuation of residents living within a six-kilometer radius of the volcano, a wire service reported. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) confirmed the alert upgrade, warning of increased volcanic activity and the potential for further eruptions. According to PHIVOLCS, the eruption produced a dense ash plume that rapidly rose approximately 3,000 metres above the volcano’s summit crater. Moderate winds carried the plume west-southwest, with ashfall expected in the communities of Daraga, Guinobatan and neighboring municipalities in Albay province. The wire service explained that Alert Level 3 indicates a significant increase in volcanic activity, including sustained volcanic earthquakes and powerful emissions of steam and ash. PHIVOLCS warned that Mayon has entered a new phase of magmatic eruption, increasing the likelihood of lava flows in the coming days and weeks. Authorities also cautioned residents about potential volcanic hazards, including lava flows, rockfalls and other dangerous phenomena associated with increased volcanic activity. Mayon volcano, also known as Mount Mayon, is an active stratovolcano located in Albay province in the Bicol region of the Philippines, on the southeastern part of Luzon Island. It is among the country’s most closely monitored active volcanoes due to its history of eruptions and potential risks to nearby communities. Earlier, the wire service reported a magnitude 4.8 earthquake had struck China on October 29.

headline: 3 dead after helicopters collide in US Oregon
description: SAN FRANCISCO - Three people were killed after two helicopters collided in midair on Thursday near a small airport southwest of Portland, the US state of
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: SAN FRANCISCO - Three people were killed after two helicopters collided in midair on Thursday near a small airport southwest of Portland, the US state of Oregon, according to local authorities. Yamhill County Sheriff Sam Elliott told a news briefing Thursday that the collision occurred at around 2:15pm local time (2115 GMT) near McMinnville Municipal Airport, southeast of McMinnville. All three people aboard the two helicopters were killed. The victims included a flight instructor from Texas, a student pilot from Britain and a pilot from Newberg, Oregon, according to local authorities. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) identified the aircraft involved as a Robinson R22 carrying one pilot and an Airbus H125 carrying two people. The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will investigate the collision, with the NTSB leading the investigation and providing further updates. The cause has yet to be determined.

headline: Pakistan urges UN to safeguard global maritime trade amid rising conflicts
description: UNITED NATIONS - Pakistan Thursday strongly warned that intensifying global conflicts must not be allowed to paralyse international maritime commerce,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: UNITED NATIONS - Pakistan Thursday strongly warned that intensifying global conflicts must not be allowed to paralyse international maritime commerce, stressing that global shipping cannot become a “casualty of conflict and strife”. Speaking at a high-level United Nations Security Council debate, Pakistan’s Acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, stressed that international waterways must remain resilient drivers of the global economy. The debate on “Emerging Technologies and Maritime Security: Implications for Peace and Security” was convened by Greece, which holds the presidency of the 15-member Council for the month of October. Highlighting how rapidly regional choke points can trigger widespread energy and food crises, Ambassador Jadoon called for a legally grounded, cooperative framework to guarantee safe passage, secure critical marine infrastructure, and shield vulnerable developing economies from the cascading shocks of geopolitical instability. In this context, the Pakistani envoy strongly condemned the Houthi militia’s “nefarious designs” to weaponise Bab-Al-Mandab, attacking merchant shipping and seafarers navigating the strait, asserting that these attacks undermine maritime security and threaten peace and development of regional countries, especially that of Saudi Arabia, which has faced the group’s “blatant aggression”. “Pakistan reaffirms its unwavering support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and stands in complete solidarity with its leadership and people.” Ambassador Jadoon reiterated Pakistan’s unwavering support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of neighbouring and brotherly countries in the region bearing the collateral brunt of the maritime crises.

headline: Xi Jinping plays key role in drafting CPC resolution on party governance
description: BEIJING - Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has played a decisive role in drafting the Party
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: BEIJING - Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has played a decisive role in drafting the Party leadership’s Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance, a senior official said Friday. Hailing the resolution as the most important outcome of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, Tang Fangyu, head of the Policy Research Office of the CPC Central Committee, said the drafting of the resolution was carried out under the leadership of the CPC Central Committee, with Xi acting as the chief of the document drafting group, personally planning, guiding throughout the process, and setting the overall vision. Tang made the remarks at a press conference on the guiding principles from the just-concluded plenum, which was held in Beijing from Oct 26 to 29.

headline: Four nation Tehran talks signal emerging regional security architecture
description: ISLAMABAD - The high-level engagement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, the three signatories of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), and
author: MATEEN HAIDER
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The high-level engagement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, the three signatories of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), and Iranian leadership in Tehran has opened a potentially significant diplomatic pathway towards a new regional security architecture, with Pakistani diplomats and defence analysts describing the October 26 meeting as an important confidence-building initiative aimed at preventing further escalation in the Middle East. The Tehran engagement has assumed particular significance against the backdrop of heightened regional tensions, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the continuing Iran-US confrontation and growing concerns over maritime security in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Former Pakistani diplomats and senior defence analysts underscored that the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Türkiye security partnership should not be viewed merely through the prism of collective military defence. Rather, they argue, it could evolve into a broader regional arrangement that accommodates Iran and other Gulf countries, promotes strategic confidence and creates conditions for a negotiated settlement of regional conflicts.

Former Pakistani Ambassador to Russia Qazi M Khalilullah while talking to The Nation described the Tehran meeting as a commendable diplomatic initiative and a masterstroke of Pakistani diplomacy, arguing that the MJDA could become a building block of emerging regional security architecture.

In his assessment of the October 26 meeting, Ambassador Khalilullah observed that the arrangement could gradually expand into an inclusive regional framework with the participation of all Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states and Iran. Although the participating countries did not publicly disclose the substance of their discussions in Tehran, he said the positive atmosphere surrounding the engagement offered important indications about the intentions of the parties. According to Ambassador Khalilullah, the meeting reflected two significant considerations. First, the MJDA member states appeared determined to involve Iran rather than isolate it as they explored mutually acceptable ways to end the ongoing wars in the Middle East and establish lasting regional peace. He particularly welcomed the agreement among the four countries to maintain dialogue, saying continued engagement would help strengthen regional cooperation, peace and security. A similar emphasis on the complementary relationship between collective defence and diplomacy was highlighted by former Pakistani High Commissioner to Canada Ambassador Raza Bashir Tarar.

He said the meeting between the three MJDA signatories and Iranian leadership demonstrated that collective defence commitments did not contradict diplomatic engagement. Ambassador Tarar identified preventing further escalation as the most pressing regional priority, particularly in the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He also stressed the importance of resuming Iran-US dialogue and ensuring maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. Highlighting Pakistan’s unique diplomatic position, he noted that Islamabad maintained important relationships with both Riyadh and Tehran and had demonstrated its ability to facilitate communication between Washington and Tehran.

These factors, he argued, made Pakistan’s role particularly significant in efforts to defuse regional tensions. However, Ambassador Tarar cautioned against overstating the outcome of the Tehran engagement. While the participating countries reached an agreement in principle to continue regional dialogue, he said it would be premature to describe the meeting as a diplomatic breakthrough. He argued that the Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, concluded in September 2025 and augmented by Türkiye on August 7, 2026, had the potential to evolve into a significant regional deterrence framework, with other Middle Eastern countries potentially joining in the future. According to the senior defence analyst, the arrangement is fundamentally defensive and focuses on mutual defence cooperation, intelligence sharing, military interoperability, joint defence production, advanced technology sharing and maritime security. While some commentators have compared the emerging arrangement with NATO, Major General (Retd) Raza Muhammad maintained that it should not be viewed as a replication of the Western military alliance. Instead, its strategic value lies in combining the military capabilities, economic potential and diplomatic influence of the participating countries to deter aggression and promote regional security.

Gen Raza who served as president of Islamabad policy research Institute, also stressed that Middle Eastern stability was essential for global energy security and international commerce because of the region’s strategic maritime routes, hydrocarbon resources and critical shipping corridors, particularly the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab.

He argued that the contemporary regional confrontation was increasingly shaped by competition over strategic resources, maritime access and geopolitical influence, making a negotiated regional security understanding imperative.

Major General (r) Raza Muhammad credited Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, with the support of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, for Pakistan’s sustained efforts to facilitate regional peace and bring competing regional stakeholders to the negotiating table.

The agreement to maintain quadrilateral dialogue among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Iran offers an opportunity to institutionalise communication between important regional stakeholders at a time when the costs of further confrontation are becoming increasingly difficult to contain.

However, the sustainability of this initiative will depend on whether the participating countries can translate their diplomatic understanding into practical confidence-building measures, effective security cooperation and a wider political process involving the United States and other relevant regional actors.

For Pakistan, Gen Raza said the challenge and opportunity lie in sustaining its role as a credible interlocutor between competing regional powers while ensuring that the emerging defence partnership contributes to peace rather than becoming another source of geopolitical polarisation.

The Tehran meeting may not have delivered an immediate breakthrough, but it has opened a diplomatic window that regional stakeholders would ignore at their own peril.

ISLAMABAD - The high-level engagement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, the three signatories of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), and Iranian leadership in Tehran has opened a potentially significant diplomatic pathway towards a new regional security architecture, with Pakistani diplomats and defence analysts describing the October 26 meeting as an important confidence-building initiative aimed at preventing further escalation in the Middle East. The Tehran engagement has assumed particular significance against the backdrop of heightened regional tensions, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the continuing Iran-US confrontation and growing concerns over maritime security in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Former Pakistani diplomats and senior defence analysts underscored that the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Türkiye security partnership should not be viewed merely through the prism of collective military defence.  Rather, they argue, it could evolve into a broader regional arrangement that accommodates Iran and other Gulf countries, promotes strategic confidence and creates conditions for a negotiated settlement of regional conflicts.

Federal Constitutional Court upholds finality of judgments, rejects repeated challenges in land dispute

Former Pakistani Ambassador to Russia Qazi M Khalilullah while talking to The Nation described the Tehran meeting as a commendable diplomatic initiative and a masterstroke of Pakistani diplomacy, arguing that the MJDA could become a building block of emerging regional security architecture.

In his assessment of the October 26 meeting, Ambassador Khalilullah observed that the arrangement could gradually expand into an inclusive regional framework with the participation of all Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states and Iran. Although the participating countries did not publicly disclose the substance of their discussions in Tehran, he said the positive atmosphere surrounding the engagement offered important indications about the intentions of the parties. According to Ambassador Khalilullah, the meeting reflected two significant considerations. First, the MJDA member states appeared determined to involve Iran rather than isolate it as they explored mutually acceptable ways to end the ongoing wars in the Middle East and establish lasting regional peace. He particularly welcomed the agreement among the four countries to maintain dialogue, saying continued engagement would help strengthen regional cooperation, peace and security. A similar emphasis on the complementary relationship between collective defence and diplomacy was highlighted by former Pakistani High Commissioner to Canada Ambassador Raza Bashir Tarar.

DG ISPR says Pakistan-Saudi defence cooperation could expand, rules out wider military campaigns

He said the meeting between the three MJDA signatories and Iranian leadership demonstrated that collective defence commitments did not contradict diplomatic engagement. Ambassador Tarar identified preventing further escalation as the most pressing regional priority, particularly in the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He also stressed the importance of resuming Iran-US dialogue and ensuring maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. Highlighting Pakistan’s unique diplomatic position, he noted that Islamabad maintained important relationships with both Riyadh and Tehran and had demonstrated its ability to facilitate communication between Washington and Tehran.

Qatar offers Pakistani travellers free 30-day visa on arrival under four conditions

These factors, he argued, made Pakistan’s role particularly significant in efforts to defuse regional tensions. However, Ambassador Tarar cautioned against overstating the outcome of the Tehran engagement.  While the participating countries reached an agreement in principle to continue regional dialogue, he said it would be premature to describe the meeting as a diplomatic breakthrough. He argued that the Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, concluded in September 2025 and augmented by Türkiye on August 7, 2026, had the potential to evolve into a significant regional deterrence framework, with other Middle Eastern countries potentially joining in the future. According to the senior defence analyst, the arrangement is fundamentally defensive and focuses on mutual defence cooperation, intelligence sharing, military interoperability, joint defence production, advanced technology sharing and maritime security. While some commentators have compared the emerging arrangement with NATO, Major General (Retd) Raza Muhammad maintained that it should not be viewed as a replication of the Western military alliance. Instead, its strategic value lies in combining the military capabilities, economic potential and diplomatic influence of the participating countries to deter aggression and promote regional security.

Gen Raza who served as president of Islamabad policy research Institute, also stressed that Middle Eastern stability was essential for global energy security and international commerce because of the region’s strategic maritime routes, hydrocarbon resources and critical shipping corridors, particularly the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab.

He argued that the contemporary regional confrontation was increasingly shaped by competition over strategic resources, maritime access and geopolitical influence, making a negotiated regional security understanding imperative.

Major General (r) Raza Muhammad credited Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, with the support of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, for Pakistan’s sustained efforts to facilitate regional peace and bring competing regional stakeholders to the negotiating table.

APHC leader links Indian policies in Kashmir with Israeli practices in Palestine

The agreement to maintain quadrilateral dialogue among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Iran offers an opportunity to institutionalise communication between important regional stakeholders at a time when the costs of further confrontation are becoming increasingly difficult to contain.

However, the sustainability of this initiative will depend on whether the participating countries can translate their diplomatic understanding into practical confidence-building measures, effective security cooperation and a wider political process involving the United States and other relevant regional actors.

For Pakistan, Gen Raza said the challenge and opportunity lie in sustaining its role as a credible interlocutor between competing regional powers while ensuring that the emerging defence partnership contributes to peace rather than becoming another source of geopolitical polarisation.

The Tehran meeting may not have delivered an immediate breakthrough, but it has opened a diplomatic window that regional stakeholders would ignore at their own peril.

headline: Polio drive launched to vaccinate 24 million children across country
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Syed Mustafa Kamal on Friday inaugurated a nationwide sub-national
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Syed Mustafa Kamal on Friday inaugurated a nationwide sub-national polio vaccination campaign targeting approximately 24 million children in 97 high-risk districts from November 2 to 8. The campaign was launched at the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication, where the minister administered the first polio vaccine drops, marking the beginning of intensified efforts to interrupt poliovirus transmission and protect children from lifelong paralysis. The drive will mobilise more than 200,000 frontline polio workers to administer oral polio vaccine to children under five. It will run simultaneously in Pakistan and Afghanistan, the last two countries where wild poliovirus remains endemic, with coordinated cross-border efforts to prevent its spread. Speaking at the inauguration, Syed Mustafa Kamal said polio eradication remained a national priority and the government was committed to sustaining vaccination efforts until transmission was interrupted across the country.

The Minister said the campaign will run from the 2nd to the 8th of next month in ninety seven selected districts across the country. He highlighted that around twenty four million children under the age of five will be administered anti polio drops during the campaign. He urged parents to cooperate with polio workers and ensure that their children are vaccinated against this crippling disease. The Federal Minister also highlighted a decline in the number of polio cases in Pakistan as a result of the government’s sustained efforts. He said the November campaign would focus on improving vaccination coverage in selected districts and ensuring that every eligible child received the life-saving vaccine.

He also highlighted the challenges in southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where continued transmission required targeted interventions, stronger coordination and sustained vaccination activities.

The minister said the federal government was working closely with provincial authorities, district administrations and relevant stakeholders to address security and access challenges and ensure that children in affected areas were not missed.

He urged parents and caregivers to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure that every child under five received polio drops.

Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8 per cent since the launch of its national eradication programme in 1994, from an estimated 20,000 cases to 31 in 2025. Seven cases have been reported so far in 2026, underscoring the need for continued vigilance and high vaccination coverage.

Health authorities emphasized that polio has no cure and can cause permanent paralysis or death.

They urged parents to ensure that children receive two drops of oral polio vaccine during every campaign, describing the vaccine as safe and effective and stressing that repeated vaccination is essential to protecting children.

He urged parents to cooperate with polio workers and ensure that their children are vaccinated against this crippling disease. He said the November campaign would focus on improving vaccination coverage in selected districts and ensuring that every eligible child received the life-saving vaccine.
He also highlighted the challenges in southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where continued transmission required targeted interventions, stronger coordination and sustained vaccination activities.

Health authorities emphasized that polio has no cure and can cause permanent paralysis or death.

headline: PPP invites opposition parties to join parliamentary committees
description: ISLAMABAD - A Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) delegation, led by Senator Sherry Rehman on the directives of Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, on Friday invited
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) delegation, led by Senator Sherry Rehman on the directives of Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, on Friday invited opposition parties to join the parliamentary committee on electoral reforms and work together. The PPP delegation, visited the chamber of Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, and discussed the proposed electoral reforms committee. Speaking on the occasion, Sherry said the PPP wanted to develop an electoral system that enjoyed the confidence of all political parties. She urged opposition parties to present their proposals to the committee. She said repeated questions about the electoral process affected the credibility of Parliament, adding that free, fair and transparent elections were essential for protecting voters’ rights and strengthening democratic institutions. She said a resolution had been passed on the proposal of PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari for the formation of an electoral reforms committee comprising members of the National Assembly and Senate. The committee would prepare recommendations on electoral reforms and present them before Parliament for approval, she added. Allama Raja Nasir Abbas agreed with the proposal to make the electoral process more transparent.

The PPP delegation included Nayyar Bukhari, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Senator Waqar Mehdi, while the opposition delegation comprised Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Noor-ul-Haq Qadri and Senator Ali Zafar.

headline: Gold prices decline by Rs5,100 per tola to Rs420,536
description: ISLAMABAD - Gold prices witnessed a decline in the domestic market on Friday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs5,100 to Rs420,536,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Gold prices witnessed a decline in the domestic market on Friday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs5,100 to Rs420,536, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association. Similarly, the price of 10 grams of 24-karat gold decreased by Rs4,373 to Rs360,541, while the price of 10 grams of 22-karat gold declined by Rs4,009 to Rs330,507. In the international market, the price of gold decreased by $51 to $3,980 per ounce, the association reported. Meanwhile, the price of silver per tola declined by Rs238 to Rs5,530, while the price of 10 grams of 24-karat silver fell by Rs204 to Rs4,741. The price of silver in the international market also registered a decline, decreasing by $2.38 to $50.52 per ounce, the association added.

headline: PM Shehbaz orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan, ensures timely funding
description: ISLAMABAD - Prime Minister, Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, on Friday directed the relevant ministries and departments to accelerate work on ongoing federal
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Prime Minister, Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, on Friday directed the relevant ministries and departments to accelerate work on ongoing federal development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and ensure timely provision of funds for their completion. Chairing a review meeting on federal development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan, the prime minister ordered that all bottlenecks impeding project implementation be removed on a priority basis and effective coordination among relevant institutions be ensured to expedite progress, a Prime Minister’s Office news release said. He also directed regular monitoring of development projects, particularly those related to the energy sector, to ensure that the people of Gilgit-Baltistan could benefit from their outcomes at the earliest. The prime minister specifically instructed the authorities to ensure early completion of the 100-megawatt solar power project launched by the federal government for the people of Gilgit-Baltistan. The meeting also reviewed progress on ongoing hydropower, infrastructure and solar energy projects, including the completion of the Naltar Power Project. Discussions were also held on strengthening counterterrorism capabilities and installing digital infrastructure in the region.

A report of the committee constituted in July 2026 on the prime minister’s directives was presented during the meeting. It outlined the current status of federal development projects, obstacles to their implementation and measures required to ensure their timely completion. The prime minister reaffirmed that the development of Gilgit-Baltistan, provision of basic facilities to its people and improvement in their living standards remained among the federal government’s priorities.

The meeting also paid tribute to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan, who celebrate November 1 as the historic day marking their liberation from Dogra rule in 1947 and subsequent accession to Pakistan.

The prime minister is expected to visit Gilgit-Baltistan on November 1 to participate in the commemorations.

Gilgit-Baltistan, Chief Minister, Amjad Hussain attended the meeting as a special participant.

Federal Ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Azam Nazeer Tarar, Aleem Khan, Musadik Malik, Attaullah Tarar, Shaza Fatima, Sardar Awais Leghari, Prime Minister’s Advisers Rana Sanaullah and Muhammad Ali, along with senior relevant officials, also attended the meeting.

headline: Cop martyred in Lakki firing; two suspected accused killed in operation
description: PESHAWAR - A police constable was martyred in an armed attack in Lakki Marwat on Friday, while police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel later
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
PESHAWAR - A police constable was martyred in an armed attack in Lakki Marwat on Friday, while police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel later killed two suspected target killers in a retaliatory operation. Police spokesperson said unidentified gunmen opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near MC Bank within the jurisdiction of Shahbazkhel Police Station, leaving him critically injured. He later succumbed to his injuries. Following the attack, police launched a search operation to trace the assailants. The spokesperson said a joint police and CTD team, led by District Police Officer (DPO) Sajjad Ahmad Sahibzada, conducted an operation and killed two suspects allegedly involved in the constable’s murder.

The personnel launched another search operation in the area to trace other suspects linked to the attack. Police said efforts were underway to maintain security and prevent further incidents in the district.

headline: Modern Karakoram Express begins operations under private-sector management
description: LAHORE - Pakistan Railways’ model train, Karakoram Express, equipped with modern travel facilities, has commenced operations under private-sector
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan Railways’ model train, Karakoram Express, equipped with modern travel facilities, has commenced operations under private-sector management. Chief Executive Officer Pakistan Railways Muhammad Hafeezullah, accompanied by directors of M/s Prime Rail, inaugurated the train at Lahore Railway Station on Friday and saw off passengers travelling to Karachi. The private firm, M/s Prime Rail, has announced a 25 per cent discount on fares of all classes until November 6. Comprising 20 coaches, the train offers AC Sleeper, AC Business, AC Standard and Economy classes, along with modern facilities including mineral water, fresh meals, bedding, mobile charging, Wi-Fi and an infotainment system. Complimentary services will also be provided to passengers travelling in AC Sleeper and AC Business classes. Departing simultaneously from Lahore and Karachi at 3:00 pm, the Karakoram Express will stop at Raiwind, Sahiwal, Khanewal, Bahawalpur, Rohri, Nawabshah, Hyderabad, Landhi and Drigh Road stations. The train will cover the distance between Lahore and Karachi in 19 hours. Under the discounted fare structure applicable until November 6, the AC Sleeper fare has been fixed at Rs12,600, AC Business at Rs9,550, AC Standard at Rs7,550 and Economy Class at Rs4,150. Passengers travelling in AC Sleeper and AC Business classes will also be provided complimentary services within the same ticket fare. It may be mentioned that Pakistan Railways has outsourced the commercial management of the Karakoram Express to private firm M/s Prime Rail for an annual amount of Rs3.9015 billion.

headline: Govt steps up capital market reforms to boost corporate debt issuance
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Finance and Revenue Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired the fourth meeting of the Capital Market Development Council (CMDC) at the
author: Imran Ali Kundi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Finance and Revenue Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired the fourth meeting of the Capital Market Development Council (CMDC) at the Finance Division on Friday to review progress on capital market reforms. Discussions focused on deepening Pakistan’s corporate debt market, broadening the issuer and investor base, strengthening market infrastructure and facilitating access to long-term financing.

The council reviewed progress on the reform agenda and implementation of decisions taken at its previous meeting, noting important developments in corporate debt issuance, listing facilitation, secondary-market trading and institutional investor engagement. The finance minister appreciated the progress achieved by the relevant institutions and emphasised the need to build on this momentum through coordinated and time-bound implementation.

The council was informed that corporate debt issuances reached Rs291 billion during January–September 2026, following Rs326 billion raised during 2025, representing a 30 percent increase over 2024. The market has also witnessed 12 new listed corporate debt issuances worth Rs45.4 billion between February 2025 and September 2026, reflecting growing activity in Sukuk and other debt instruments. The council underscored the importance of encouraging more public offerings and enabling a wider range of businesses to access capital market financing.

A key development discussed was the proposed Shariah-compliant Sukuk programme of the National Grid Company of Pakistan Limited (NGC), with an aggregate programme size of up to Rs100 billion and an inaugural issuance of up to Rs20 billion, with a tenor of up to 10 years. The programme is intended to be issued in tranches through public offerings listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), subject to the requisite approvals and market conditions. The finance minister welcomed the initiative as an important opportunity to demonstrate the potential of listed corporate debt instruments and encourage similar issuances by other entities. The council noted progress on measures to simplify and facilitate corporate debt issuance. Dedicated Corporate Debt Market Desks have been established at the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) and PSX to support potential issuers and provide market guidance. The finance minister emphasised the need to enhance awareness and outreach around these facilities to ensure greater utilisation by prospective issuers. The one-window listing mechanism is already operational through SECP and PSX, with simplified listing procedures and related information available online, while work is underway to integrate the Central Depository Company (CDC) into the mechanism to further streamline the listing process.

The meeting reviewed the proposed reform agenda under four thematic working groups covering tax and fiscal matters; debt and issuance; market infrastructure; and investor protection and enforcement. These workstreams aim to address tax-related distortions, streamline issuance and listing procedures, reduce transaction costs, strengthen market liquidity and investor safeguards, and promote greater use of innovative financing instruments, including green and thematic Sukuk.

On secondary-market development, the Council noted a significant improvement in trading activity, with average daily traded value increasing from Rs3.93 billion in FY2026 to over Rs10 billion during FY2027 to date, as of October 15, 2026. Thirteen banks have been onboarded and are actively participating in secondary-market trading arrangements, supported by ongoing engagement among PSX, the Pakistan Banks’ Association (PBA), CDC and the National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited (NCCPL). The finance minister welcomed the improvement in market activity and stressed the importance of sustaining liquidity and broadening participation.

The council also reviewed measures to facilitate banks’ participation in government Sukuk trading through PSX, including existing arrangements permitting banks and other eligible institutions to trade government securities without maintaining broker accounts. Further regulatory and operational considerations relating to Sukuk-based liquidity facilities were also discussed. To broaden the institutional investor base, SECP briefed the council on consultations undertaken with 17 pension fund managers and 44 insurance companies.

The engagement has identified opportunities to improve the availability of suitable debt instruments, secondary-market liquidity, issuer disclosures and the broader investment framework. The council emphasised the importance of translating these consultations into practical measures that encourage greater participation by long-term institutional investors.

The meeting also reviewed outreach to potential corporate issuers, including SMEs, medium-sized and non-blue-chip companies. The finance minister called for greater priority to be given to facilitating SME access to capital market financing, directing SECP to work closely with PSX and other relevant platforms to develop practical solutions. He also encouraged stronger engagement between investment banks, financial advisers, consultants and prospective issuers, with the involvement of the Pakistan Business Council (PBC) and PBA, to build awareness, encourage long-term debt issuance and develop a stronger pipeline of corporate financing transactions.

The finance minister further encouraged SECP and PSX to renew engagement with MSCI to explore Pakistan’s potential future reclassification to Emerging Markets status. Referring to his positive interaction with the MSCI team on the sidelines of the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, earlier this month, he emphasised the importance of sustained dialogue and continued progress on market development and accessibility.

Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb emphasised that the next phase of capital market development must focus on translating regulatory and institutional reforms into increased issuance, deeper liquidity and wider investor participation. He underscored the importance of expanding financing options beyond conventional bank lending, mobilising domestic savings for productive investment and enabling more businesses to access long-term capital.

The finance minister urged all stakeholders to maintain the reform momentum, address remaining bottlenecks and pursue focused engagement with issuers and investors to accelerate the development of a more diversified, efficient and accessible capital market. The meeting was attended by the SECP Chairman, representatives of SBP, PSX, PBA and the Tax Policy Office, alongwith senior officials of the Finance Division.

ISLAMABAD - Federal Finance and Revenue Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired the fourth meeting of the Capital Market Development Council (CMDC) at the Finance Division on Friday to review progress on capital market reforms. Discussions focused on deepening Pakistan’s corporate debt market, broadening the issuer and investor base, strengthening market infrastructure and facilitating access to long-term financing.

The council reviewed progress on the reform agenda and implementation of decisions taken at its previous meeting, noting important developments in corporate debt issuance, listing facilitation, secondary-market trading and institutional investor engagement. The finance minister appreciated the progress achieved by the relevant institutions and emphasised the need to build on this momentum through coordinated and time-bound implementation.

The council was informed that corporate debt issuances reached Rs291 billion during January–September 2026, following Rs326 billion raised during 2025, representing a 30 percent increase over 2024. The market has also witnessed 12 new listed corporate debt issuances worth Rs45.4 billion between February 2025 and September 2026, reflecting growing activity in Sukuk and other debt instruments. The council underscored the importance of encouraging more public offerings and enabling a wider range of businesses to access capital market financing.

A key development discussed was the proposed Shariah-compliant Sukuk programme of the National Grid Company of Pakistan Limited (NGC), with an aggregate programme size of up to Rs100 billion and an inaugural issuance of up to Rs20 billion, with a tenor of up to 10 years. The programme is intended to be issued in tranches through public offerings listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), subject to the requisite approvals and market conditions. The finance minister welcomed the initiative as an important opportunity to demonstrate the potential of listed corporate debt instruments and encourage similar issuances by other entities. The council noted progress on measures to simplify and facilitate corporate debt issuance. Dedicated Corporate Debt Market Desks have been established at the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) and PSX to support potential issuers and provide market guidance. The finance minister emphasised the need to enhance awareness and outreach around these facilities to ensure greater utilisation by prospective issuers. The one-window listing mechanism is already operational through SECP and PSX, with simplified listing procedures and related information available online, while work is underway to integrate the Central Depository Company (CDC) into the mechanism to further streamline the listing process.

The meeting reviewed the proposed reform agenda under four thematic working groups covering tax and fiscal matters; debt and issuance; market infrastructure; and investor protection and enforcement. These workstreams aim to address tax-related distortions, streamline issuance and listing procedures, reduce transaction costs, strengthen market liquidity and investor safeguards, and promote greater use of innovative financing instruments, including green and thematic Sukuk.

On secondary-market development, the Council noted a significant improvement in trading activity, with average daily traded value increasing from Rs3.93 billion in FY2026 to over Rs10 billion during FY2027 to date, as of October 15, 2026. Thirteen banks have been onboarded and are actively participating in secondary-market trading arrangements, supported by ongoing engagement among PSX, the Pakistan Banks’ Association (PBA), CDC and the National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited (NCCPL). The finance minister welcomed the improvement in market activity and stressed the importance of sustaining liquidity and broadening participation.

The council also reviewed measures to facilitate banks’ participation in government Sukuk trading through PSX, including existing arrangements permitting banks and other eligible institutions to trade government securities without maintaining broker accounts. Further regulatory and operational considerations relating to Sukuk-based liquidity facilities were also discussed. To broaden the institutional investor base, SECP briefed the council on consultations undertaken with 17 pension fund managers and 44 insurance companies.

The engagement has identified opportunities to improve the availability of suitable debt instruments, secondary-market liquidity, issuer disclosures and the broader investment framework. The council emphasised the importance of translating these consultations into practical measures that encourage greater participation by long-term institutional investors.

The meeting also reviewed outreach to potential corporate issuers, including SMEs, medium-sized and non-blue-chip companies. The finance minister called for greater priority to be given to facilitating SME access to capital market financing, directing SECP to work closely with PSX and other relevant platforms to develop practical solutions. He also encouraged stronger engagement between investment banks, financial advisers, consultants and prospective issuers, with the involvement of the Pakistan Business Council (PBC) and PBA, to build awareness, encourage long-term debt issuance and develop a stronger pipeline of corporate financing transactions.

The finance minister further encouraged SECP and PSX to renew engagement with MSCI to explore Pakistan’s potential future reclassification to Emerging Markets status. Referring to his positive interaction with the MSCI team on the sidelines of the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, earlier this month, he emphasised the importance of sustained dialogue and continued progress on market development and accessibility.

Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb emphasised that the next phase of capital market development must focus on translating regulatory and institutional reforms into increased issuance, deeper liquidity and wider investor participation. He underscored the importance of expanding financing options beyond conventional bank lending, mobilising domestic savings for productive investment and enabling more businesses to access long-term capital.

The finance minister urged all stakeholders to maintain the reform momentum, address remaining bottlenecks and pursue focused engagement with issuers and investors to accelerate the development of a more diversified, efficient and accessible capital market. The meeting was attended by the SECP Chairman, representatives of SBP, PSX, PBA and the Tax Policy Office, alongwith senior officials of the Finance Division.

headline: SBP injects over Rs1tr to maintain liquidity in market
description: KARACHI - State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), Friday, injected Rs1,075.9 billion through Reverse Repo Purchase and Shariah Compliant Mudarabah based Open Market
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KARACHI - State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), Friday, injected Rs1,075.9 billion through Reverse Repo Purchase and Shariah Compliant Mudarabah based Open Market Operations (OMO) for maintaining liquidity in the market. The central bank conducted the Open Market Operation, Reverse Repo Purchase (Injection) for 7 and 14-day tenors on October 30, 2026, and injected Rs886.15 billion against 17 quotes while other Rs189.75 billion were injected through Shariah Compliant Mudarabah based OMO.

The central bank, for the Reverse Repo Purchase of 14-day tenor, received 14 bids cumulatively offering Rs1,046.8 billion at the rate of return ranging between 12.03 percent to 12.10 percent. The SBP accepted Rs575.05 billion against 12 quotes at 12.05 percent rate of return. The total amount offered at 12.05 percent was Rs530.5 billion, out of which SBP accepted Rs293.85 billion on a pro rata basis. Moreover, the SBP also received 5 bids for the 7-day tenor, cumulatively offering Rs311.1 billion at the rate of return ranging between 12.01 percent to 12.10 percent. The SBP accepted the entire amount against all the 5 quotes at a 12.01 percent rate of return. Meanwhile, SBP also conducted Shariah Compliant Mudarabah-based Open Market Operation for the 7 and 14-day tenors. The central bank received no bid for the 7-day tenor, while 5 quotes were received for the 14-day tenor offering Rs189.75 billion at rate of return ranging between 12.05 percent to 12.06 percent. SBP accepted the entire amount against the 5 bids at 12.05 percent rate of return.

headline: PSX turns bearish, loses over 784 points
description: ISLAMABAD - The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) turned around to a bearish trend on Friday, shedding 784.19 points, a negative
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) turned around to a bearish trend on Friday, shedding 784.19 points, a negative change of 0.47 percent, to close at 166,409.25 points against 167,193.44 points recorded in the previous trading session. The ready market witnessed a trading volume of 825.467 million shares, compared to 816.834 million shares traded in the previous session. The traded value of the ready market reached Rs23.123 billion, down from Rs31.542 billion a day earlier.

Meanwhile, total market capitalisation decreased to Rs18.389 trillion from Rs18.493 trillion recorded in the previous session. Out of 501 companies that traded in the ready market, 173 posted gains, 300 suffered losses, while 28 remained unchanged, reflecting the dominant bearish trend across the market. Pervez Ahmed Co led the volume chart with 165.865 million shares, followed by Cnergyico PK with 111.992 million shares, and F Nat Equities with 40.465 million shares. Among the top gainers in the ready market, Unilever Pakistan Foods Limited surged by Rs428.80 to close at Rs26,280.00, while Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited advanced by Rs104.14 to settle at Rs8,587.46. On the losing side, Pakistan Engineering Company Limited declined by Rs35.70 to close at Rs880.29, while Sazgar Engineering Works Limited fell by Rs33.11 to Rs1,400.25.

In the futures (DFC) market, turnover stood at 738.201 million shares with a traded value of Rs28.522 billion, compared with 520.614 million shares worth Rs23.051 billion in the previous session. Of the 313 companies traded in the DFC market, 70 advanced, 238 declined, and 5 remained unchanged.

headline: Rising inflation poses fresh challenge to govt’s macroeconomic stability claims
description: ISLAMABAD - Despite the government’s tall claims of achieving macroeconomic stability, rising inflation continues to pose a major challenge for the
author: Imran Ali Kundi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Despite the government’s tall claims of achieving macroeconomic stability, rising inflation continues to pose a major challenge for the PML-N-led coalition government, as food and energy prices remain persistently high.

The Government of Pakistan set an official annual inflation target of 8.2 percent for current fiscal year (FY2026–27) in the federal budget. However, it remained almost in the double digit in the so far period (July to October) of the current fiscal year. The Ministry of Finance has already warned that inflation would be in the range of 9.5 to10.5 percent for October 2026, with the subsequent path sensitive to international energy prices, food supplies and base effects.

The official data of Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) showed that the price of high speed diesel has increased to Rs402 per litre in October 2026 from Rs277 per litre in the same month of the previous year showing an increase of 45 percent. The petrol price rose to Rs390 per litre from Rs264 per litre. Similarly, prices of wheat flour, rice and other commodities have shown massive increases in the last few months. The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) in outgoing week had increased the interest rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent amid rising inflationary pressures fuelled by the intensifying Middle East conflict and persistently high global energy prices. The central bank had termed several reasons behind higher inflation outlook including geopolitical tensions, global commodity price volatility, unanticipated adjustments in energy tariffs, further uptick in wheat and allied product prices, and adverse weather conditions.

Meanwhile, the Power Division has also warned that prices of electricity can increase in the months to come, which would fuel the inflation rate in the country. Fuel price adjustments are expected to increase significantly during December, January, and February. Higher prices of liquefied natural gas (LNG), coal, and other fuels are driving up electricity generation costs, while limited domestic gas supplies could create additional challenges for power plants during the winter months.

On the other hand, the government has limited fiscal space to provide massive subsidies on the fuel and food commodities to control the inflation rate. The federal government has announced fuel subsidies for lower income class. However, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has urged the government to phase out the fuel subsidy scheme. “The fuel support scheme should be phased out promptly, given its high cost and broad targeting. Any future fuel support — should oil prices surprise on the upside — should be limited, time bound, targeted using established social assistance programmes, and accommodated within the FY27 budget envelope,” the IMF said after recently concluding talks with the government for Pakistan.

The official data of the PBS showed that inflation is on an increasing side from the last several months. The monthly inflation rate, measured through Consumer Price Indicator (CPI), was recorded at 10.3 percent during September 2026, after touching 11.1 percent in August this year. The inflation rate had only eased in July by reaching 9.2 percent after continuously increasing in previous months, as it recorded at 11.1 percent in June, 11.7 percent in May and 10.9 percent in April.

headline: Cutlery exports increase to $15.576m in 1QFY27 with 16.98pc surge
description: ISLAMABAD - The exports of cutlery witnessed an increase of 16.98 percent during the first quarter of the current fiscal year 2026-27, as against the exports
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The exports of cutlery witnessed an increase of 16.98 percent during the first quarter of the current fiscal year 2026-27, as against the exports of the corresponding quarter of last year. The cutlery exports from the country were recorded at US $15.576 million during July-September 2026-27 against the exports of $13.315 million during July-September 2025-26, according to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS). Meanwhile, on a year-on-year basis, cutlery exports surged by 15.45 percent during the month under review as opposed to the same months last year.

Cutlery exports in September 2026 were recorded at $5.296 million against the exports of $4.587 million in September 2025. On a month-on-month basis, cutlery exports also increased by 1.57 percent during September 2026, in contrast to the exports of $5.214 million in August 2026, the PBS data revealed.

It is pertinent to mention here that the overall exports from the country increased by 10.84 percent during the quarter under review as compared to the previous year, the data revealed. Exports during July-September were recorded at $8.423 billion against $7.599 billion during July-September last year. On the other hand, imports into the country also went up by 13.21 percent, growing from $16.973 billion last year to $19.215 billion this year.

headline: Ogra announces up to 15.27pc increase in Oct RLNG prices
description: ISLAMABAD - The federal government has increased the weighted average sale price of re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) by up to 15.27 percent for October
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The federal government has increased the weighted average sale price of re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) by up to 15.27 percent for October 2026. According to a determination issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the RLNG price for consumers of Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has been increased by $2.17 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), or 15.27 percent, to $18.3959 per MMBtu for October from $14.2233 per MMBtu in September. For consumers of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL), prices have been increased by $2.1296 per MMBtu, or 14 percent, to $17.3259 from $15.1963 MMBtu. The October price calculation was based on two LNG cargoes imported by state-run Pakistan State Oil under its long-term contracts with Qatar. One cargo was priced at 13.37 percent of Brent crude oil and the other at 10.20 percent of Brent. Pakistan LNG Ltd (PLL) did not procure any cargo from the international spot market during the month.

Notably, for the month of September, the government had cut the prices by up to 21.57 percent, easing fuel costs after months of supply disruptions. Qatar remains a key source of LNG for Pakistan under two long-term, Brent-linked contracts with PSO. Supplies had come under pressure after attacks on Qatari energy infrastructure on March 2 prompted QatarEnergy to declare force majeure and suspend some LNG shipments to customers in Europe and Asia, including Pakistan. The return of two Qatari cargoes in October comes as Pakistan continues to manage gas shortages and higher energy demand. RLNG accounts for roughly a fifth of the country’s energy mix and is widely used to supplement declining domestic gas supplies.

ISLAMABAD - The federal government has increased the weighted average sale price of re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) by up to 15.27 percent for October 2026. According to a determination issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the RLNG price for consumers of Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has been increased by $2.17 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), or 15.27 percent, to $18.3959 per MMBtu for October from $14.2233 per MMBtu in September. For consumers of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL), prices have been increased by $2.1296 per MMBtu, or 14 percent, to $17.3259 from $15.1963 MMBtu. The October price calculation was based on two LNG cargoes imported by state-run Pakistan State Oil under its long-term contracts with Qatar. One cargo was priced at 13.37 percent of Brent crude oil and the other at 10.20 percent of Brent. Pakistan LNG Ltd (PLL) did not procure any cargo from the international spot market during the month.

Notably, for the month of September, the government had cut the prices by up to 21.57 percent, easing fuel costs after months of supply disruptions. Qatar remains a key source of LNG for Pakistan under two long-term, Brent-linked contracts with PSO. Supplies had come under pressure after attacks on Qatari energy infrastructure on March 2 prompted QatarEnergy to declare force majeure and suspend some LNG shipments to customers in Europe and Asia, including Pakistan. The return of two Qatari cargoes in October comes as Pakistan continues to manage gas shortages and higher energy demand. RLNG accounts for roughly a fifth of the country’s energy mix and is widely used to supplement declining domestic gas supplies.

headline: Pakistan invites Saudi investment in strategic oil reserves, refinery projects
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has offered Saudi Arabia to set up tax-neutral commercial oil reserves in the country to diversify risks associated with the Strait of
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has offered Saudi Arabia to set up tax-neutral commercial oil reserves in the country to diversify risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz and Bab Al-Mandeb, as both sides pledged to cement strategic cooperation in energy and petroleum sectors. The offer was made by Federal Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik during a meeting with Saudi Arabia’s new Ambassador to Pakistan, Dr Rajeh bin Tami Al-Baqami, to discuss opportunities for strengthening bilateral cooperation in mining, petroleum and energy sectors, including strategic oil storage, refinery upgradation, LPG supplies and facilitation of commercial engagement. The Saudi Ambassador also announced that the Embassy of Saudi Arabia in Islamabad has introduced same day processing of visa applications for Pakistani citizens to facilitate travel and strengthen business, cultural and people to people exchanges.

The Minister welcomed the longstanding strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and conveyed that, during his recent visit to Riyadh, he had conveyed to His Royal Highness Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud the leadership’s special sentiments of solidarity and affection for the Saudi people. He said Pakistan deeply values its historic relationship with Saudi Arabia and remains committed to expanding cooperation across strategic sectors. The Minister informed the ambassador that Pakistan has approved a tax neutral bonded policy, benchmarked against international energy hubs such as Fujairah and Singapore. Under this framework, Saudi companies can establish commercial oil reserves in Pakistan without local tax liabilities, offering an opportunity to diversify maritime transit risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz and Bab Al Mandeb Strait while facilitating access to Asian markets. He highlighted that strategic oil storage facilities in Pakistan would provide Saudi Arabia with greater flexibility in managing supply routes and accessing regional markets.

He further highlighted Pakistan’s plans to develop a major petroleum storage and refining complex at Hub, Balochistan, under guidance of Technip Energies UK. The proposed facility, supported by the Prime Minister and the Chief of Defence Forces, will have the capacity to accommodate Very Large Crude Carriers and strengthen Pakistan’s potential as a regional energy corridor serving Central Asian and Chinese markets.

The minister also highlighted the investment opportunities offered by Pakistan’s ongoing refinery upgradation programme, aimed at modernising domestic refining infrastructure, improving operational efficiency and transitioning towards Euro 5 fuel standards. He said the programme offers significant opportunities for Saudi investment and participation in Pakistan’s refining sector.

Appreciating Saudi Arabia’s support during recent global market disruptions, the minister thanked the Saudi authorities at Yanbu port for prioritising crude oil shipments to Pakistan. He also discussed coordination with Saudi Aramco to explore expanded procurement of crude oil cargoes and dedicated LPG shipments to support Pakistan’s energy requirements, particularly in view of the anticipated increase in domestic gas demand during the winter season.

Both sides underscored that the strong defence and strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia provides a foundation for broader regional peace, stability and economic cooperation. Ambassador Dr Rajeh bin Tami Al-Baqami reiterated Saudi Arabia’s deep appreciation for Pakistan’s longstanding support, stating that the two countries stand together in all circumstances. He emphasised that their defence and energy cooperation frameworks are aimed at promoting peace, stability and economic growth across the region. The minister also invited Saudi Arabia’s Vice Minister of Mining Excellency Khalid al-Mudafier to participate in the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum scheduled to be held in Islamabad on November 12 and 13, highlighting further opportunities for cooperation and investment in Pakistan’s minerals sector.

Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening the longstanding brotherly relationship through enhanced cooperation, investment and mutually beneficial partnerships in the energy and petroleum sectors.
