headline: Empowering SMEs
description: The State Bank of Pakistan’s launch of a dedicated digital portal for Small and Medium Enterprises is a welcome initiative that addresses the chronic
author: The Nation
article_text:
The State Bank of Pakistan’s launch of a dedicated digital portal for Small and Medium Enterprises is a welcome initiative that addresses the chronic friction in the credit acquisition process. By digitising the interface between the central bank and the entrepreneurial class, the state is dismantling the bureaucratic barriers that have historically stifled small-scale growth. Easier access to finance and professional guidance will help small businesses grow, create jobs, and widen opportunity across the national economy.

A fragmented financial ecosystem has long forced small business owners to navigate a labyrinth of paperwork and contradictory requirements. When the process of securing a loan is defined by opacity and administrative delays, the inherent risk of entrepreneurship becomes an unbearable burden. This shift toward a centralised digital gateway suggests a maturation of the banking sector, moving away from a culture of exclusion toward one of accessible, data-driven support.

This systemic upgrade reveals a critical understanding of the SME sector as the primary engine of employment. Relying on traditional, brick-and-mortar banking models is a flawed strategy for a modern economy, as it excludes those without the necessary collateral or political connections. A digital-first approach ensures that credit is allocated based on viability rather than patronage, thereby democratising the opportunity for economic advancement.

Integrating this portal with a broader ecosystem of business incubation and mentorship will prevent the stagnation of new ventures. Maintaining a seamless user experience is the only path toward transforming the SME sector into a resilient pillar of national prosperity.

headline: Apartheid Elections
description: Israel’s latest election has produced a result that complicates the formation of a government without necessarily signalling a departure from the
author: The Nation
article_text:
Israel’s latest election has produced a result that complicates the formation of a government without necessarily signalling a departure from the country’s existing direction. Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc emerged largest, with 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, but fell eight short of a majority. The opposition secured 48 seats, while Arab-led parties won 19, leaving coalition negotiations, and the possibility of another election, ahead.

The arithmetic is significant, but the political questions extend beyond the prime minister’s future. The contest has been framed around Netanyahu; however, treating the country’s conduct in Gaza as the product of one leader alone risks overlooking the wider political forces that have sustained it. A change at the top would not, by itself, establish a change in policy.

Israel’s record in Gaza, and the international scrutiny surrounding its military campaign, cannot be separated from the institutions and political constituencies that have enabled successive decisions. Nor can an election result be treated as a direct referendum on every aspect of that record. Voters choose among parties and competing domestic priorities; the outcome does not offer a simple measure of public consent to each state action.

The more consequential test will therefore lie in what the eventual government does: whether it revises the conduct that has devastated Palestinian life, or preserves the broad direction under a different arrangement of parties. Coalition negotiations may alter the distribution of power in Jerusalem. For Palestinians, the measure of political change will be whether it alters realities on the ground. A new governing combination, on its own, cannot be mistaken for a new national course.

headline: Diplomacy Over Rivalries
description: Pakistan’s engagement with Iran at a moment of mounting regional instability warrants attention beyond the political quarrel it has triggered at home.
author: The Nation
article_text:
Pakistan’s engagement with Iran at a moment of mounting regional instability warrants attention beyond the political quarrel it has triggered at home. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, responding to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s objections over his participation in the Tehran meeting, defended the visit as a special assignment from the prime minister to address the unfolding crisis. He also rejected the suggestion that the gathering concerned a defence agreement, prompting an exchange of personal accusations in the Senate.

The significance of the Tehran discussions lies in the diplomatic opening they represent. Representatives of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye met Iranian leadership to explore regional cooperation and avenues for de-escalation. With tensions threatening to draw neighbouring states into a wider confrontation, maintaining communication across political and strategic divides is a matter of considerable consequence.

Against this backdrop, reducing the initiative to a dispute over ministerial attendance does little to illuminate its purpose. Fazlur Rehman is entitled to question the government’s decisions, just as ministers must account for their responsibilities. Yet criticism carries greater weight when directed at the substance of diplomatic policy rather than the personalities involved.

Support for diplomacy need not entail unquestioning approval of those conducting it. What deserves recognition is the effort to keep regional channels open; what must remain subject to examination is its effectiveness. Political rivalry should neither discredit diplomatic engagement nor shield it from accountability. In a volatile neighbourhood, the consequences of failed dialogue extend well beyond the political fortunes of those arguing over it.

headline: Punjab Assembly session adjourned sine die amid lack of quorum
description: LAHORE - The Punjab Assembly session was adjourned sine die on Friday after the government failed to maintain the required quorum, bringing proceedings
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - The Punjab Assembly session was adjourned sine die on Friday after the government failed to maintain the required quorum, bringing proceedings to an abrupt end without taking up any legislative business scheduled for the day. The session, which had been convened by the government, has been marked by repeated failures to maintain quorum, with the treasury benches unable to ensure the required attendance of lawmakers on successive sittings. The proceedings began two hours and 27 minutes behind schedule, with Deputy Speaker Malik Zaheer Iqbal Channar in the chair. Soon after the commencement of the sitting, opposition MPA Rana Shahbaz pointed out the lack of quorum, prompting the Deputy Speaker to order a five-minute bell to summon lawmakers to the House. However, the required number of members could not be mustered, forcing the chair to adjourn the session sine die. As a result, the day’s agenda remained unaddressed. It included questions relating to the Communications and Works Department, five adjournment motions submitted by lawmakers and a general discussion on the post-budget situation, which was scheduled to continue. The House was also scheduled to consider an extension in the validity of four ordinances, including the Punjab Vagrancy (Amendment) Ordinance 2026. Three bills were also on the agenda for approval, including the Provincial Motor Vehicles (Third Amendment) Bill 2026, the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Public Sector Universities (Second Amendment) Bill 2026. Speaking to the media after the adjournment, Opposition Leader Moin Riaz Qureshi criticised the government for failing to ensure its members’ attendance despite having convened the session.

He said the government had not been able to complete its own quorum on even a single day of the session.

The opposition leader also raised concerns over the alleged treatment of women political workers and legislators, claiming that around 1,400 party workers had been arrested and the houses of eight to 10 MPAs raided, with some properties damaged.

He said the opposition had raised the issue in the Assembly’s advisory committee, urging the government to ensure that women were treated with dignity, irrespective of its political differences with male opposition members.

Qureshi also expressed concern over the condition of Noreen Khan, claiming that she had been taken to hospital the previous night but had not received the treatment recommended by doctors. He further alleged that her family was not being allowed to meet her. He said the opposition had protested both inside and outside the Assembly against what he described as the treatment of women.

The opposition leader also raised concerns over the alleged treatment of women political workers and legislators, claiming that around 1,400 party workers had been arrested and the houses of eight to 10 MPAs raided, with some properties damaged.

He said the opposition had raised the issue in the Assembly’s advisory committee, urging the government to ensure that women were treated with dignity, irrespective of its political differences with male opposition members.

Qureshi also expressed concern over the condition of Noreen Khan, claiming that she had been taken to hospital the previous night but had not received the treatment recommended by doctors. He further alleged that her family was not being allowed to meet her. He said the opposition had protested both inside and outside the Assembly against what he described as the treatment of women.

headline: Kundi directs to include regional languages in Star Talent Hunt Programme
description: Peshawar - Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday directed the inclusion of all languages spoken in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Urdu and Saraiki,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday directed the inclusion of all languages spoken in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Urdu and Saraiki, in the Khyber Star Talent Hunt Programme to ensure equal representation and promote the province’s rich cultural diversity.

He issued the directives while chairing a meeting on the proposed Khyber Star Talent Hunt and Cultural Promotion Programme. Adviser to the Governor on Information and Public Relations Samar Haroon Bilour, Secretary Information Muhammad Bakhtiar Khan, Secretary Sports Muhammad Asif and officials from the relevant departments attended the meeting.

The participants were given a detailed briefing on the programme’s objectives, implementation mechanism, selection process and other related aspects.

Officials informed the meeting that the initiative aimed to identify and promote the talent of young people while highlighting the culture, traditions and diverse languages of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. They said audition camps would be established in different districts across the province, while a committee comprising representatives of relevant departments would be formed to ensure transparency and maintain high standards throughout the selection process.

Speaking on the occasion, Governor Kundi directed that all regional languages, including Urdu and Saraiki, be represented in the auditions. He said Saraiki was widely spoken in parts of Sindh, Dera Ismail Khan and Punjab and, therefore, deserved representation in the programme.

The Governor said the youth of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa possessed immense talent and potential that needed to be showcased to the world. He stressed that providing young people with positive and constructive opportunities, along with an effective platform to express their abilities, was the need of the hour.

He added that the Khyber Star Talent Hunt Programme would encourage emerging talent and help preserve, promote and showcase the province’s rich cultural heritage.

headline: Protesters demand justice over youth’s death in alleged police firing
description: Khyber - A protest erupted in Bara on Friday following the alleged killing of a young man in police firing, with protesters placing his body on the
author: Ahmad Nabi
article_text:
Khyber - A protest erupted in Bara on Friday following the alleged killing of a young man in police firing, with protesters placing his body on the road at Khyber Chowk and demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible for the incident.

The youth, identified as Tariq Afridi, was allegedly shot dead during a police operation in the Shalobar area of Tehsil Bara on Thursday night. A minor girl and a woman also sustained bullet injuries in the incident and were shifted to a hospital for medical treatment, according to local residents.

The deceased’s father, Subedar Major (retd) Rasool Shah, who said he had served in the Frontier Force/Frontier Corps for 30 years, accused the police of killing his son inside their house in front of his wife and daughter, claiming that he had committed no crime warranting such action.

Expressing profound grief over his son’s death, Rasool Shah condemned the incident as an act of injustice and brutality and demanded an impartial investigation and accountability. Questioning the circumstances surrounding the killing, he said that if his son had been wanted in any criminal case, the police should have arrested him in accordance with the law rather than resorting to lethal force.

Following the incident, protesters and members of the bereaved family gathered at Khyber Chowk, where they placed the deceased’s body on the road as a mark of protest. They announced that they would continue the sit-in and keep the body at the protest site until justice was secured for the deceased.

The Anjuman-e-Tajeran, Bara Bazaar, also condemned what it described as police brutality and expressed solidarity with the bereaved family. The traders’ association president, Said Ayaz Wazir, assured the family of the business community’s full support and said traders would extend every possible assistance in their efforts to secure justice. He warned that traders could suspend business activities if necessary to press for accountability.

Meanwhile, a statement issued by the office of the Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) said that Tariq Afridi was wanted by the police in three robbery cases, registered under FIR numbers 661, 873 and 858 at Sarband Police Station. According to the statement, a police team had raided his house to arrest him when he allegedly opened fire on the personnel, prompting retaliatory firing in which he was killed.

Later, while presenting their demands to a jirga constituted to mediate in the matter, the protesters and members of the bereaved family called for the withdrawal of the CCPO’s statement. They also demanded that the District Police Officer (DPO), Khyber, visit the bereaved family and offer Nanawatai in accordance with Pakhtun traditions. The family further demanded the registration of a case against the Sarband police personnel involved in the operation, payment of compensation in the form of diyat, and an assurance from the police that they would bear the medical expenses of the two injured persons.

It may be recalled that, in a previous incident, the Khyber police were accused of killing two young men from Jamrud in an alleged staged encounter in the Mullagori area. The incident had triggered widespread protests by members of the Koki Khel tribe.

The matter was subsequently resolved through a jirga, following which the police reportedly apologised and paid compensation to the bereaved families.

headline: KP CS directs early completion of tourism projects in Galiyat
description: Peshawar - Chief Secretary Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Dr Fakhre Alam Irfan, chaired an important meeting to review development, regulation and
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Chief Secretary Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Dr Fakhre Alam Irfan, chaired an important meeting to review development, regulation and environmental protection in Galiyat, one of the province’s major tourist destinations. The meeting was attended by the Secretary Tourism, Commissioner Hazara Division, Director General of the Galiyat Development Authority (GDA) and other relevant officials.

During the meeting, matters relating to building control, by-laws and their enforcement were discussed in detail. The Chief Secretary reiterated that environmental standards and the protection of Galiyat’s natural ecology must be ensured. He also directed that the GDA’s Master Plan and Land Use Plan be given priority.

The Chief Secretary directed the concerned authorities to expedite development work on walking tracks, beautification projects, sanitation units, washrooms and parking facilities and ensure their completion before the start of the next tourist season to facilitate visitors and promote tourism in the region.

He further emphasised the need for focused attention on solid waste management in Galiyat and directed the authorities to complete the wastewater collection and treatment system at the earliest.

headline: Mardan cantonment board launches campaign against stray dogs
description: Mardan - The Mardan Cantonment Board has launched a campaign against stray dogs following growing public complaints about their increasing presence
author: Riaz Khan
article_text:
Mardan - The Mardan Cantonment Board has launched a campaign against stray dogs following growing public complaints about their increasing presence in residential and public areas and the risks they pose to residents, particularly children, worshippers and school-going pupils. Dozens of stray dogs have reportedly been culled during the operation.

According to cantonment board officials, the campaign involves the use of poisoned bait, with the board’s dog removal team carrying out targeted operations in areas surrounding mosques, schools, hospitals and other public facilities. The action was initiated following repeated complaints from residents about the nuisance and potential dangers posed by stray dogs.

Dr Raza Shah, Chief Executive Officer of the Cantonment Board, briefed journalists on the operation, saying that a special team had been deployed to remove stray dogs from different localities within the cantonment limits.

He said the team had prioritised areas where the presence of stray dogs was disrupting residents’ daily routines and increasing the risk of dog attacks. Worshippers travelling to mosques for prayers, schoolchildren and patients visiting hospitals were among those facing difficulties and potential danger from the animals, he added.

Dr Raza said persistent complaints from residents had prompted the Cantonment Board to take immediate action. He observed that stray dogs had become a source of concern for people of all age groups, particularly children and elderly residents.

The problem was especially pronounced during the morning and evening hours, when schoolchildren and worshippers were more likely to encounter the animals.

Consequently, the board mobilised its dog removal unit and launched a sustained operation, during which dozens of stray dogs were culled using poisoned bait.

The CEO said the Cantonment Board was committed to fulfilling its responsibility to provide residents with a safe and clean environment. He maintained that action against stray dogs was not a one-off exercise, as the board conducted such campaigns periodically in response to public complaints and emerging needs.

He added that the operations would continue across the cantonment area to enable residents to move around without fear, particularly in the vicinity of mosques, educational institutions, hospitals and residential neighbourhoods.

Meanwhile, residents have welcomed the board’s action, urging the authorities to maintain the campaign on a regular basis to protect vulnerable members of society, particularly children, women, elderly people and worshippers, from the potential dangers posed by stray dogs.

headline: One killed, 17 injured as school jeep plunges into ravine in Shangla
description: Shangla - A school transport jeep carrying students of The Smart School, Bely Baba Campus, plunged into a deep ravine in Shangla on Friday
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
Shangla - A school transport jeep carrying students of The Smart School, Bely Baba Campus, plunged into a deep ravine in Shangla on Friday afternoon, killing a third-grade pupil and injuring 17 others, including a girl. Several of the injured children were reported to be in critical condition.

The deceased was identified as Niaz Ali, son of Arjab Shah, a Class III student, who died at the scene. His brother Ali, who was also travelling in the vehicle, was among the injured, adding to the family’s grief.

According to local residents and police sources, the accident occurred when the students were returning home from school in a local jeep used for transport in the mountainous and remote areas of Shangla. The children were travelling to their respective villages in the upper reaches of the district when the vehicle reportedly went out of control while negotiating a sharp turn on a steep slope.

The jeep skidded off the road and plunged into a deep ravine, overturning several times before coming to rest at the bottom. The impact left the vehicle badly damaged, trapping several children beneath the wreckage and prompting desperate cries for help. The noise of the crash and the children’s cries alerted nearby residents, who rushed to the scene.

Local residents and volunteers launched an immediate rescue operation without waiting for official emergency teams to arrive. Despite the difficult mountainous terrain and the depth of the ravine, they risked their lives to pull the injured children from the wreckage. After providing initial assistance at the scene, they carried the injured on cots and their shoulders to the road, from where they were transported to hospital.

All the injured children were initially shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital in Alpuri, where emergency arrangements were made and doctors and paramedical staff provided them with medical assistance. Hospital sources said several children had sustained multiple injuries, including fractures and head injuries, as a result of the fall.

Given the severity of their injuries, several children were referred to Saidu Sharif Teaching Hospital in Swat for specialised treatment following initial medical care. Their treatment was continuing at the hospital at the time of filing this report, with doctors describing the condition of some of the injured as critical.

The death of Niaz Ali and the injuries sustained by his brother have left the family devastated. His funeral prayer was offered in his native village and attended by a large number of relatives, local elders, teachers, fellow students and residents from different walks of life. He was subsequently laid to rest in the local graveyard.

The accident has once again raised serious concerns about the safety of schoolchildren travelling in public and privately operated vehicles in the mountainous areas of Shangla. Local residents and parents expressed concern that young pupils were frequently transported in open jeeps along steep, narrow and poorly maintained roads, often without adequate safety arrangements.

They said several private schools in the district lacked proper transport facilities of their own, leaving children dependent on privately operated local jeeps, which were often overcrowded and, in some cases, mechanically unfit.

Meanwhile, police and the local administration have initiated an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. Police officials said preliminary findings pointed to possible overloading, brake failure and the poor condition of the road as contributing factors. They added that a detailed inquiry would establish the exact cause of the accident and determine responsibility, with action to be taken against anyone found negligent.

headline: New superintendent appointed at Bisham Sub-Jail
description: Shangla - Ikram Ullah Khan has assumed charge as Superintendent of Bisham Sub-Jail, prompting felicitations and expressions of goodwill from
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Shangla - Ikram Ullah Khan has assumed charge as Superintendent of Bisham Sub-Jail, prompting felicitations and expressions of goodwill from members of the local community, social circles and journalists.

Various sections of society have expressed hope that he will use his professional experience, administrative capabilities and leadership skills to improve the jail’s management, maintain discipline and ensure the protection of prisoners’ legal rights.

They described his appointment as an important responsibility, expressing the expectation that he would take practical measures to ensure the institution’s administration remained in accordance with the law and prescribed rules. They also emphasised the need for appropriate treatment of prisoners, attention to their basic needs and resolution of their legitimate concerns.

Congratulating Khan on assuming his new responsibilities, members of different circles observed that the role of jail administration extended beyond the supervision and security of inmates. They said respect for human dignity, observance of legal provisions, prisoners’ rehabilitation and access to lawful facilities were equally important aspects of prison management.

They stressed that maintaining discipline in correctional facilities must go hand in hand with ensuring prisoners’ health, hygiene, food and other basic necessities. Providing inmates with opportunities to exercise their legal rights, consult lawyers and maintain contact with their families in accordance with applicable rules was also an essential responsibility of the jail administration, they added.

The community representatives expressed hope that special attention would be given to these matters at Bisham Sub-Jail and that an effective strategy would be developed to improve its administrative arrangements.

They further expected the new superintendent to work in close coordination with jail staff to strengthen the institution’s administrative structure while maintaining the required standards of security and discipline. They said legitimate complaints and problems faced by prisoners should be addressed through transparent procedures and in accordance with the law.

They also observed that an accountable administrative system, effective discharge of official responsibilities and a proper mechanism for addressing complaints could contribute significantly to improving the institution’s overall performance.

Expressing their best wishes for Khan, the local representatives hoped that he would discharge his responsibilities with professionalism, integrity and a spirit of public service, while promoting the rule of law, protecting prisoners’ rights and improving the administration of Bisham Sub-Jail.

headline: KP orders probe into fatal school jeep accident in Shangla
description: Peshawar - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser for Information and Public Relations Samar Haroon Bilour has expressed profound grief over the death of a
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser for Information and Public Relations Samar Haroon Bilour has expressed profound grief over the death of a child in a jeep accident involving schoolchildren in Shangla, calling for a thorough investigation and a comprehensive review of safety arrangements for vehicles used to transport pupils. In a statement issued here on Friday, Ms Bilour extended her heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family and expressed solidarity with them over their loss. She prayed for eternal peace for the deceased child and strength and patience for the family to endure the tragedy.

She also prayed for the speedy and complete recovery of the injured children and directed the relevant authorities to ensure that they received the best possible medical treatment and facilities. Emphasising the importance of children’s safety, she said their lives could not be put at risk under any circumstances.

The adviser called for a thorough investigation into all aspects of the accident, stressing that anyone found responsible for negligence or lapses, at any level, would be held accountable.

She said the fitness, mechanical condition and safety arrangements of vehicles used for school transport would be comprehensively reviewed. The use of old, dilapidated and unroadworthy vehicles for transporting schoolchildren, she stressed, must be strictly prohibited.

Ms Bilour further said the relevant departments would be directed to conduct regular inspections of school transport vehicles and ensure strict compliance with prescribed safety standards.

“Ensuring safe transportation for children to and from educational institutions is our fundamental responsibility,” she said, adding that effective and practical measures would be introduced to prevent similar tragedies in the future.

Reiterating the government’s commitment to children’s welfare, she said protecting their lives, ensuring their safety and providing them with a secure educational environment remained among its top priorities.

headline: UoM holds plantation drive, environmental awareness walk
description: PESHAWAR - The University of Malakand (UoM) organised an environmental awareness walk and plantation drive at its Botanical Garden to promote
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
PESHAWAR - The University of Malakand (UoM) organised an environmental awareness walk and plantation drive at its Botanical Garden to promote environmental conservation and encourage young people to contribute to a greener and more sustainable future.

Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Muhammad Idrees attended the event as chief guest and led the awareness walk. As part of the initiative, 500 seed balls were dispersed across the university’s hilly areas, while 100 saplings were planted at the Botanical Garden to promote vegetation and environmental sustainability on the campus.

Pro-Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Mir Azam, Director of the Botanical Garden Prof Dr Nisar, Focal Person of the Green Youth Movement Ayub Khan, faculty members, administrative officers and a large number of students participated in the activities.

The initiative aimed to raise environmental awareness among students, encourage plantation and promote collective efforts to protect the natural environment for future generations.

The participants also highlighted the importance of engaging young people in addressing environmental challenges and supporting sustainable development.

The event was organised by the Green Youth Movement (GYM) Club, an integral part of the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme, in collaboration with the Youth Development Centre and the Directorate of Botanical Garden and Herbarium, University of Malakand.

The event was organised by the Green Youth Movement (GYM) Club, an integral part of the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme, in collaboration with the Youth Development Centre and the Directorate of Botanical Garden and Herbarium, University of Malakand.

headline: Pak-China Friendship Hospital: A New Hope for Free and Quality Healthcare
description: Karram Elahi Wazir googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-1681982472501-0'); }); Access to quality
author: Karram Elahi Wazir
article_text:
Karram Elahi Wazir

Access to quality healthcare should never depend on a person’s financial circumstances. For thousands of families across Pakistan, however, the cost of medical treatment remains a major source of anxiety, often forcing them to delay essential care or rely on limited resources to meet mounting medical expenses. The restoration and operationalisation of the Pak-China Friendship Hospital in Islamabad represents an important step towards addressing this challenge and ensuring that financial hardship does not deprive citizens of their fundamental right to healthcare.

Inaugurated by Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, the 182-bed facility is intended to provide comprehensive medical services entirely free of charge. Its operationalisation reflects the government’s commitment to improving access to healthcare, particularly for low-income and underserved communities. Patients from Islamabad and Rawalpindi, as well as those travelling from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the country, are expected to benefit from its facilities.

What distinguishes this initiative is not merely the establishment of another hospital, but the opportunity it creates to connect vulnerable citizens with modern medical services without imposing an unbearable financial burden on them. With round-the-clock emergency care, surgical facilities, paediatric services, diagnostic support and intensive care arrangements, the hospital can become a significant addition to the country’s public healthcare infrastructure.

The Prime Minister has directed that patients receive 100 per cent free treatment, with the government bearing the costs of medicines, medical procedures and other essential requirements. This directive carries a broader message: the ability to pay should not determine whether a patient receives timely and appropriate medical attention. The real success of the initiative will ultimately be measured by how effectively this commitment is translated into practical relief for ordinary citizens.

Pakistan’s healthcare system continues to face considerable challenges. Overcrowding, limited resources and gaps in service delivery at some government hospitals frequently compel patients to turn to private healthcare providers, where treatment costs can be beyond the reach of low-income households. For families already struggling with inflation and other financial pressures, a serious illness can become an economic crisis. In these circumstances, strengthening public hospitals and expanding access to free treatment are essential components of a people-centred welfare policy.

The revival of the Pak-China Friendship Hospital also highlights the importance of ensuring that existing public assets are used efficiently. The facility was gifted to Pakistan by China during the COVID-19 pandemic but remained non-functional for several years. After taking notice of a newspaper report concerning its prolonged closure, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed Federal Minister for Health Syed Mustafa Kamal to take immediate measures to restore and operationalise the hospital.

The Prime Minister also conveyed an apology to the Chinese government and people, through Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, over the delay in making the facility operational. His decision to order a third-party audit of the hospital’s medical facilities, treatment standards and administrative performance further underlines the need for transparency, accountability and effective management of public healthcare institutions.

The episode offers an important lesson for policymakers: constructing infrastructure is only the first step. Public investment achieves its true purpose when facilities become functional, professional services are consistently available, and citizens can benefit from the resources allocated for their welfare. Preventing similar delays in the future should be a priority for all relevant departments.

The hospital’s restoration has also renewed attention on the longstanding partnership between Pakistan and China. The project stands as a practical expression of bilateral cooperation, demonstrating how friendly relations can translate into initiatives that directly benefit ordinary people.

China contributed US$4 million towards the project, while the total construction cost was approximately Rs. 980 million.

The hospital building was constructed in 2020 by the Frontier Works Organization, with support from the National Disaster Management Authority and the National Institute of Health. Its name recognises the enduring friendship between the two countries and China’s financial contribution to the initiative. The participation of Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong in the inauguration ceremony further highlighted the significance attached to the project by both countries.

Beyond the immediate healthcare benefits, the initiative reinforces the broader spirit of the Pakistan-China relationship. As the two countries pursue further cooperation under the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, opportunities to expand collaboration in social development, healthcare, technology and other public welfare sectors deserve particular attention. Economic partnerships become more meaningful when their benefits reach communities and improve people’s everyday lives.

Effective management will be central to the hospital’s long-term success. The facility will be operated through a partnership between the Government of Pakistan and Indus Hospital and Health Network (IHHN), an organisation with an established healthcare service network across the country. Its experience in delivering medical services can contribute to the efficient utilisation of resources, improved patient care and the development of sustainable operational arrangements.

According to the information shared at the inauguration ceremony, Indus Hospital and Health Network operates 15 hospitals, 140 primary healthcare centres, four blood centres and four rehabilitation centres across Pakistan. Its network serves approximately 700,000 patients every month. Such experience provides a valuable foundation for managing the Pak-China Friendship Hospital and ensuring that its facilities remain accessible to those who need them most.

Nevertheless, the provision of free treatment must be supported by adequate staffing, the timely availability of medicines, modern diagnostic equipment, reliable emergency services and effective administrative oversight. Transparent monitoring and regular performance assessments will be essential to maintaining standards and building public confidence. The proposed third-party audit can serve as an important mechanism for identifying weaknesses and ensuring that the hospital delivers on its intended objectives.

During the inauguration ceremony, the Federal Minister for Health also informed participants that a 200-bed cancer hospital at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences had been completed and was expected to become operational the following year. The development points to the potential for expanding specialised healthcare services and addressing critical gaps in treatment facilities. Once operational, such institutions could further strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to complex and costly medical needs.

The Pak-China Friendship Hospital should, therefore, be viewed as part of a broader effort to improve healthcare access rather than as an isolated achievement. Pakistan needs more hospitals capable of providing quality treatment without imposing financial hardship on patients. Particular attention should be given to underserved districts, remote communities and regions where people must travel long distances to access specialist care.

The establishment of similar facilities elsewhere would require stronger coordination between the federal and provincial governments, particularly in planning, financing, infrastructure development and service delivery. Following the 18th Constitutional Amendment, health has primarily become a provincial responsibility. However, this constitutional arrangement does not diminish the importance of intergovernmental cooperation in addressing national healthcare challenges.

A coordinated approach could help mobilise resources, improve the utilisation of existing facilities, reduce delays in fund releases and encourage partnerships with experienced healthcare organisations. The federal government and provincial administrations can also exchange expertise and develop practical models for delivering affordable, accessible and quality medical services.

Ultimately, the true value of the Pak-China Friendship Hospital will lie in the lives it improves, the families it supports and the patients it treats without discrimination. Its restoration offers an opportunity to demonstrate that public institutions can deliver meaningful relief when political commitment is matched by efficient administration, transparency and sustained investment.

The government must now ensure that the hospital operates to its full potential and that the promise of completely free treatment remains a practical reality for every eligible patient. At the same time, the experience gained from this initiative should be used to develop similar healthcare facilities across the country.

A nation’s progress cannot be measured solely through economic indicators, infrastructure projects or international partnerships. It must also be judged by the quality of life enjoyed by its people and the support available to those facing illness and hardship. By making quality healthcare accessible regardless of financial means, Pakistan can move closer to a system in which treatment is determined by medical need rather than the ability to pay. The Pak-China Friendship Hospital offers a promising step in that direction.

Patients from Islamabad and Rawalpindi, as well as those travelling from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the country, are expected to benefit from its facilities.

What distinguishes this initiative is not merely the establishment of another hospital, but the opportunity it creates to connect vulnerable citizens with modern medical services without imposing an unbearable financial burden on them. With round-the-clock emergency care, surgical facilities, paediatric services, diagnostic support and intensive care arrangements, the hospital can become a significant addition to the country’s public healthcare infrastructure.

The Prime Minister has directed that patients receive 100 per cent free treatment, with the government bearing the costs of medicines, medical procedures and other essential requirements. This directive carries a broader message: the ability to pay should not determine whether a patient receives timely and appropriate medical attention. The real success of the initiative will ultimately be measured by how effectively this commitment is translated into practical relief for ordinary citizens.

Pakistan’s healthcare system continues to face considerable challenges. Overcrowding, limited resources and gaps in service delivery at some government hospitals frequently compel patients to turn to private healthcare providers, where treatment costs can be beyond the reach of low-income households. For families already struggling with inflation and other financial pressures, a serious illness can become an economic crisis. In these circumstances, strengthening public hospitals and expanding access to free treatment are essential components of a people-centred welfare policy.

The revival of the Pak-China Friendship Hospital also highlights the importance of ensuring that existing public assets are used efficiently. The facility was gifted to Pakistan by China during the COVID-19 pandemic but remained non-functional for several years. After taking notice of a newspaper report concerning its prolonged closure, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed Federal Minister for Health Syed Mustafa Kamal to take immediate measures to restore and operationalise the hospital.

The Prime Minister also conveyed an apology to the Chinese government and people, through Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, over the delay in making the facility operational. His decision to order a third-party audit of the hospital’s medical facilities, treatment standards and administrative performance further underlines the need for transparency, accountability and effective management of public healthcare institutions.

The episode offers an important lesson for policymakers: constructing infrastructure is only the first step. Public investment achieves its true purpose when facilities become functional, professional services are consistently available, and citizens can benefit from the resources allocated for their welfare. Preventing similar delays in the future should be a priority for all relevant departments.

The hospital’s restoration has also renewed attention on the longstanding partnership between Pakistan and China. The project stands as a practical expression of bilateral cooperation, demonstrating how friendly relations can translate into initiatives that directly benefit ordinary people.

China contributed US$4 million towards the project, while the total construction cost was approximately Rs. 980 million.

The hospital building was constructed in 2020 by the Frontier Works Organization, with support from the National Disaster Management Authority and the National Institute of Health. Its name recognises the enduring friendship between the two countries and China’s financial contribution to the initiative. The participation of Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong in the inauguration ceremony further highlighted the significance attached to the project by both countries.

Beyond the immediate healthcare benefits, the initiative reinforces the broader spirit of the Pakistan-China relationship. As the two countries pursue further cooperation under the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, opportunities to expand collaboration in social development, healthcare, technology and other public welfare sectors deserve particular attention. Economic partnerships become more meaningful when their benefits reach communities and improve people’s everyday lives.

Effective management will be central to the hospital’s long-term success. The facility will be operated through a partnership between the Government of Pakistan and Indus Hospital and Health Network (IHHN), an organisation with an established healthcare service network across the country. Its experience in delivering medical services can contribute to the efficient utilisation of resources, improved patient care and the development of sustainable operational arrangements.

According to the information shared at the inauguration ceremony, Indus Hospital and Health Network operates 15 hospitals, 140 primary healthcare centres, four blood centres and four rehabilitation centres across Pakistan. Its network serves approximately 700,000 patients every month. Such experience provides a valuable foundation for managing the Pak-China Friendship Hospital and ensuring that its facilities remain accessible to those who need them most.

Nevertheless, the provision of free treatment must be supported by adequate staffing, the timely availability of medicines, modern diagnostic equipment, reliable emergency services and effective administrative oversight. Transparent monitoring and regular performance assessments will be essential to maintaining standards and building public confidence. The proposed third-party audit can serve as an important mechanism for identifying weaknesses and ensuring that the hospital delivers on its intended objectives.

During the inauguration ceremony, the Federal Minister for Health also informed participants that a 200-bed cancer hospital at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences had been completed and was expected to become operational the following year. The development points to the potential for expanding specialised healthcare services and addressing critical gaps in treatment facilities. Once operational, such institutions could further strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to complex and costly medical needs.

The Pak-China Friendship Hospital should, therefore, be viewed as part of a broader effort to improve healthcare access rather than as an isolated achievement. Pakistan needs more hospitals capable of providing quality treatment without imposing financial hardship on patients. Particular attention should be given to underserved districts, remote communities and regions where people must travel long distances to access specialist care.

The establishment of similar facilities elsewhere would require stronger coordination between the federal and provincial governments, particularly in planning, financing, infrastructure development and service delivery. Following the 18th Constitutional Amendment, health has primarily become a provincial responsibility. However, this constitutional arrangement does not diminish the importance of intergovernmental cooperation in addressing national healthcare challenges.

A coordinated approach could help mobilise resources, improve the utilisation of existing facilities, reduce delays in fund releases and encourage partnerships with experienced healthcare organisations. The federal government and provincial administrations can also exchange expertise and develop practical models for delivering affordable, accessible and quality medical services.

Ultimately, the true value of the Pak-China Friendship Hospital will lie in the lives it improves, the families it supports and the patients it treats without discrimination. Its restoration offers an opportunity to demonstrate that public institutions can deliver meaningful relief when political commitment is matched by efficient administration, transparency and sustained investment.

The government must now ensure that the hospital operates to its full potential and that the promise of completely free treatment remains a practical reality for every eligible patient. At the same time, the experience gained from this initiative should be used to develop similar healthcare facilities across the country.

A nation’s progress cannot be measured solely through economic indicators, infrastructure projects or international partnerships. It must also be judged by the quality of life enjoyed by its people and the support available to those facing illness and hardship. By making quality healthcare accessible regardless of financial means, Pakistan can move closer to a system in which treatment is determined by medical need rather than the ability to pay. The Pak-China Friendship Hospital offers a promising step in that direction.

headline: Designated rickshaw stands established at Taxila Chowk to ease traffic congestion
description: Wah cantt - The local administration has established designated rickshaw stands on both sides of Taxila Chowk to improve traffic flow and ease
author: APP
article_text:
Wah cantt - The local administration has established designated rickshaw stands on both sides of Taxila Chowk to improve traffic flow and ease congestion at the busy intersection.

Assistant Commissioner Taxila Dr Muhammad Anas Saeed directed the establishment of the stands to prevent indiscriminate parking of rickshaws and ensure smooth movement of traffic here on Friday.

Traffic wardens have been instructed to ensure compliance with the designated parking arrangements and keep roads clear of unnecessary parking. Dr Saeed said maintaining smooth traffic flow, facilitating commuters and addressing congestion were among the administration’s priorities.

The measures aim to reduce roadside obstructions and facilitate motorists and other road users.

Traffic wardens will ensure compliance, keep roads clear and facilitate commuters.

headline: Pakistan to end foreign funding for vaccine procurement by 2030: Minister
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for National Health Syed Mustafa Kamal told the National Assembly that Pakistan will completely phase out
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for National Health Syed Mustafa Kamal told the National Assembly that Pakistan will completely phase out foreign financial assistance for vaccine procurement by 2030, and a barcode system to curb fake medicines will be enforced across the country by end of November.

Responding to questions during Question Hour on Friday, the minister said Pakistan provides vaccines for 13 preventable diseases and all are currently imported. At present, federal and provincial governments bear 51 percent of the total cost, while international partners provide 49 percent. He said by 2030 Pakistan will have to bear 100 percent of vaccine procurement costs, estimated at around $1.2 billion annually.

The government has already started work on self-reliance in local vaccine manufacturing so that all 13 vaccines can be produced domestically and save foreign exchange.

The minister clarified that foreign assistance constituted less than 3 percent of Pakistan’s overall health sector spending. Global Fund supports HIV, malaria and TB elimination programs, but funds were not given directly to the government and are implemented through two private NGOs in Pakistan.

headline: Dr Aamer reviews KP Private Schools Act amendments
description: Peshawar - Member of the Advisory Council for Education Dr Aamer Abdullah on Friday chaired a meeting to review proposed amendments to the Khyber
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Member of the Advisory Council for Education Dr Aamer Abdullah on Friday chaired a meeting to review proposed amendments to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Private Schools Regulatory Authority Act, 2017, with a focus on strengthening the regulatory framework and improving its implementation.

The meeting considered various proposals aimed at strengthening the provisions of the Act, streamlining its implementation mechanism and enhancing the regulation of private educational institutions across the province.

Secretary Elementary and Secondary Education Inayatullah Waseem, Managing Director of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Private Schools Regulatory Authority Javed Iqbal and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

Various provisions of the Act were examined in detail, with discussions covering their legal, administrative and regulatory implications. Particular attention was given to proposed amendments to different sections of the law, the functioning of the Appellate Tribunal, penalties for violations, and the rules and regulations governing private educational institutions.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Aamer said the proposed amendments should make the legislation more effective, comprehensive and practical to implement. He emphasised the need for a stronger regulatory and monitoring framework for private educational institutions while ensuring children’s access to quality education and a safe and conducive learning environment.

He stressed that the proposed amendments and regulations should also safeguard children’s educational interests and incorporate appropriate space standards for educational institutions. He offered suggestions for improving various provisions of the Act and underscored the importance of ensuring their effective implementation and enforcement.

Dr Aamer directed the relevant officials to finalise the draft amendments and submit them to the Law Department by Tuesday for further legal scrutiny and proceedings.

headline: COMSATS Lahore signs accord to strengthen Pak-China industrial ties
description: ISLAMABAD - COMSATS University Islamabad’s Lahore campus has signed an agreement of intent for cooperation with Everest International Expo
author: INP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - COMSATS University Islamabad’s Lahore campus has signed an agreement of intent for cooperation with Everest International Expo (Pvt) Ltd, the Pakistan-based operating entity of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), to strengthen Pakistan-China industrial cooperation and promote closer links between academia and industry. The university said that the partnership would focus on industry and artificial intelligence (AI), agriculture, automotive supply chains, technology transfer, biopharmaceuticals, and research and development.

The collaboration aims to promote joint research and publications, industry-driven innovation, AI-based solutions, and enterprise surveys.

It will also create opportunities for students and faculty members to engage with Chinese enterprises, investors, and international business networks, according to the university.

The initiative seeks to bridge the gap between academic expertise and industrial needs, encourage applied research, provide students with practical experience, and support technological innovation and economic development.

Through this partnership, COMSATS Lahore and Everest International Expo aim to expand knowledge exchange and create opportunities for sustained cooperation between Pakistani and Chinese academic and industrial stakeholders, Gwadar Pro reported on Friday.

headline: KP govt announces reforms to improve governance, public services
description: Peshawar - Adviser Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Samar Haroon Bilour, has said that comprehensive measures are underway
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Samar Haroon Bilour, has said that comprehensive measures are underway to introduce institutional reforms, improve governance, ensure transparency and strengthen public service delivery under the vision of a “Changing, Progressive and Stronger Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.”

Addressing a news conference at the Information Cell, Civil Secretariat, Peshawar, she said she would continue to keep the media informed about the activities, initiatives and progress of the Governor and the Advisory Council, fulfilling her commitment to maintaining regular communication with journalists.

She said that, following the tragic incident in Dir Colony, Peshawar, inspections had been conducted at public and private schools and madaris across the province. During these inspections, 4,049 educational institutions were identified as requiring repairs and rehabilitation.

A comprehensive plan is being formulated to address the situation. Students enrolled in the affected institutions will be accommodated in nearby government schools according to their respective grade levels, while second shifts will be introduced wherever necessary to ensure the uninterrupted continuation of their education.

Bilour said the investigation into the Dir Colony incident had been completed and that a detailed report would be shared with the media shortly. She added that a subcommittee was also examining the responsibilities of the relevant departments and Tehsil Municipal Administrations (TMAs) to identify any negligence in the inspection, approval and monitoring of buildings.

Regarding police reforms, she said eight modern armoured vehicles had been handed over to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police to enhance its operational capabilities. She further stated that a comprehensive plan to strengthen police infrastructure and improve operational capacity would be developed over the next five to six weeks.

Paying tribute to police personnel for their courage, commitment and sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, she said providing them with modern equipment, adequate resources and improved facilities remained a government priority.

Clarifying the government’s position on the Sehat Card programme, Samar Bilour said internal irregularities within the programme were being reviewed; however, there was no intention to discontinue or abolish it. She added that the performance and administrative structures of Medical Teaching Institutions (MTIs), along with the professional qualifications and merit-based selection of their board members, were also being evaluated.

She emphasised that appointments to key positions must be made strictly on the basis of professional competence and merit, rather than political affiliations, personal relationships or favouritism. She added that any proposed reforms would be guided by institutional performance and professional standards, not political victimisation.

Regarding the ongoing anti-encroachment campaign, she said traffic congestion and drainage problems in Peshawar could not be effectively addressed without removing illegal encroachments from government land, green belts and drainage infrastructure. She maintained that the operation was being conducted indiscriminately, without favour or discrimination on the basis of political affiliation, personal connections or recommendations. She added that the government also planned to rehabilitate and beautify the cleared areas to make them more accessible and beneficial to the public.

Speaking about urban sanitation, she said the performance of urban sanitation services and the Water and Sanitation Services Company (WSSP) was improving, with sanitation teams continuing their work until late at night. She said the removal of accumulated waste in Peshawar was underway, while a comprehensive waste collection plan was also being developed. Measures were being considered to address shortages of manhole covers and dustbins and ensure the long-term availability, maintenance and protection of these public facilities.

Highlighting initiatives for young people, Samar Bilour said the Zalmi Madrasa League had successfully concluded, while another positive initiative for the youth of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would soon be announced in collaboration with Khyber TV.

On digital governance, she said Adviser on Legal Affairs Amir Javed had brought various institutions together on a common digital portal, in accordance with their respective mandates and statutory responsibilities. The portal had become operational and was designed to facilitate public access to institutional services and complaint redressal mechanisms through a single platform.

Discussing the political situation, Bilour said Sohail Afridi remained in protective custody. She added that available evidence relating to allegations of corruption involving billions of rupees was being compiled and that further details would be shared as investigations progressed.

Responding to recent statements by Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Ms Bilour described him as a senior and respected political leader. However, she observed that his recent statements appeared to reflect political dissatisfaction and frustration. She said allegations of corruption relating to the Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM) period, including matters involving individuals close to the JUI-F leadership, also required proper investigation and clarification.

She further suggested that dissatisfaction over the absence of a desired political role in the existing technocratic setup could also be a factor behind Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s recent political stance.

Ms Bilour said the government welcomed constructive suggestions and guidance from the JUI-F chief and remained open to acknowledging and addressing any shortcomings. However, she cautioned that the government’s patience should not be misconstrued as weakness. She reiterated that the provincial government’s priority was to act responsibly, safeguard the interests of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and address issues through appropriate institutional mechanisms.

headline: 18 PTI Shangla workers released from Swat Jail
description: Shangla - Eighteen workers of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Shangla, who were arrested under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (3-MPO)
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
Shangla - Eighteen workers of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Shangla, who were arrested under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (3-MPO) during the emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, have been released from Swat Jail following 16 days of continuous legal efforts.

The release has been described as a welcome development for the workers’ families and party circles. The Insaf Lawyers Forum (ILF) Malakand Division also paid tribute to its legal team, particularly former provincial assembly candidate Sadar ur Rehman Advocate, for their efforts in securing the workers’ release.

According to a statement issued by the Insaf Lawyers Forum Malakand Division, lawyers made continuous efforts to secure the release of the arrested workers and stood by them and their families during a difficult period. Expressing satisfaction over the release of all 18 workers after a 16-day legal struggle, the forum said that practical efforts to protect the rights of workers reflected a genuine commitment to professional and legal responsibilities.

The statement particularly acknowledged the services of Sadar ur Rehman Advocate, who made all-out efforts to secure the workers’ release and supported them throughout the legal proceedings. The forum also paid tribute to the tireless efforts and legal services of the entire ILF Malakand Division team, particularly Haq Nawaz Advocate, Raheemullah Chitrali Advocate, Kamal Advocate, Sadar ur Rehman Advocate and Jawad Ali Noor Advocate.

The arrests of PTI workers in Shangla assumed significance amid the evolving political and administrative situation following the imposition of emergency and Governor’s Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Actions under Section 3 of the MPO against various party leaders and workers in the district were accompanied by a series of arrests and raids. Consequently, affected families had to seek legal assistance to secure the release of their relatives.

Following the release of the 18 workers, the Insaf Lawyers Forum Malakand Division thanked all lawyers, assistants and other individuals who contributed to the legal struggle. The forum said its legal team had fulfilled its responsibilities by standing up for the rights of the workers during this difficult period, adding that all those involved deserved appreciation.

Describing the workers’ release as a source of happiness and relief for their families, the forum prayed that Almighty Allah would keep all the released workers safe, bless their families with happiness and reward everyone who contributed to the legal struggle.

headline: VXR festival set to bring immersive art and emerging technologies to Pakistan
description: Lahore - Pakistan will host the first local editions of VXR Festival, an international festival dedicated to virtual and extended reality (XR) art, digital
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: Lahore - Pakistan will host the first local editions of VXR Festival, an international festival dedicated to virtual and extended reality (XR) art, digital creativity and emerging technologies. Founded by Dr. Najam Ul Assar, the festival will take place in Lahore from 8–11 November and Islamabad from 13–15 November 2026.The festival will take place at multiple venues including Alliance Française de Lahore, National College of Arts Lahore, R Space and Beaconhouse National University Lahore. The 2026 editions in Pakistan are supported by the Embassy of France in Pakistan, Alliance Française de Lahore, the Institut français, the Embassy of Spain in Pakistan and AECID, in collaboration with UNESCO. The festival will bring together artists working across virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), extended reality (XR) and other immersive practices from Pakistan, France, Spain and beyond. Confirmed participating artists include Amna Tariq (Pakistan), Lola Zoido (Spain), Manel Bafaluy (Spain), Marie Lienhard (France), Sana Akram (Pakistan) and Sandrine Deumier (France), including others. A major highlight will be the first presentation in Pakistan of the Claude Monet Experience in VR, offering audiences an opportunity to encounter the work of one of the world’s most celebrated artists through immersive technology and a new digital perspective. “VR and XR art are no longer simply about new technologies; they are becoming important artistic languages through which we can rethink perception, space, memory and our relationship with technology,” said Dr. Najam Ul Assar, Festival Director. “There is a real need to bring these practices into public and cultural spaces in Pakistan, creating opportunities for audiences to experience, question and engage with the possibilities of immersive art.” VXR Festival builds on the work of the Lahore Digital Arts Festival team, which has supported digital art and creative technology in Pakistan since 2019. Through its programme of international and Pakistani artists, VXR Festival aims to expand opportunities for audiences to experience immersive art and explore the evolving relationship between artistic expression and emerging technologies.

headline: AI chatbot crime confessions raise privacy, legal concerns
description: Criminal confessions made to AI chatbots raise questions over privacy, legal obligations and whether technology companies should report suspicious
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots can be told about crimes, but uncertainties surrounding legal frameworks or measures that would mandate these tools to report confessions to law enforcement cast doubt on the pace of AI development.

AI chatbots have entered daily life, with many users worldwide using and sometimes misusing these tools, often making headlines around the world.

In August, a 19-year-old University of Missouri student reportedly confessed to ChatGPT that he damaged 17 parked cars on campus late at night and asked, “Will I go to jail?”

ChatGPT responded with “tips about the potential outcome of getting caught” but urged the user to dial 911 after the messages grew increasingly aggressive, police documents showed.

The chat history was uncovered after the student allowed investigators to examine his phone, and the history was used as evidence against him in court, becoming instrumental in the felony property-damage charges against him.

In a similar instance, court records in Florida showed that days before two college students went missing in April and were later found dead, their roommate had asked ChatGPT, “What happens if a human has put in a black garbage bag and thrown in a dumpster.”

Canada’s British Columbia provincial government filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT.

The lawsuit, filed in February, concerned a mass school shooting that left nine people, mostly children, dead and 27 injured.

The case alleged that the firm failed to report the shooter’s chat with ChatGPT to law enforcement and argued that the attack could have been prevented if OpenAI had warned police.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman apologized in a letter, but whistleblowers told The Wall Street Journal newspaper that the conversation between the shooter and ChatGPT had allegedly already been flagged in June 2025. However, Altman and the firm’s leadership reportedly overrode the safety team’s recommendations to contact police.

The ethical implications of these interactions continue to deepen, as a study in Australia found that children are more likely to report sexual abuse online to chatbots than to responsible adults.

The same privacy principles that apply between lawyers and clients or doctors and patients do not apply to AI chatbot conversations, so tech firms can share logs with investigators.

While researchers debate whether chatbots should report crimes, the prospect is further complicated by algorithms misinterpreting intent.

For instance, Anthropic’s Claude 5 gave a false tip about an unsolved murder to a US police hotline in July.

AI chatbots should not be used in crime prediction Matthew Trail, an American legal scholar and researcher at Goethe University in Germany, told Anadolu that each company developing AI chatbots adopts different rules and that these chatbots are not designed to respond to inquiries about planning murders and similar acts.

Trail stated that chatbots are trained to avoid certain topics, especially those regarding child sexual abuse, and refer these conversations to human moderators. However, users can compose their prompts in a certain way, such as by pretending to ask for help with writing fiction, to circumvent these filters and obtain AI-generated answers to otherwise inappropriate questions or requests.

Trail noted that while law enforcement could request a person’s chat history from AI firms when the person is suspected of having committed a crime, the primary goal of AI chatbots must not be to predict crimes before they are committed, as laws and policies surrounding this prospect are very unclear.

He added that allowing these AI models to collect more data than they already do to make more accurate assessments of crime potential is not a good idea, either.

Can AI chatbot conversations ever be private? People across the globe discuss a myriad of topics with AI chatbots, especially personal matters ranging from health issues to psychological support and life advice.

As more and more people turn to AI for conversations, ethical debates over privacy have come to the fore.

Altman said in July 2025 that conversations with AI chatbots must be based on confidentiality.

Robert Diab, a law professor at Thompson Rivers University in Canada, stated that laws do not treat communications between accomplices as confidential, arguing that chats between humans and AI chatbots could be treated according to the same principle.

Diab said models like ChatGPT appear to be capable of detecting when users are prone to criminal behavior and argued that chatbot developers could prevent crime by notifying law enforcement.

He mentioned that alerting law enforcement based on all suspicious messages could also increase the workload of human teams due to false alarms.

He added that users will always find a way to circumvent security measures to use AI to commit a crime.

headline: Canada, EU launch alliance to strengthen economic, defence and technology ties
description: Canada and the EU launch a new strategic alliance covering critical minerals, energy, artificial intelligence, digital trade and defence cooperation at the
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Canada and the European Union on Friday launched a new alliance aimed at strengthening economic security, defense cooperation, and technological ties, with agreements covering critical minerals, artificial intelligence (AI), digital trade, and energy.

The announcement came at the 21st EU-Canada Summit, held in Montreal, where Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

In a joint statement, the leaders announced the launch of the Canada-EU Alliance for the Future, an initiative designed to create a common prosperity and economic security space between the two partners.

"Our Alliance for the Future will be based on the principle of reciprocity in industrial sectors where both sides have agreed to deepen strategic cooperation to identify and mitigate shared economic security concerns and to build more integrated and resilient supply chains across our markets," the statement said.

Critical minerals, energy, economy

A major pillar of the new alliance will be securing access to critical raw materials and strengthening supply chains on both sides of the Atlantic.

Canada and the EU intend to accelerate investment across the entire critical minerals value chain, from extraction and processing to refining, manufacturing, and recycling.

The leaders also agreed to explore mechanisms to improve security of supply, including possible stockpiling arrangements for strategic resources needed by civilian and defense industries.

The European Investment Bank and Canada have also concluded negotiations on an agreement intended to facilitate European investment in Canada's critical resources, particularly critical raw materials.

Energy cooperation will also be expanded, including support for the development of liquefied natural gas exchanges, in line with both sides' climate commitments.

AI, trade, education

Canada and the EU announced the conclusion of substantive negotiations on a digital trade agreement, which aims to provide a modern framework for digital trade, improve legal certainty, and facilitate cross-border data flows.

The partners will work to remove bilateral trade barriers, strengthen regulatory and standards cooperation, and develop sectoral roadmaps for strategic industries.

They also plan to establish a business council bringing together companies from both sides of the Atlantic.

The two sides also intend to deepen cooperation on digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence, including trusted and sovereign cloud infrastructure, computing capacity, data, AI models, software, and applications.

On education and research, Canada and the EU will launch negotiations towards deeper Canadian participation in Erasmus+, the EU's flagship program for education, training, youth, and sport.

No reference to 'associate membership'

The summit also takes place against the backdrop of a debate over the future institutional relationship between Canada and the EU.

Von der Leyen had previously floated the idea of associate membership for Canada during her State of the Union address in Strasbourg, suggesting a closer relationship that would stop short of full EU membership.

However, the proposal reportedly ran into resistance among some EU member states ahead of the summit, with Germany reportedly leading efforts to remove the wording.

The final joint statement makes no reference to associate membership.

Instead, the leaders describe their ambition as creating an even closer association between Canada and the EU, with more frequent high-level political engagement, exchanges on shared priorities, and closer coordination on international challenges.

article_html:
Canada and the European Union on Friday launched a new alliance aimed at strengthening economic security, defense cooperation, and technological ties, with agreements covering critical minerals, artificial intelligence (AI), digital trade, and energy.

The announcement came at the 21st EU-Canada Summit, held in Montreal, where Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

In a joint statement, the leaders announced the launch of the Canada-EU Alliance for the Future, an initiative designed to create a common prosperity and economic security space between the two partners.

Federal Constitutional Court upholds finality of judgments, rejects repeated challenges in land dispute

"Our Alliance for the Future will be based on the principle of reciprocity in industrial sectors where both sides have agreed to deepen strategic cooperation to identify and mitigate shared economic security concerns and to build more integrated and resilient supply chains across our markets," the statement said.

Critical minerals, energy, economy

A major pillar of the new alliance will be securing access to critical raw materials and strengthening supply chains on both sides of the Atlantic.

Canada and the EU intend to accelerate investment across the entire critical minerals value chain, from extraction and processing to refining, manufacturing, and recycling.

The leaders also agreed to explore mechanisms to improve security of supply, including possible stockpiling arrangements for strategic resources needed by civilian and defense industries.

The European Investment Bank and Canada have also concluded negotiations on an agreement intended to facilitate European investment in Canada's critical resources, particularly critical raw materials.

Energy cooperation will also be expanded, including support for the development of liquefied natural gas exchanges, in line with both sides' climate commitments.

AI, trade, education
