Canada and the EU announced the conclusion of substantive negotiations on a digital trade agreement, which aims to provide a modern framework for digital trade, improve legal certainty, and facilitate cross-border data flows.

The partners will work to remove bilateral trade barriers, strengthen regulatory and standards cooperation, and develop sectoral roadmaps for strategic industries.

They also plan to establish a business council bringing together companies from both sides of the Atlantic.

The two sides also intend to deepen cooperation on digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence, including trusted and sovereign cloud infrastructure, computing capacity, data, AI models, software, and applications.

On education and research, Canada and the EU will launch negotiations towards deeper Canadian participation in Erasmus+, the EU's flagship program for education, training, youth, and sport.

No reference to 'associate membership'

The summit also takes place against the backdrop of a debate over the future institutional relationship between Canada and the EU.

Von der Leyen had previously floated the idea of associate membership for Canada during her State of the Union address in Strasbourg, suggesting a closer relationship that would stop short of full EU membership.

However, the proposal reportedly ran into resistance among some EU member states ahead of the summit, with Germany reportedly leading efforts to remove the wording.

headline: Pakistan to observe public holiday on November 9 for Iqbal Day
description: The federal government has announced a nationwide public holiday on Monday, November 9, 2026, to commemorate the birth anniversary of national poet Allama
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has announced a nationwide public holiday on Monday, November 9, 2026, to commemorate the birth anniversary of national poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal.

A notification issued by the Cabinet Division confirmed that the holiday would be observed across the country in accordance with the annual holiday schedule released on January 19, 2026.

All federal ministries and government departments have been instructed to implement the decision. Public and private offices, along with educational institutions, will remain closed on the day.

The holiday will provide employees and students following a Saturday-Sunday weekend with three consecutive days off, from November 7 to 9. Normal office and educational activities will resume on Tuesday, November 10.

headline: US approves $2.1bn sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine
description: US State Department approves possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles worth $2.1bn to Ukraine, with funding provided by European allies and partners.
author: Anadolu
article_text:
The US State Department on Friday approved a possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement missiles and related equipment to Ukraine at an estimated cost of $2.1 billion.

The department said the cost is “funded entirely by partners and allies.”

“Ukraine will pay for this purchase with donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan,” it said in a statement. “No U.S. funds are involved in this sale.”

The package also includes classified and unclassified spare parts, along with logistics and program support.

Lockheed Martin will be the principal contractor.

The approval comes days after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine this year has received an average of 12 Patriot interceptors per month from the US, while it needs to intercept around 150 Russian ballistic missiles per month.

On Monday, Zelenskyy said Kyiv had been waiting nearly a month for US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems.

The Ukraine Support Loan is an EU credit instrument of up to €90 billion (over $100 billion) for 2026-2027, with €60 billion allocated to Ukraine’s defense needs. The European Commission has approved Ukraine’s use of the loan to buy US-made Patriot interceptors.

headline: Diesel price rises by Rs2.29 per litre, petrol rate unchanged
description: The federal government has raised the price of high-speed diesel by Rs2.29 per litre, while keeping petrol rates unchanged for the period from October 31 to
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has raised the price of high-speed diesel by Rs2.29 per litre, while keeping petrol rates unchanged for the period from October 31 to November 2.

Under the revised rates, diesel will now cost Rs402.96 per litre, compared with its previous price, while petrol will continue to be sold at Rs377.91 per litre.

The Petroleum Division issued a notification confirming that the new prices took effect on October 31 and will remain applicable until November 2.

Separately, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has begun uploading daily petroleum price calculations to its official website in a move aimed at improving transparency in fuel pricing.

Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said the calculations were based on a seven-day average of international oil market rates, following practices adopted in other countries.

The revised mechanism is intended to help domestic fuel prices respond more promptly to movements in global petroleum markets.

headline: Azhar Javaid elected chairman of Pakistan Press Club UK
description: Senior Pakistani journalist and political commentator Azhar Javaid has been elected chairman of the Pakistan Press Club UK (PPCUK) following the merger of
author: APP
article_text:
Senior Pakistani journalist and political commentator Azhar Javaid has been elected chairman of the Pakistan Press Club UK (PPCUK) following the merger of Pakistan Press Club UK and Pakistan Press Club UK International.

The unification brings together two major organisations representing Pakistani journalists across the United Kingdom under a single platform.

Pakistan’s High Commissioner to the UK, Tipu Usman, welcomed a delegation of the newly unified organisation, led by its chairman, Azhar Javaid, at the Pakistan High Commission in London.

Representatives of the Pakistani journalistic community from London, Birmingham, Manchester, Bradford and Sheffield attended the meeting.

During the gathering, High Commissioner Tipu Usman and PPCUK President Arshad Rachyal formally handed over the notification of Javaid’s appointment as chairman.

Javaid is a London-based journalist, political commentator and analyst with more than three decades of experience. He has worked with several leading Pakistani news organisations, including Geo News, ARY News, Dunya News and Samaa TV, and has held senior positions overseeing international news gathering and operations.

Speaking on the occasion, Tipu Usman emphasised the importance of strengthening engagement with the Pakistani diaspora across the UK, particularly younger generations. He also highlighted initiatives undertaken by the Pakistan High Commission to facilitate Pakistanis living in the country.

The unification of the two press clubs is expected to promote professional cooperation, strengthen media networking, provide a collective voice for Pakistani journalists and enhance engagement with the Pakistani diaspora.

The development marks a new chapter for the organisation, bringing Pakistani journalists from across the United Kingdom onto a common platform.

headline: Trump may consider major Iran strike after midterm setbacks: report
description: Trump could consider a major military operation against Iran following Republican midterm setbacks, Axios reports, as Qatar mediates renewed US-Iran talks.
author: Anadolu
article_text:
US President Donald Trump may be more inclined to approve a large-scale military operation against Iran if Republicans fare badly in the midterm elections next week, according to a report on Friday.

"If he feels embarrassed or disenfranchised, he will do something bold," a US official told Axios, adding that it is the message being passed to Iranian officials, who are being told their best chance for a deal is now.

A White House official rejected the idea, telling the outlet that election results will not factor into Trump's decisions on Iran.

The report said Qatari mediators spent more than 12 hours on Friday in Tehran, staying in regular contact with the White House, to restart direct talks between Washington and Tehran. A diplomatic source described "positive progress," and discussions are due to continue Saturday in Doha.

Talks have stalled over competing demands, according to one US official. Washington wants nuclear concessions as part of any return to negotiations, while Tehran insists the US first lift its naval blockade, release frozen funds and allow oil sales.

The report said Doha is urging Iran to allow UN inspectors into its bombed nuclear sites in exchange for limited sanctions relief.

Pointing to divisions within Trump's circle, the report said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are skeptical of any deal and favor further weakening of Iran’s leadership. Vice President JD Vance and envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner back resuming talks.

The report comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway for global energy shipments.

The US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on Feb. 28, triggering Iranian retaliation in the region.

Despite subsequent diplomatic efforts and a memorandum signed by Washington and Tehran in June, tensions have persisted over security arrangements and navigation through the strait.

headline: Sikandar Raza becomes oldest player to score a T20I century at 40
description: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza has entered the record books after becoming the first player aged 40 or above to score a century in men's T20 Internationals.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza has entered the record books after becoming the first player aged 40 or above to score a century in men's T20 Internationals.

The all-rounder reached the milestone during the second T20I against Afghanistan at Sharjah Cricket Stadium, striking an unbeaten 106 from just 56 balls.

His innings included nine sixes and five fours, as he produced an aggressive display despite Zimbabwe eventually losing the match.

Raza's achievement surpassed the previous record held by a Gibraltar batter, who scored a T20I hundred against Bulgaria at the age of 39 years and 272 days.

The 40-year-old's century marks a significant individual milestone in his career and adds another record to his achievements in international cricket.

headline: Islamabad police impose traffic diversions at Khanna Pul, Lehtrar Road
description: Islamabad Traffic Police (ITP) has imposed traffic diversions at Khanna Pul and Lehtrar Road from Saturday until further orders due to ongoing construction
author: NNI
article_text:
Islamabad Traffic Police (ITP) has imposed traffic diversions at Khanna Pul and Lehtrar Road from Saturday until further orders due to ongoing construction work, advising motorists to use alternative routes and allow an additional 20 to 25 minutes for their journeys.

An ITP official said traffic heading towards Tramri Chowk, Lehtrar Road and Ali Pur should use alternative routes via Faizabad, Rawal Dam Chowk and Park Road.

Motorists travelling from Khanna Pul towards Islamabad Expressway have been advised to use Ghouri Town Link Road.

The official said traffic police personnel had been deployed at key points to guide motorists and ensure smooth traffic flow during the construction work.

Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Kianat advised citizens to plan their journeys in advance and allow extra travel time to avoid inconvenience.

headline: SHC orders removal of encroachments from park in Karachi's Scheme 33
description: Sindh High Court orders removal of illegal constructions from a park in Karachi's Scheme 33 and seeks a compliance report from authorities by January 20.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Sindh High Court (SHC) has ordered the removal of encroachments and illegal constructions from a park in Karachi's Scheme 33 and directed the authorities concerned to restore the land to its original condition.

The directives were issued during the hearing of a petition challenging the occupation of park land and construction of buildings in Sector 15-A of Scheme 33.

The court directed the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) to assist the relevant authorities in removing the encroachments and restoring the park.

It also sought a compliance report from the deputy commissioner East and revenue officials by January 20.

During the hearing, the petitioner's counsel, Advocate Usman Farooq, argued that the illegal constructions posed a threat to human lives, particularly because K-Electric installations were located at the site.

He informed the court that K-Electric had also issued a letter warning of the potential dangers associated with construction activities in the area.

The petitioner sought immediate demolition of the illegal structures in Scheme 33, Sector 15-A, and requested the court to restrain the builder from undertaking further construction or booking units in the building.

headline: Islamabad launches anti-polio drive targeting over 447,000 children
description: Islamabad administration launches sixth anti-polio campaign of 2026, aiming to vaccinate 447,614 children across the capital from November 2 to 5.
author: APP
article_text:
The Islamabad district administration has launched preparations for the sixth anti-polio campaign of 2026, targeting 447,614 children across the federal capital during a four-day vaccination drive scheduled from November 2 to 5.

The campaign was inaugurated by the deputy commissioner of Islamabad at Golra Railway Station, where he administered polio drops to children travelling by train.

During the inauguration, the additional deputy commissioner (headquarters) briefed participants on the arrangements and preparations made for the vaccination drive.

According to the district administration, all necessary preparations have been completed to ensure the smooth conduct of the campaign.

Polio vaccination teams will visit households, educational institutions and hospitals across Islamabad to administer vaccine doses to children.

Special vaccination camps will also be established at public places to facilitate parents and ensure wider immunisation coverage.

The administration said the campaign aimed to vaccinate 447,614 children during the four-day drive as part of ongoing efforts to protect children against the poliovirus.

Officials urged citizens to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure that their children receive the required polio drops.

Parents were also requested to facilitate polio workers during their visits to homes and other designated locations.

The vaccination campaign will continue across the federal capital until November 5 as part of efforts to prevent the spread of polio.

headline: UAE crush India by six wickets to end Cup semi-final hopes at Hong Kong Sixes
description: The United Arab Emirates secured a commanding six-wicket victory over India in the Hong Kong Sixes tournament, eliminating the Indian side from contention for
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The United Arab Emirates secured a commanding six-wicket victory over India in the Hong Kong Sixes tournament, eliminating the Indian side from contention for a place in the Cup semi-finals.

The Group C fixture took place at Mission Road Ground, where the UAE opted to bowl after winning the toss.

India posted 94 for six in their allotted six overs, with Natarajan scoring 38 from 14 balls and Rahul Tripathi adding 24 off just seven deliveries.

Zahid Ali was the pick of the UAE bowlers, taking three wickets, while Muhammad Farooq and Muhammad Faraz claimed one apiece.

The UAE made light work of the 95-run target, reaching 96 without losing a wicket in only 4.2 overs.

Captain Khalid Shah spearheaded the chase with an unbeaten 52 off 14 balls, including six sixes and three fours. Ansh Tandon supported him with 39 not out from 12 deliveries, hitting five sixes and two boundaries.

The emphatic win secured the UAE's victory while bringing India's Cup semi-final campaign to an end.

headline: World Bank approves $150m for Sindh property tax reforms
description: The World Bank’s Board of Executive Directors has approved $150 million in financing for a programme aimed at improving property tax collection and
author: NNI
article_text:
The World Bank’s Board of Executive Directors has approved $150 million in financing for a programme aimed at improving property tax collection and strengthening municipal service delivery in Sindh, particularly Karachi.

The Sindh Property Revenues Enhancement Program (Sindh PREP) will support the provincial government in improving urban immovable property tax (UIPT) collection and strengthening the service delivery capacity of selected local councils, according to a World Bank news release issued on Saturday.

World Bank Country Director for Pakistan Bolormaa Amgaabazar said Sindh’s local councils currently depended on provincial transfers for more than 95 per cent of their revenues.

She said the programme would help cities generate their own revenues and invest in infrastructure and essential public services.

Despite being one of the world's largest cities, Karachi currently collects around $8.5 million annually in property taxes, significantly less than comparable cities.

The programme aims to increase Karachi’s annual property tax collection to $85 million by raising compliance from 20 to 50 per cent.

It will strengthen tax administration through a property tax management information system covering billing, payment processing and grievance redressal, alongside integrated financial management systems across local councils.

Around 70 per cent of the collected property tax revenue will be reinvested in municipal infrastructure and services across Karachi’s 25 local councils, benefiting approximately 3.58 million people.

The investments will cover drainage, sewerage, schools, fire stations, roads and street lighting, with funding linked to annual performance assessments.

The programme also includes a $40 million investment financing component to expand property surveys and tax administration to 20 local councils in other urban centres of Sindh, indirectly benefiting around 4.5 million people.

World Bank Senior Urban Development Specialist Davison Muchadenyika said Karachi had significant untapped potential to generate revenue from its property base and use it to finance infrastructure and services.

headline: Khawaja Asif urges educated youth to play role in Pakistan's development
description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif urges skilled youth to contribute to national development, highlights Pakistan's military and diplomatic achievements and
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Saturday urged educated and skilled young people to contribute to Pakistan's development, saying they had a vital role to play in shaping the country's future.

Addressing the annual convocation of the University of Central Punjab in Sialkot, Khawaja Asif congratulated the graduating students and stressed the importance of education and professional skills in advancing national progress.

The minister said Pakistan had secured a prominent position internationally, particularly following what he described as its victory in Marka-e-Haq, which he claimed had significantly strengthened the country's diplomatic standing.

Referring to Pakistan's military confrontation with India, he said relying on foreign military bases could not guarantee national security.

"Overseas bases established by foreign powers cannot protect you. Such bases are created to serve vested interests, while real security comes from your own strength," he said.

Khawaja Asif claimed that Pakistan had attained an international standing unprecedented in its 78-year history.

He said Pakistan had defeated an adversary five times its size during Marka-e-Haq, adding that while the outcomes of previous wars had remained open to interpretation, Indian leaders had themselves acknowledged defeat following the latest confrontation.

The defence minister also claimed that US President Donald Trump had referred to India's defeat on 11 occasions and repeatedly mentioned the downing of Indian aircraft.

Praising Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir's leadership, Khawaja Asif said Pakistan continued to make progress despite having confronted terrorism for several decades.

Highlighting Islamabad's diplomatic engagement, he said Pakistan was playing an important role in efforts to secure a ceasefire between Iran and the United States.

He added that Pakistan's diplomatic initiatives had also helped ease tensions between Iran and Arab countries, expressing hope that the country's efforts to promote international peace would succeed.

Reflecting on his political career, the minister said he had served the country for 36 years and had faced imprisonment on several occasions.

He recalled spending seven months in jail during the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) government, alleging that those responsible for his arrest had failed to establish the charges against him.

The minister said he generally refrained from discussing politics at educational institutions despite being a politician.

He also expressed gratitude to the people of Sialkot, saying the city had accorded him considerable respect since the beginning of his political career.

Criticising the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), Khawaja Asif alleged that accountability institutions often arrested individuals before determining the charges or preparing cases against them.

He regretted that such practices had remained a recurring feature of Pakistan's political history over the past 78 years.

Addressing the annual convocation of the University of Central Punjab in Sialkot, Khawaja Asif congratulated the graduating students and stressed the importance of education and professional skills in advancing national progress.

The minister said Pakistan had secured a prominent position internationally, particularly following what he described as its victory in Marka-e-Haq, which he claimed had significantly strengthened the country's diplomatic standing.

"Overseas bases established by foreign powers cannot protect you. Such bases are created to serve vested interests, while real security comes from your own strength," he said.

Khawaja Asif claimed that Pakistan had attained an international standing unprecedented in its 78-year history.

He said Pakistan had defeated an adversary five times its size during Marka-e-Haq, adding that while the outcomes of previous wars had remained open to interpretation, Indian leaders had themselves acknowledged defeat following the latest confrontation.

Highlighting Islamabad's diplomatic engagement, he said Pakistan was playing an important role in efforts to secure a ceasefire between Iran and the United States.

The minister said he generally refrained from discussing politics at educational institutions despite being a politician.

headline: NCCIA arrests four suspects over fake visa, air ticket scam
description: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Islamabad has arrested four suspects allegedly involved in defrauding citizens through fake visa and air
author: NNI
article_text:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Islamabad has arrested four suspects allegedly involved in defrauding citizens through fake visa and air ticket services advertised on WhatsApp groups.

According to an NCCIA official, the suspects were operating a financial fraud network under the guise of a travel agency, attracting customers by offering visa and air ticket services through WhatsApp groups.

The suspects allegedly collected payments from citizens seeking travel services but provided forged travel documents instead of genuine visas and tickets.

The official said the suspects used WhatsApp groups to approach potential customers and persuade them to transfer money for travel-related services.

The NCCIA has registered two First Information Reports (FIRs) under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016 and the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

Further investigation is underway to determine the extent of the alleged fraud and identify other individuals involved in the network.

headline: China's biotechnology sector shifts from manufacturing to exploring pharma innovation
description: China's biotechnology sector is expanding its role in the global pharmaceutical industry, moving beyond the manufacturing of conventional medicines and
author: Web Desk
article_text:
China's biotechnology sector is expanding its role in the global pharmaceutical industry, moving beyond the manufacturing of conventional medicines and pharmaceutical ingredients to the development and international licensing of innovative drugs, as growing demand for Chinese-developed therapies creates new opportunities for international research and commercial partnerships.

According to pharmaceutical industry data provider PharmCube, overseas licensing agreements involving Chinese pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies reached a combined potential value of approximately $139.4 billion by October 8, 2026, surpassing the $138.8 billion recorded throughout 2025.

The agreements cover innovative treatments for cancer, obesity and autoimmune diseases, reflecting growing international interest in China's pharmaceutical research and development capabilities. Upfront payments under these agreements amounted to approximately $8 billion during the first three quarters of 2026.

Major international pharmaceutical companies, including AstraZeneca, GSK and Novo Nordisk, have entered licensing partnerships involving Chinese-developed therapies, highlighting China's growing importance in global drug discovery and the commercial development of new medicines.

Dr Ijaz Akram, Assistant Professor at the Department of Biotechnology, Institute of Space Technology, told Wealth Pakistan that China's expanding biotechnology licensing market demonstrated how pharmaceutical competitiveness was increasingly being shaped by research, clinical development and intellectual property rather than manufacturing capacity alone.

“Pakistan can benefit from closer cooperation with Chinese companies through specialised manufacturing, technology transfer and joint research programmes,” he said.

The growing value of overseas licensing agreements reflects a broader transformation in China's pharmaceutical industry, with domestic companies increasingly developing innovative therapies and securing commercial partnerships with international drug manufacturers.

According to China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the potential value of overseas licensing agreements involving innovative Chinese medicines exceeded $100 billion during the first half of 2026.

The ministry also reported that China approved 38 innovative medicines for marketing during the same period, including 31 developed by domestic companies, indicating the country's growing capabilities in pharmaceutical research and product development.

In September 2026, Chinese authorities outlined further plans to strengthen the biomedical industry, with an emphasis on innovative medicines, biotechnology research and international competitiveness.

The expansion of China's pharmaceutical innovation sector is creating opportunities for developing economies to establish partnerships in drug research, specialised manufacturing, technology transfer and clinical development.

For Pakistan, closer cooperation with Chinese biotechnology companies could provide an opportunity to move beyond importing medicines and pharmaceutical raw materials towards developing domestic research capabilities and higher-value pharmaceutical products.

Dr Ijaz Akram said Pakistan should prioritise partnerships that strengthen local technical expertise rather than limiting cooperation to the importation or packaging of finished pharmaceutical products.

"Technology-transfer agreements should include workforce training, research collaboration and the development of local production capabilities. This would help Pakistani pharmaceutical companies gradually move towards higher-value products and improve their prospects in international markets," he said.

He added that cooperation with Chinese pharmaceutical companies could help Pakistan gradually develop expertise in specialised manufacturing and research-based pharmaceutical production, provided such partnerships included meaningful knowledge transfer and technical training.

The growing international demand for innovative medicines also highlights the importance of strong research institutions, clinical-trial capabilities and regulatory systems in supporting pharmaceutical development.

Talking to Wealth Pakistan, Fatima Ayub, Researcher at the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Hamdard University, said Pakistan could benefit from China's progress in biotechnology by developing stronger links between pharmaceutical companies, universities and research institutions.

"Pakistan has opportunities to collaborate with Chinese biotechnology institutions in drug discovery, clinical research and advanced pharmaceutical development. However, these partnerships will require reliable clinical-trial systems, internationally recognised quality standards and sustained investment in scientific expertise," she said.

Fatima emphasised that international pharmaceutical cooperation should focus on building long-term scientific and technological capabilities rather than relying solely on short-term commercial arrangements.

“Joint research laboratories, researcher exchanges and collaborative clinical development programmes could help Pakistan strengthen its biotechnology ecosystem. The objective should be to create the capacity to develop and commercialise pharmaceutical innovations locally,” she added.

She said stronger collaboration between academic institutions and pharmaceutical manufacturers could help translate scientific research into commercially useful products while improving the skills and experience of local researchers.

China's expanding role in international pharmaceutical licensing also demonstrates the growing commercial importance of intellectual property and research-led innovation in the global medicines market.

Unlike conventional pharmaceutical exports, licensing agreements allow drug developers to commercialise their research through international partners, potentially generating upfront payments, milestone revenues, and royalties as medicines progress toward the market.

However, the reported $139.4 billion represents the combined potential value of licensing agreements, including payments linked to future development and commercial milestones, rather than revenue already received by Chinese companies.

For Pakistan, China's transformation offers an opportunity to strengthen pharmaceutical cooperation through joint research, technology transfer, workforce development and specialised manufacturing.

The country's ability to benefit from these opportunities will depend on sustained investment in scientific expertise, internationally recognised regulatory standards and partnerships that support the development of domestic pharmaceutical innovation.

headline: Regionalisation of the Pakistan-Afghanistan Conflict
description: The conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan, historically rooted in disputes over the Durand Line, cross-border militancy and mutual mistrust, is
author: Rania Daultana
article_text:
The conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan, historically rooted in disputes over the Durand Line, cross-border militancy and mutual mistrust, is increasingly acquiring a wider geopolitical dimension. China's growing diplomatic, military and economic engagement with Pakistan, alongside India's renewed ties with Afghanistan, has brought the longstanding tensions between Islamabad and Kabul into the broader strategic rivalry between Beijing and New Delhi.

Although neither China nor India created the conflict, both have significant interests in its outcome. Their involvement is reshaping regional calculations, complicating diplomatic efforts and raising the stakes of an already volatile relationship.

China's Strategic and Economic Interests

China's involvement is closely tied to its longstanding strategic partnership with Pakistan. As Pakistan's largest trading partner and a major defence supplier, Beijing has invested heavily in the country's economic development, particularly through the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), a flagship component of its Belt and Road Initiative.

According to the Council on Foreign Relations, the corridor's highway and energy projects represent investments estimated at approximately $65 billion. Protecting these investments from militant attacks and regional instability remains a central Chinese concern.

Afghanistan presents both a security challenge and an economic opportunity for Beijing. Militant organisations operating in the region threaten Chinese interests, while improved relations with Kabul could open new trade routes connecting South and Central Asia.

China is particularly concerned about the Turkistan Islamic Party, which Beijing associates with separatist militancy in Xinjiang. Afghanistan's narrow Wakhan Corridor borders China's western region, reinforcing Beijing's concerns that militant groups could exploit Afghan territory to threaten Chinese security.

Consequently, China has repeatedly sought assurances from the Taliban authorities that Afghanistan will not provide sanctuary to organisations threatening its interests.

Economic considerations are equally important. In May 2025, China, Pakistan and Afghanistan agreed to cooperate on extending CPEC into Afghanistan, potentially improving regional trade and infrastructure connectivity. The three countries also discussed closer counterterrorism coordination.

China's diplomatic involvement became particularly visible in April 2026, when representatives from Pakistan and Afghanistan attended talks in Urumqi from April 1 to 7 amid escalating tensions.

The discussions brought together senior foreign affairs, defence and security officials. Afghanistan described the consultations as useful, while China indicated that both sides had agreed to explore comprehensive solutions and avoid further escalation.

Pakistan used the talks to reiterate its security demands, including action against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the dismantling of militant infrastructure allegedly operating from Afghan territory.

Beijing's role demonstrated its emergence as more than an economic and military partner of Islamabad. It has also become an important diplomatic intermediary between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

For China, continued hostilities threaten investments, regional connectivity, the security of Chinese nationals and prospects for expanding trade. Its interests therefore extend beyond Pakistan's immediate concerns about cross-border terrorism.

India's Renewed Engagement with Afghanistan

India, meanwhile, has gradually rebuilt its relationship with Afghanistan following the Taliban's return to power in August 2021.

New Delhi initially closed its embassy in Kabul but subsequently adopted a cautious policy of engagement, establishing a technical mission in 2022 to coordinate humanitarian assistance and maintain diplomatic contacts.

In January 2025, Taliban officials described India as a significant regional and economic partner. Relations advanced further in October 2025, when Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi visited New Delhi and India announced plans to restore its full diplomatic presence in Kabul.

Despite this engagement, India has not formally recognised the Taliban government.

India's interests in Afghanistan are both economic and strategic. New Delhi has invested more than $3 billion in Afghan development projects over the years, including healthcare, infrastructure and water management.

It has also maintained humanitarian assistance while exploring trade opportunities through Iran's Chabahar Port, which provides access to Afghanistan without relying on Pakistani transit routes.

For Islamabad, however, India's expanding engagement with Kabul raises longstanding security concerns.

Analysts Feryaz Ocakli and Yelena Biberman, writing for the Lowy Institute, have highlighted Pakistan's apprehension that India could exploit deteriorating relations between Islamabad and Kabul to strengthen its influence along Pakistan's western frontier.

India, for its part, sees engagement with Afghanistan as an opportunity to preserve its regional influence, protect economic interests and address potential security threats, including those involving militant organisations.

Pakistan has accused India of supporting the TTP and has portrayed the Taliban administration as increasingly aligned with New Delhi. These allegations reflect Islamabad's longstanding concerns about strategic encirclement and the possibility of facing hostile pressures along both its eastern and western borders.

However, India's growing diplomatic relationship with Kabul does not, in itself, establish Indian involvement in TTP attacks or military operations against Pakistan. Distinguishing between legitimate security concerns, political allegations and verifiable evidence remains essential.

A Wider Regional Challenge

The evolving regional alignments should not be mistaken for two equivalent alliances.

China's relationship with Pakistan is longstanding, institutionalised and supported by extensive military, diplomatic and economic cooperation. India's relationship with Taliban-ruled Afghanistan, by contrast, remains relatively recent, cautious and largely pragmatic.

Nevertheless, the growing involvement of both powers has introduced additional strategic considerations into the Pakistan-Afghanistan dispute.

China seeks stability to protect its investments, contain militancy and expand regional connectivity. India wants to preserve its influence in Afghanistan, maintain access to Central Asia and prevent Pakistan from dominating Kabul's foreign relations.

Pakistan remains primarily concerned about cross-border militancy, particularly attacks attributed to the TTP, while Afghanistan's Taliban authorities face their own political, economic and security pressures.

The result is a conflict that can no longer be understood exclusively through the historical grievances between Islamabad and Kabul.

Yet describing Afghanistan as merely another arena for China-India competition would oversimplify the situation. The fundamental disputes remain bilateral, even as wider geopolitical rivalries increasingly influence diplomatic choices.

Ultimately, reducing tensions will require sustained engagement between Pakistan and Afghanistan, credible counterterrorism commitments and regional cooperation. China's mediation and India's diplomatic engagement could contribute to stability, provided their competing interests do not deepen existing divisions.

The consequences of continued confrontation would extend well beyond the two neighbouring countries, affecting security, trade and economic connectivity across South and Central Asia.

headline: Musadik Malik calls for satellite technology to strengthen disaster preparedness
description: Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadik Malik on Saturday called for greater use of satellite technology, artificial intelligence and digital modelling
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadik Malik on Saturday called for greater use of satellite technology, artificial intelligence and digital modelling to strengthen Pakistan’s disaster preparedness and protect vulnerable communities from climate-related hazards.

Addressing the closing ceremony of an international conference titled “Leveraging Space Technology for Early Warning for All, Climate Action and Disaster Risk Assessment”, the minister said the government would work towards producing an annual satellite-based report before the next monsoon season to identify construction and human activities in riverbeds and floodplains.

He said satellite-based evidence could help identify vulnerable locations and provide a scientific basis for effective land-use planning and disaster-risk reduction, regardless of the economic or political influence of those involved.

Emphasising the need for location-specific early-warning systems, Dr Musadik Malik said issuing a warning was not enough unless it reached people directly exposed to a particular hazard.

“A warning without an address is addressed to no one,” he said, calling for a mechanism to ensure that residents, tourists and communities in vulnerable mountainous areas received timely alerts about impending disasters.

Referring to a flood incident in which a family was caught in rapidly rising water despite an earlier warning, he said scientific information must be translated into practical measures to save lives.

The minister also referred to the reported deaths of around 4,600 people in Karachi during a week-long heatwave, questioning why such losses continued despite the availability of scientific information and weather forecasting capabilities.

He stressed that disaster preparedness required an effective follow-up mechanism, comparing it with medical professionals who monitor patients after diagnosis and treatment.

Highlighting the potential of digital modelling, he said digital twins could help assess risks associated with building collapses, inadequate construction standards, inappropriate zoning and poor drainage systems.

He added that satellite data could provide evidence-based information on land use and environmental changes, enabling authorities to identify risks and make informed policy decisions.

The minister also called for greater use of artificial intelligence and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research and improve disaster-risk assessments.

Referring to the recently launched $10 million Green Innovation Startup Fund, he invited universities, research institutions and young innovators to use satellite data and develop practical solutions to climate challenges.

He particularly encouraged institutions, including NUST, LUMS and Aga Khan University, as well as international universities, to participate in innovation initiatives and develop applications supporting disaster preparedness.

Dr Musadik Malik urged scientists and researchers to focus their work on protecting vulnerable populations, stressing that rescue operations should be the last resort rather than the first response.

headline: Lahore tops global pollution rankings as citywide AQI reaches 253
description: Lahore has emerged as the world's most polluted city, with its overall Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 253 amid worsening air quality across several
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lahore has emerged as the world's most polluted city, with its overall Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 253 amid worsening air quality across several localities.

Burki Road and nearby areas recorded the highest pollution level in the city, with an AQI of 520. Gulberg followed at 457, while the area surrounding Government College University registered 392.

Other locations also reported hazardous readings, including Samanabad at 363, Defence at 332, Model Town at 324 and Iqbal Town at 304. Achhra and its adjoining neighbourhoods recorded an AQI of 281.

Global air monitoring data showed northwesterly winds moving across Lahore at approximately 8 kilometres per hour.

In response to the deteriorating conditions, medical experts have urged residents to limit unnecessary outdoor movement and use protective masks when going outside. They have also advised keeping windows shut at homes and workplaces to reduce exposure to polluted air.

headline: Punjab private MBBS admissions open till Nov 6

The University of Health Sciences has set November 6 as the closing date for receiving applications, and candidates have been urged to complete the process within the stipulated timeframe to avoid any inconvenience.

headline: Anti-narcotics awareness seminar held at Sialkot college
description: An anti-narcotics awareness seminar was held at Government Muhammad Nawaz Sharif Graduate College for Women, Sialkot, on Saturday to educate students about the
author: NNI
article_text:
An anti-narcotics awareness seminar was held at Government Muhammad Nawaz Sharif Graduate College for Women, Sialkot, on Saturday to educate students about the harmful effects of drug abuse and encourage healthy and responsible lifestyles.

The seminar was organised on the initiative of Principal Gulzaib Waqas Awan in coordination with Jabran Malik.

Assistant Director Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) Sialkot Farooq Azam Chaudhry and Central Founder and President of All Pakistan Media House Dr Muhammad Zaman Hunjra attended the event as distinguished guests.

Addressing the participants, the speakers highlighted the importance of collective efforts to combat drug abuse and stressed the need to raise awareness among young people to build a healthier, drug-free society.

The guests also met Principal Gulzaib Waqas Awan and Vice Principal Faiza Aleem to discuss matters of mutual interest and explore opportunities for collaboration, awareness initiatives and constructive engagement with students.

The seminar highlighted the importance of sustained awareness, education, community participation and collective responsibility in preventing drug abuse among young people.

headline: French ambassador calls on CM Punjab, discusses trade, investment cooperation
description: Newly appointed French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier called on Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif here on Saturday and discussed ways to
author: APP
article_text: Newly appointed French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier called on Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif here on Saturday and discussed ways to enhance bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, and industrial development. The CM warmly welcomed the French ambassador on his visit to Lahore and congratulated him on assuming his new diplomatic responsibilities. She also thanked him for inviting her to visit France to promote bilateral trade relations. During the meeting, both sides discussed exploring new opportunities for trade, investment and industrial partnerships between Punjab and France. CM Maryam Nawaz invited French investors to invest in Punjab’s agriculture, industry and livestock sectors under the PIVOT (Punjab Innovation for Value, Opportunity and Transformation) development plan. She also invited French companies to participate in urban wastewater governance projects in major cities of the province. The CM said French companies in dairy, food processing and cold-chain sectors could help increase agricultural value addition, while French utility firms could collaborate in water supply, wastewater treatment and solid waste management projects under the public-private partnership model. She also highlighted opportunities for French energy companies in solar, grid and energy-efficiency projects in industrial estates. The meeting also discussed Pakistan’s GSP+ status and its importance for exports to European markets. The chief minister said France’s support was important for protecting Pakistan’s trade interests in the European Union. She said Pakistan’s exports to the EU reached approximately $8.96 billion in 2025-26, adding that preferential access to European markets was vital for the country’s textile, garments, sports goods and leather industries. CM Maryam Nawaz thanked France for providing a 180-million-euro loan for NTDC transmission lines and grid stations in Punjab. She also appreciated France’s recognition of Palestine and its principled position on justice and equal rights. She said Pakistan and France enjoyed decades-old friendly relations, adding that the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, adopted in 1789, had set out enduring principles of freedom, equality and human dignity. Both sides expressed their commitment to strengthening long-term institutional relations and expanding trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

headline: APHC leader links Indian policies in Kashmir with Israeli practices in Palestine
description: Former Information Secretary of the All Parties Hurriyat Conference (APHC) has expressed concern over Indian policies in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and
author: APP
article_text: Former Information Secretary of the All Parties Hurriyat Conference (APHC) has expressed concern over Indian policies in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), drawing parallels with Israeli practices in occupied Palestine. In a statement issued here on Saturday, he said that India’s domicile and settlement policies in IIOJK were raising concerns about attempts to change the demographic composition of the territory. He said the policies resembled what he described as Israel’s settlement practices in Palestine, while growing defence and security cooperation between India and Israel had raised concerns over the possible transfer of military technologies and practices. The APHC leader said that the people of Kashmir and Palestine had faced decades of dispossession and repression and continued to seek their UN-recognized right to self-determination. He called upon the international community to take steps for the protection of human rights, implementation of international law, and provision of justice to the people of both territories. He also urged the international community to oppose demographic changes and support the right of the Kashmiri and Palestinian people to freedom and self-determination.

headline: ECP targets registration of 174,845 women voters in two-district pilot project
description: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) will launch a pilot campaign in Kasur, Punjab, and Qambar Shahdadkot, Sindh, from December 2026 to February 2027,
author: APP
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) will launch a pilot campaign in Kasur, Punjab, and Qambar Shahdadkot, Sindh, from December 2026 to February 2027, aiming to register 174,845 women voters and narrow the gender gap in electoral rolls.

The initiative will focus on women who are eligible to vote but either do not have Computerised National Identity Cards (CNICs) or are not registered on the electoral rolls. The commission plans to reach them through door-to-door visits and mobile registration facilities.

Under the project, the ECP has set a target of registering 115,689 women in Kasur and 59,156 in Qambar Shahdadkot. Areas with a wider gap between male and female voter registration will be given priority.

Preparatory data collection is scheduled for November 2026, while the registration campaign will run over the following three months.

Local social workers and enumerators will visit households to identify eligible women, prepare lists for individual statistical blocks and raise awareness about obtaining CNICs and completing voter registration.

To make the process easier, the ECP will work with the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to send Mobile Registration Vans (MRVs) to women's doorsteps. Registration services will also be available at designated centres in government buildings.

Educational and health institutions, civil society organisations, community representatives and other stakeholders will assist in mobilising residents, spreading awareness and helping women complete the registration process.

The ECP's Gender and Social Inclusion Wing, provincial and district election commissioners, and Election Monitoring and Coordination Centres will oversee the campaign in coordination with NADRA.

The commission plans to use the pilot project not only to increase women's participation in the electoral rolls in the two districts but also to develop a model that could be introduced in other parts of the country.

The exercise will also help identify operational challenges, measure the results and assess how similar campaigns could be expanded nationwide.

The ECP reiterated its commitment to an inclusive electoral system, stressing that all eligible citizens, particularly women and marginalised communities, should have equal opportunities to obtain identity documents and exercise their constitutional right to vote.

headline: Qatar offers Pakistani travellers free 30-day visa on arrival under four conditions
description: Pakistani citizens can obtain a free tourist visa on arrival in Qatar for stays of up to 30 days, provided they meet four requirements set by the Qatari
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistani citizens can obtain a free tourist visa on arrival in Qatar for stays of up to 30 days, provided they meet four requirements set by the Qatari Ministry of Interior.

According to the ministry, the visa can be issued for a maximum of 30 days or for a shorter period depending on the visitor’s hotel reservation.

Travellers must hold a passport with at least three months of validity remaining and present a confirmed return ticket. They are also required to book their accommodation through Discover Qatar, the country’s official tourism platform. Hotel reservations made through other websites or online booking services will not qualify.

In addition, Pakistani visitors must have valid health insurance issued by a company approved by Qatar’s Ministry of Public Health.

The ministry has made clear that all four conditions must be fulfilled to qualify for the free visa-on-arrival facility. Passengers who fail to provide the required documents or meet the eligibility criteria are not assured entry under this arrangement.

The facility is separate from Qatar’s other visa-free entry arrangements and tourist visa schemes. Pakistani travellers are therefore advised to review the latest requirements and arrange all necessary documents before travelling.

headline: DG ISPR says Pakistan-Saudi defence cooperation could expand, rules out wider military campaigns
description: Director General of Inter-Services Public Relations (DG ISPR) Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said Pakistan’s growing engagement with Saudi
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Director General of Inter-Services Public Relations (DG ISPR) Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said Pakistan’s growing engagement with Saudi Arabia reflects positive developments, while indicating that the country’s defence cooperation with the kingdom could be expanded.

In an interview with British news agency Reuters, Chaudhry said the Field Marshal’s repeated visits to Saudi Arabia suggested progress.

“Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” he said when asked whether the visits were a positive sign.

However, he cautioned that “powerful spoilers ​and detractors,” who believed conflict served their interests, continued to pose challenges. He did not identify the individuals or groups he meant.

Commenting on the possibility of expanding the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, Chaudhry said Pakistan would welcome other countries that shared its objectives of collective deterrence and regional stability.

“Anyone who has a shared ‌vision of ⁠collective deterrence and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that any decision would rest with the political leadership of the three principal parties to the agreement.

Asked whether Pakistan planned to deploy additional troops to Saudi Arabia under the arrangement, the military spokesperson said the matter would depend on the prevailing situation and decisions taken by the political leadership of both countries.

He reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s defence, including the protection of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. However, he made clear that Pakistan was not involved in the conflict in Yemen.

“We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which ​is an intra-Yemen conflict,” he added.

On the security situation in the province and the possibility of broader military-led operations, Chaudhry said the army’s counterterrorism strategy relied on intelligence-based action rather than large-scale campaigns.

“Our counter-terrorism operations are based on what we call IBOs, intelligence-based operations… The tempo of the freedom ⁠of action ​of (those) IBOs will further increase,” he said.

headline: Federal Constitutional Court upholds finality of judgments, rejects repeated challenges in land dispute
description: The Federal Constitutional Court has ruled that matters settled through final court judgments cannot be repeatedly brought before different judicial forums,
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Federal Constitutional Court has ruled that matters settled through final court judgments cannot be repeatedly brought before different judicial forums, describing such attempts as an abuse of the legal process.

The court dismissed a petition filed by the heirs of Anwari Bibi, who had sought leave to appeal in a dispute over land used for the construction of a girls’ school in Bhakkar. The decision upheld an earlier ruling by the Lahore High Court.

In its judgment, the court observed that a final decision could only be reopened if fraud, a legal error or a lack of jurisdiction by the relevant court was established. It said repeatedly pursuing the same dispute before different courts was not permissible under the law.

The ruling noted that the land’s partition and subsequent re-allotment had already been contested before the Supreme Court. It added that the consolidation authorities’ decision on the partition had also attained finality, meaning the matter could not be reopened through execution proceedings.

The court further explained that an executing court is authorised to implement a decree within its legal limits but cannot exceed its scope or change rights that have already been determined.

The dispute arose after Anwari Bibi’s heirs claimed that a girls’ school in Bhakkar had been constructed on their property. They had also challenged previous decisions relating to the land’s partition and the school’s construction.

The bench, comprising Justice Rozi Khan Breach and Justice Syed Arshad Hussain Shah, announced the decision. Justice Syed Arshad Hussain Shah authored the detailed judgment.

The court stressed that respecting the finality of judgments was necessary to maintain the continuity of the justice system, ensure legal certainty and uphold the rule of law.
